items.quote: So strategy sir, mainly for the large QSR, there is a huge demand for breads, certain kinds of breads which we are developing, which we propose to start producing. So there alrea dy is a huge demand. We are already in dialogue with customers

items.statement: Plant-based meat demand low in India but growing in Europe; targeting export market
items.quote: So plant-based meat products in India are not taking off. But exports, yes there is a demand coming in. Some of our customers also whom we are supplying to are exporting. So the European market is growing not at a very fast pace as it was expected to grow in 2021 or '19, 2'0 or before that. But the market is definitely growing in the European markets and the England markets.

items.statement: New plant 60% flatbreads (naan, tortillas, paratha), ready-to-eat retort and frozen formats
items.quote: But in the new veg unit, our 60% capacity is going to come from flatbread line. We are talking of products like naan, tortillas, malabari paratha and then we are coming out with a very innovative product which I won't disclose now, which is a flatbread. It has been rated as one of the most popular flatbread in the world. So that's going to comprise of almost 60% of the capacity. Then we are going

items.statement: New plant average realization INR90-115/kg vs current INR220/kg for veg products
items.quote: The per unit sale, so the per unit sale on the bread is going to be much lower. The per kg sale it's going to be much lower then we are going into the ready to eat section where we are already in dialogue with a few customers for retort rice to the US that is also much lower. So these numbers are averaging between INR90 to INR115 per kg.

items.statement: Chicken pricing hedged: 70% annual contracts, 20-30% monthly; customers support justified price increases
items.quote: We are normally on majority of our sourcing, we are working on annual prices. Majority of our sourcing. Like 70% of our chicken purchase is done on annual pricing. Our pricing with customers is also annual. So, we just left with 20%, 30% purchase on chicken, which we normally do on a monthly basis. So, it is all hedged. Our pricing is always hedged.

items.statement: Export focus on Middle East, US, Europe via white label; participating in Gulf Food, Anuga, Gulfood fairs
items.quote: For the new plant, we are definitely looking at exports, Vinayakji. So that's one of the major areas we will focus on. So even in our financials, what we are planning for the next three years ahead, we are looking at budgets to participate in, the Gulf food fairs and other fairs, the trade fairs too. It's going to be a very big focus for us on the exports. This new plant with such a high capacity

items.statement: New plant commissioning by March 2025; 30-35% utilization Year 1, 60-65% Year 2
items.quote: The first year, that's what I'm saying. The first year should be around 30 %-35%. Second year, we're targeting around 65%. Okay. So 25%-26% is around 30-35% because it'll take a little bit of time for us to get the customers on board, start delivering the products. So we're not looking at a very large capacity utilization. So it'll be a 30%- 35% utilization. And then next year, yes, we'll be targe

items.statement: Next chicken capacity expansion likely in FY26 due to demand trends
items.quote: Well Neil, I think for chicken, the way things are moving now, we might have to look at a capacity expansion in 26. Neil Bahal: Next year? Paramjit Singh Chatha: Next to next year. 24-25, 25-26, we will need a capacity expansion in chicken with the way the trend is going on

items.statement: Manpower increase ~50% at full utilization for new plant due to automation
items.quote: If you look at the labor, I think it will be close to a 50% increase in the manpower. Not more than that. Agastya Dave: At full utilization

items.statement: Regional bird flu manageable; widespread pandemic would be uncontrollable
items.quote: If there is a widespread pandemic like we had COVID in chicken, there is nothing much you can do about it. But regional flus do keep coming and going. I think region based flus, bird flus where we called them or influenza, avian influenza. It keeps coming and going every year. It is almost coming a region-based. It becomes PAN India kind of a pandemic so I don't think we can have any backups for t

items.statement: IPO proceeds INR33.39 crores used for debt repayment and share issue expenses
items.quote: And our cash flow from financing activities were INR26.06 crores which comprises of INR33.39 crores of proceeds from the IPO and payment of INR7.33 crores towards our borrowings and share ratio expenses.

items.statement: Cash flow from operations INR12.18 crores; post working capital changes and taxes INR3.51 crores
items.quote: And our cash flows from the operations for this period were INR12.18 crores and the cash generated from operating activities post working capital changes and taxes was INR3.51 crores.

items.statement: Innovative dessert bakery product launching July 22 for large customer; may accelerate expansion
items.quote: And we have developed a very, very innovative product, which is as a bakery product, as a dessert bakery product. It's going to be launched on the 22nd of, this month, July. So if these kind of products we are able to develop, we might have to go into for some additional expansions even earlier if these kind of products take off in the veg section.

items.statement: Competitors include Darshan Foods, Vista, Venky's, CP, Republic of Chicken
items.quote: So there are companies, there is Darshan Foods, there is Vista, they're much larger, Venky's is much larger than us CP is much larger than us in terms of companies as well. So there are much larger companies than us. Darshan Foods is our size, Republic of Chicken is our size.

items.statement: Flight take rates expected to hover between 7% and 7.5% going forward
items.quote: So if you want a guidance of sorts I would say that, look we would expect these take rates on flight side to hover between 7% and 7.5% kind of going forward.

items.statement: Train volumes expected to maintain double-digit, mid-teens growth
items.quote: We think that maintaining double-digit growth, mid-teens growth on volumes is something which is quite doable there.

items.statement: Flights to continue growing faster than overall market
items.quote: On the flight side, we have been growing way faster than the overall market. And we intend to continue that.

items.statement: Buses to continue growing marginally faster than overall market
items.quote: On buses side, we've been growing marginally faster than the overall market. And again, I think there is scope to improve certain things there over time and continue that momentum.

items.statement: Group contribution margin percentage rose from 43.51% to 44.8% in FY24
items.quote: And we can see that when we look at the contribution margin percentage, it's a percentage of net revenue and it's risen from 43.51% to 44.8% in this fiscal year.

items.statement: Train contribution margin percentage expanded from 32.28% to 34.9% in FY24
items.quote: The contribution margin grew to INR 129 crores, with the contribution margin percentage as a percentage of segment revenue expanding from 32.28% to 34.9%.

items.statement: Bus contribution margin percentage grew to 66% in FY24
items.quote: The contribution margin percentage grew to 66%.

items.statement: Flight contribution margin percentage was 48.5% in FY24
items.quote: Now the contribution margin percentage for FY '24 was 48.5%.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA increased to INR 55.3 crores in FY24 from INR 44.3 crores in FY23
items.quote: Our group adjusted EBITDA increased to INR 55.3 crores in FY '24 compared to INR 44.3 crores in FY '23.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 adjusted EBITDA was INR 17.1 crores, up 0.66% YoY
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA of INR 17.1 crores in Q4 '24 was up 0.66% over the previous year.

items.statement: International flight passenger segments grew 100% YoY in FY24
items.quote: We are proud to report that our international flight passenger segments have grown by 100% year-on-year in FY '24.

items.statement: Domestic flight passenger segments grew 41.8% YoY in Q4 FY24 and 77% for full year
items.quote: Despite these headwinds, ixigo managed to grow our flight passenger segments by 41.8% for Q4 FY '24 versus Q4 FY '23, and by a remarkable 77% for the full year.

items.statement: Bus passenger segments grew 21.2% YoY in FY24
items.quote: the Le Travenues Technology Limited - July 04, 2024 bus vertical booked 1.2 crores passenger segments worth INR 1,175 crores in GTV representing 21.2% more segments and 21.7% higher GTV as compared to FY ‘23

items.statement: PhonePe partnership extended to exclusively power flights and buses in addition to trains
items.quote: PhonePe has chosen to extend this partnership to exclusively partner with us for our flights and buses business as well, primarily due to the superior customer experience we've built.

items.statement: Launched travelsupermall.com (TSM) B2B2C platform for offline travel agents
items.quote: Today, our group has launched travelsupermall.com, nicknamed TSM, our B2B2C distribution platform.

items.statement: Tax assessment order for FY22 of ~INR 19 crores being contested
items.quote: We want to keep you updated about the tax assessment orders for financial year 2021-22 of approximately INR 19 crores of demand basis on some addition/disallowances made by the assessing officer.

items.statement: Board approved vertical demerger of Real Estate business into wholly owned subsidiary Raymond Realty Limited; process expected to take 12-15 months; each Raymond shareholder to receive one share of Raymond Realty for every share held
items.quote: Yesterday, Board has approved another corporate initiative for vertical demerger of its real estate business from Raymond Limited into its wholly owned subsidiary, Raymond Realty Limited or RRL and the process of demerger is expected to take anything between 12 to 15 months and will create Raymond Realty Limited into a pure play net debt-free listed real estate entity.

items.statement: Lifestyle business demerger completed on 30 June 2024; record date fixed for 11 July 2024; Raymond Lifestyle shares expected to list by end of August or early September
items.quote: Demerger of its Lifestyle business got completed on 30th June 2024 and 11th July 2024 is fixed as a record date for the lifestyle business demerger.

items.statement: Real Estate business reported revenue of ~INR1,600 crores, EBITDA of INR370 crores, and booking value pre-sales of INR2,250 crores in FY24
items.value: INR1,600 crores revenue, INR370 crores EBITDA, INR2,250 crores pre-sales
items.quote: The strategic move of demerger has come as Raymond's real estate business has achieved a scale by reporting a revenue of approximately INR1,600 crores and an EBITDA of INR370 crores with a booking value pre-sales of INR2,250 crores in fiscal '24, positioning it well to chart its own growth path as a separate entity.

items.statement: Thane land parcel has revenue potential of ~INR25,000 crores with 11.4 million sq ft RERA-approved carpet area; currently developing ~40 acres with 4 million sq ft and INR9,000 crores revenue potential; over 65% of Thane inventory already s
items.value: INR25,000 crores total potential, INR9,000 crores current phase
items.quote: The Thane land has the revenue potential of approximately INR25,000 crores with 11.4 million square feet RERA-approved carpet area. Currently, we are developing almost 40 acres with RERA-approved carpet area of 4 million square feet and a revenue of INR9,000 crores.

items.statement: Four JDAs signed in MMR with ~2 million sq ft carpet area and combined revenue potential of ~INR7,000 crores; Thane + JDAs give total potential revenue of over INR32,000 crores
items.value: INR7,000 crores JDA potential, INR32,000 crores total potential
items.quote: We have leveraged and recently Raymond Realty has signed four JDAs in the Mumbai metropolitan region with carpet area of approximately 2 million square feet. The combined revenue potential from these four JDAs is approximately INR7,000 crores and with the development of Thane land bank and current four JDAs gives the company a potential revenue of over INR32,000 crores.

items.statement: Execution timeline for INR32,000 crores GDV estimated at 7-8 years; JDA projects take 1-1.5 years to start and have 5-6 year lifecycle
items.quote: I think it will be over a seven, eight-year period, because as you know, on the INR32,000 crores, you have INR7,000-odd crores, which is the JDA led, which we have signed in the last three to four, six months, which takes to start the project anything between one year to 15 months. And then it's a life cycle of a five to six-year project.

items.statement: Real Estate business targets annual revenue potential of INR4,000 crores in next 3-5 years with 24-25% EBITDA margin and 25% IRR
items.quote: So, I think if the company takes and the way it is working on a 10 million square feet under construction, you can comfortably say in the next three to five years, we are at least having a revenue potential of INR4,000 crores every year. And we have been delivering anything between 24%-25% EBITDA margin with 25% IRR.

items.statement: Engineering business revenue doubled to INR1,800-1,900 crores post-Maini acquisition; management believes it can double again over next 4-5 years with faster EBITDA compounding due to aerospace/defense margin profile
items.quote: So I think overall, as an engineering business, we believe comfortably over the next four or five years, you should be able to double from here. And also, because the margins on the aerospace and defense is much higher with the auto components business and the engineering consumable, I think it will be sooner when you will be able to double the EBITDA.

items.statement: Aerospace & Defense segment growing at 25-30% YoY; Auto components at INR1,200 crores growing 10-15%; Engineering consumables at ~INR500 crores growing 8-12%
items.quote: One is in aerospace-defense, which grows phenomenally at a pace more than 25%-30% year-on-year. Then you have the auto business, which is in the range of INR1,200-odd crores, which also grows at a good 10% to 15%. And then you have the engineering consumable business, which is roughly INR500-odd crores, which grows somewhere in the range of 8% to 12%.

items.statement: Aerospace & Defense business run rate ~INR300 crores with 25-27% EBITDA margin
items.quote: As far as the business is concerned, I can tell you what the business is all about. We have a run rate around INR300 crores with a 25%, 27% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Maini Precision machining capacity currently utilized at ~85%; can add capacity with smaller capex to grow revenue; focus on improving productivity and moving up value chain to assemblies
items.quote: Therefore, at this juncture maybe I'm utilizing 85% of the capacity, but what is also good in this thing is that with a smaller capex you can keep adding the business and growing the business.

items.statement: Engineering business: 65% export sales, 85% repeat customers; supplies engine-critical components for 737 MAX and A320/321neo engines; covers top 15 global auto OEMs
items.quote: So 65% is export. And repeat customer I think would be 85% as we continue to get some of the new customers every year.

items.statement: JK Files enjoys 65% market share in India; branded Files sold across Western Africa, Latin America, South America with distributor relationships of 30-50 years
items.quote: Our JK Files is sold as a branded product in India, and we enjoy 65% market share in India. And even in the Western Africa, in the whole of Africa, Latin America and South America market, our Files are sold as a branded product.

items.statement: Working capital estimates: Lifestyle ~INR1,200 crores, Real Estate ~INR500 crores, Engineering ~INR300-350 crores (including Maini)
items.value: Lifestyle INR1,200 cr, Real Estate INR500 cr, Engineering INR300-350 cr
items.quote: working capital, basically, what would happen is, if I look at it in the lifestyle business, it should be in the range of INR1,200-odd crores, the working capital, networking capital. And in the real estate, it would be in the range of somewhere INR500 crores of working capital. Deepesh Agarwal: And engineering? Amit Agarwal: Engineering could be INR300 crores to INR350 crores

items.statement: Group net debt-free after FMCG sale for INR2,825 crores; Lifestyle had net cash of ~INR200 crores as of 31 Mar 2024; Realty has excess of INR500 crores cash
items.value: Lifestyle net cash INR200 cr, Realty cash >INR500 cr
items.quote: For debt, very clearly, we have all the businesses which are net debt free. And clearly, in the Lifestyle, we are having at least to as on 31st of March 2024, we were having net cash of almost INR200 crores. And in the Realty business, we have in excess of INR500 crores of cash.

items.statement: JDA projects require peak investment of INR300-350 crores per ~INR2,000 crores top-line project; cash flow from launches recovers this investment; no significant capital raise needed for next 2 years given current projects and sales visibil
items.value: INR300-350 crores peak investment per project
items.quote: typically, any project which is ranging between around INR2,000 crores top line, which is what on an average, it is in the city of Bombay, the peak investment on a thumb rule basis for a project like that is somewhere in the range of INR300 crores-INR350 crores

items.statement: Engineering business consolidation into two subsidiaries under Raymond Limited (auto/engineering consumables and aerospace/defense) expected to complete by 31 March 2025; Gautam Maini to be CEO of consolidated engineering business
items.quote: So I think what we expect before 31st March 2025 the engineering consolidation and the demerger of two subsidiaries -- of two subsidiaries under Raymond Limited should happen by 31st March 2025.

items.statement: Maini Precision acquired at 10x enterprise value multiple; total Maini revenue ~INR900 crores (Auto ~INR600 cr, A&D ~INR300 cr) with EBITDA ~INR140-145 crores; combined Ring Plus + Maini Auto revenue ~INR1,200 crores
items.value: 10x EV multiple, INR900 cr revenue, INR140-145 cr EBITDA
items.quote: And that is a business which is roughly clocking on the run rate of INR300 crores. So total business of Maini is roughly INR900 crores, delivering an EBITDA of close to INR140 to INR145 crores. And we bought a multiple enterprise value of 10x.

items.statement: Real Estate future growth 99.9% focused on JDA model; not pursuing outright land purchases unless very attractive; Chairman sees $2 trillion JDA opportunity in Mumbai long-term
items.quote: At this juncture, we are very clear that we are moving towards JDA because there is enough and more opportunities in JDA. So, we are not going to invest today to tomorrow into land unless something very, very nice or something very attractive comes. But 99.9% of our focus is on building on JDA capability.

items.statement: Real Estate maintains cash surplus (INR500+ crores) for exigencies like COVID (kept 500 people on site 24/7); philosophy to never starve business of liquidity to avoid project delays
items.quote: And we believe as a good prudent philosophy, we don't want to starve ever any business that is running short of liquidity. And because of that, there is a delay in project. And you know, we come from a manufacturing mindset.

items.statement: Mumbai/Thane real estate market experiencing healthy volumes with steady pricing (5-8% price hikes); no slowdown experienced in micro-markets where Raymond operates; Thane sales ~INR1,500-1,600 crores annually for last 2 years; every 3rd ho
items.quote: So Bombay market in that sense is not volatile at all very healthy strong volumes with steady pricing. So that's what we have experienced so far and we continue to do so. Even this quarter, we are experiencing that last quarter also.

items.statement: JDA deal structures vary by micro-market; target 25% IRR through boundary conditions on deposit, sharing ratio, and other deal terms; all four signed JDAs have different structures
items.quote: Even the four deals we have done, they are all different. But we are very clear of the boundary conditions that we want to follow. I mean, one of the things that I mentioned to you is in terms of average size and the peak investment that we are looking at. And we look at a multiple of that peak investment coming to us in the form of the return. Basically, we target for about 25% IRR based on all t

items.statement: Non-Thane JDA projects: Bandra already launched (55-60% sold in 30 days); other three projects to launch by H1 next year; time from JDA signing to launch ~12-15 months vs industry 18-24 months
items.quote: So, by H1 of next years, all the projects that we have signed would be launched. One project is already launched as you may be knowing the Bandra one, which has been extremely well received in the market and in terms of sales and construction going on in full swing and we are ahead of schedule there.

items.statement: Real Estate team currently ~330 people, targeting 400 by year-end; no bandwidth constraint for adding new projects; evaluated ~700 projects in MMR over last 3 years
items.quote: I mean it's close to 330 people today by the end of the year we will be 400 people. So clearly there is no real constraint that we have for taking on new projects.

items.statement: Real Estate demerger requires SEBI, stock exchange, NCLT, shareholder, and creditor approvals; record date for Real Estate demerger likely in Q3/Q4 of next fiscal year
items.quote: As far as Raymond Reality is concerned as a process we just announced yesterday, got the approval from the board which takes anything between 15 months, 16 months. So till such time all the approval, various requisite approvals which is the SEBI, stock exchanges, NCLT, shareholders, creditors, all sorts of approvals takes that kind of a timelines.

items.statement: Lifestyle business to become net debt-free post-demerger; NCDs held by Raymond Limited will knock off against transferred debt; cash on balance sheet expected
items.quote: Now, once the deme rger gets completed of the Lifestyle, the debt to NCD should buy Raymond Lifestyle to the business getting transferred, knocks off each other, and it will become a net debt free, and there will be a cash on the balance sheet

items.statement: Denim JV (B2B export) retained in Raymond Limited, not part of Lifestyle (B2C); two diverse businesses with no distribution dependency
items.quote: The lifestyle business is primarily focused on a B2C business. It is a consumer-led business. And the Denim is primarily a B2B business, which is into the export of the fabrics, and it is a joint venture with a partner. Therefore, it was felt appropriate to keep into the Raymond Limited and not into the Lifestyle business.

items.statement: Unallocable expense split between Real Estate, Engineering, and Lifestyle to be finalized in next 30 days; pro forma Lifestyle numbers to be shared in Q1 FY25 results
items.quote: I think over the next one to two months, we are going to work out a structure which will enable us to identify e xactly that how much it is for the Real Estate business, how much is for the Engineering and how much is going to be for the Lifestyle business, which we are in the process. So hopefully, in the next 30 days, we should have that done

items.statement: Binding agreement for 5 million tablets before June 2025 and 15 million tablets before December 2025, with a four-year supply agreement plus automatic four-year renewal
items.quote: They agreed to this and along with this, they have agreed for the US $10 million milestone payment. Now, they are placing the binding agreement order for the 5 million tablets to be delivered before the June '25 and 15 million tablets before the December '25.

items.statement: EBITDA margin above 50% on this NCE CDMO project
items.quote: It is a NCE molecule. So I think we are the exclusive supplier for them. So we have enough like CDMO margin like we have the margins in this that much we can tell you above 50.

items.statement: Innovator confident enough to place binding orders before NDA filing and approval
items.quote: And every year definitely once the patient takes more and more probably with this, without getting this filing and without putting the approval, they are placing this order. That shows that how confident they are on their product.

items.statement: OLC (Oxylanthanum Carbonate) is an NCE with 20-year patent runway, different from previously mentioned pending NDA filings
items.quote: Because now they have 20 years. I think it will be not less than 10 years or 12 years for sure, but I am not knowing exactly frankly, but I think once it is a NCE molecule so you can understand they have enough runway

items.statement: Revenue potential described as substantial but not quantified
items.quote: It is a multimillion, but I think today projecting for the next year we have some indications from them, but currently telling will be difficult but it is a substantial revenue for Shilpa. That much we can tell you.

items.statement: Continue to target FY25 revenue growth better than FY24
items.quote: No, we continue to stick with our guideline that we've talked about in the last quarter. We definitely want to exit this financial year with a better growth rate as compared to last financial year.

items.statement: Target EBITDA margin range of 28% to 29% for FY25
items.quote: Gaurav Bajaj: 28% to 29%. Manoj Raghavan: Yes around 28%. Essentially the way to look at it is if you look at the entire financial year perspective, we hope to maintain last year's performance, maybe beat it a little bit

items.statement: One-time expense of INR19.78 crore to Progressive Electoral Trust impacted Q1 margins
items.quote: The company made a contribution to the Progressive Electoral Trust of INR19.78 crores for the quarter ended June 30, 2024, which is included in the other expenses. If not for this onetime expense, our EBITDA margin would have been 29.4% and our PBT margin would have been 28.4%.

items.statement: Average wage hikes of 5% to 6% split between Q2 (junior) and Q3 (senior), expected minimal margin impact
items.quote: The average wage hikes would be in the range of 5% to 6%. But I think we are well covered with respect to margins and so on. We have enough levers to address that. So, I don't see too much of an impact on the wage hikes or on our margins.

items.statement: Media & Communications vertical grew 0.5% QoQ in constant currency, seeing green shoots and large consolidation opportunities
items.quote: We see some green shoots definitely. There are some large consolidation opportunities that we are bidding for and at the same time let me tell you that the industry is still under a lot of stress.

items.statement: OEM mix in Transportation vertical increased to 66% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Apurva Prasad: 66%. Got that.

items.statement: On-site mix sustainable at 25-75, slight uptick in Q1 due to new engagement ramp-ups
items.quote: A sustainable level, I mean, from our perspective, it's definitely 25-75. And we will hover around that range only.

items.statement: Tax rate increased due to SEZ units exiting tax holiday, expected to remain in current range for FY25
items.quote: Yes, I think we indicated during the last couple of quarters that in this financial year, our tax rate will go up because we are coming out of the tax holiday in few of our SEZ unit. One more SEZ unit came out of 100% bracket to 50% bracket. So going forward in this financial year, it would be likely in this range only.

items.statement: Client concentration in top 10/20 customers accepted as strategic focus, not a concern
items.quote: So from our perspective, from the size of business that we have, we will continue to have a lot more focus on our top 20 customers because that is what will drive our growth. So we want to be a lot more relevant to these customers, build strategic relationships with these customers and grow with these customers.

items.statement: Utilization has not peaked, significant headroom to improve as deals ramp up
items.quote: Absolutely. I mean, utilization has not peaked at all, right? We have a long way to go. And that is where we are confident that we have enough levers to manage the margins. So yes, so that will be the focus in the coming 3 quarters in the years, right? We really need to ramp up our utilization.

items.statement: GCCs viewed as both opportunity and threat; ER&D work less susceptible than traditional IT/BPO
items.quote: GCCs are both an opportunity as well as a threat. It's not that every company would move all the work to their GCCs. Most of our customers have a balance between what they give to their own centers GCCs and what they outsource or work with strategic partners like us.

items.statement: No immediate competitive impact from traditional IT companies' automotive ER&D acquisitions
items.quote: True, yes. We have seen the likes of HCL, Infosys and so on make large acquisitions. So far, we have not seen an immediate impact in any of our customer base.

items.statement: FY25 targets of 30% YoY revenue growth, 30% YoY volume growth and 40% VAP share remain unchanged
items.quote: Everything is in line. There is no change in whatever you mentioned before. Everything is just as in line as mentioned in the last concall.

items.statement: DFT machinery has arrived at Mangaon plant and is under installation, expected to commission this quarter
items.quote: The DFT has already arrived at the plant. It's under the installation phase and it's before time that it has arrived. We are expecting it to arrive later this quarter. Everything is in the plant and it should be setting up right now.

items.statement: Government demand expected to pick up after budget; government orders were below 15% of volumes in Q1
items.quote: Demand has picked up from before, but the final flow of demand will open up after the budget. So it's a few days away from budget and we should see new government orders lining up after that.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 8.5% in Q1 FY25 from 7.2% in Q1 FY24 driven by high-margin product focus and scale
items.quote: EBITDA for Q1 FY25 stood at INR438 million, reflecting a 21% increase from Q1 FY24, underscoring our efficient cost management and operational excellence. The EBITDA margin improved to 8.5% in Q1 FY25, up from 7.2% in Q1 FY24, driven by strategic focus on high margin products and increasing scale.

items.statement: Average price gap between secondary (patra) and primary (HRC) steel is INR4-5 per kg; last month gap was INR3.5-4 per kg
items.quote: The last month's gap was around INR3.5 - INR4. It's a very fluctuating market. The gaps are keeps on rising and decreasing, but we've encountered on average during the year, the gap is more or less in the range of INR4 - INR5 per kg

items.statement: Export volumes hit all-time high at 7% of sales (5,917 tons); export growth expected to continue with DFT and SKU expansion
items.quote: Quarterly exports stood at an all-time high, at 7% and the total export sales was 5,917 metric tons.

items.statement: VAP share was 25% of sales volume (21,261 tons) in Q1; management defines VAP as galvanized pipes above INR7,500/ton
items.quote: Notably, VAP products contributed 25% of total sales mix, with sales volumes of 21,261 metric tons.

items.statement: Nabha Steel output not yet meeting JTL's quality specs; about 1-2 months away from producing required HR coils for backward integration
items.quote: Right now they are not meeting the quality that or like the exact requirements we require at JTL. So it is about a month away or 2 months away from the exact products that we require at JTL to make our type.

items.statement: QIP enabling resolution passed; no immediate plans; promoters paid INR168 cr (one-fifth) of INR600 cr warrant issue, balance payable when company needs funds

items.quote: EBIT for the quarter was INR13.7 billion, translating into an operating margin of 15% compared with 14.7% in the previous quarter. The absence of project cancellation impact of the last quarter and operational efficiencies led to margin improvement of more than 100 basis points.

items.statement: Pass-through revenue in Q1 similar to Q4; not a significant driver of Q1 growth
items.quote: So I think as far as the pass-through is concerned, the pass-through in Q1 is fairly similar to what we had in Q4. So the growth that you'll see, I don't think the pass-throughs have paid any significant role in Q1.

items.statement: Early signs of recovery: clients deploying savings from cost takeout into high-priority transformation and AI foundational investments; short-cycle sprint-based demand in top 3 verticals
items.quote: Clients continue to focus on efficiency via cost takeout or vendor consolidation deals. However, we are seeing early signs that they are beginning to deploy the savings in additional budget towards kicking off high-priority transformation programs and making foundational investments for AI.

items.statement: AI demand translating into data engineering, governance, platform build-out, and digital engineering projects; assisting majority of top 100 clients in AI
items.quote: As per our recent survey in collaboration with an external research agency, more than 85% of enterprises are looking to accelerate their AI-related investments. Many customers are progressing from the Proof-Of-Concept stage and looking to deploy AI use cases across the enterprise.

items.statement: Macro environment unchanged; elections and interest rates could disrupt H2 momentum; wage hikes planned for Q3 with quantum undecided
items.quote: We expect the market to follow this path for FY '25, where the focus will continue to be on cost takeout, but also on select high priority transformations. As clients continue building their AI momentum and graduating AI beyond the proof-of-concept stages, we are well-positioned to capitalize on this opportunity.

items.statement: Utilization ex-trainees at 88.3%; TTM attrition stable at 14.4%; onboarded 1,400 freshers in Q1; significant lateral hiring increase planned for Q2
items.quote: As a result of a ramp-up in deals won, our utilization, excluding trainees, increased to 88.3% from 86.9% last quarter. For the quarter, our TTM attrition remained stable at 14.4%. We onboarded around 1,400 freshers this quarter.

items.statement: Plans to launch INR12,000 crores GDV in FY25 across 9 projects
items.quote: This year itself, we are planning to launch another INR12,000 crores of this, in the current financial year.

items.statement: Targets INR15,000-16,000 crores GDV additions annually
items.quote: And also, we are looking at adding every year about INR15,000 crores, INR16,000 crores of in GDVs every year.

items.statement: Expects INR2,900 crores collections in real estate for FY25
items.quote: This is our expected target of collections is roughly around INR2,900 crores.

items.statement: Targets INR15,000-20,000 crores GDV acquisitions in FY25
items.quote: Largely we are looking at about INR15,000 crores to INR20,000 crores this year and would like to continue to look at that sort of number.

items.statement: Expects paper EBITDA around INR12 per kg for FY25
items.quote: But I can say that our EBITDA will be roughly on average at the end of the year at about INR12 per kg.

items.statement: Overall GDV pipeline stands at INR54,000 crores with INR12,500 crores launched and INR9,500 crores sold
items.quote: Yes, as you very rightly pointed out, we have an overall GDV of INR54,000 Crs. As you know, we have already launched about INR12,500 Cr out of that and we have clocked sales of about INR9,500 crores out of that.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 bookings of INR262 crores, up 27% YoY
items.quote: We achieved booking of Rs.INR262 crores in Q1 '25 at our already launched project, representing a growth of 27% year-on-year.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 collections of INR488 crores across all projects
items.quote: We maintained very strong collection of INR488 crores from all projects during the quarter.

items.statement: Acquired 13.27 acres in Gurugram with GDV INR5,300 crores and 16.5 acres in Manjri, Pune with GDV INR2,500 crores in Q1 FY25
items.quote: We did two major acquisitions during the quarter, wherein we acquired 13.27 acres of land parcel in Gurugram with a GDV of INR5,300 crores. And we also acquired 16.5 acres of land parcel in Manjri, Pune with GDV of INR2,500 crores.

items.statement: Targets 25-30% EBITDA margin and 20%+ IRR on new Pune Manjri project
items.quote: We're looking at a margin of at least about 25% to 30% in terms of EBITDA margin. More importantly, we, as you know, we always look at very strong IRR – north to 20%.

items.statement: Delivered projects achieving 27.5% EBITDA margin at project level
items.quote: At this point of time, whatever we have already accounted for is about 27.5%.

items.statement: Paper NSR down 14% YoY but flat QoQ in Q1 FY25
items.quote: In Q1 '25, paper, board and tissue prices continue to see a downturn trajectory with average net sales realization down by 14% year-on-year, although they were at par vis-a-vis previous quarter.

items.statement: Using bamboo, veneer chips and fiber plant pulp to reduce raw material costs in paper segment
items.quote: The company continued to take various cost reduction initiatives like the in creased usage of bamboo and veneer chips to reduce raw material costs. Also, we use fiber plant pulp instead of imported pulp in tissue machine, added by suitable chemical program to reduce input costs

items.statement: Paper demand subdued due to deferred government tenders and seasonal factors; tissue demand picking up
items.quote: Demand for writing and printing paper was subdued in Q1 '25 due to deferment of government tenders, seasonal closing of education institution and courts for summer vacation.

items.statement: Expects moderate revival in printing paper pricing and demand in Q2 FY25; tissue demand to pick up towards quarter end
items.quote: On the market outlook, seasonal factors are expected to moderately revive pricing a printed paper demand in Q2. In Q2 '25, order flow in tissue segment is forecasted to be slightly lower in the initial months on account of lean season. However, demand is expected to pick up towards the end of quarter.

items.statement: Paper division has capex plans that cannot be deferred without impacting future profitability
items.quote: We cannot hold those capex plan because that will impact our profitability in the future year.

items.statement: Paper working capital peaked due to linkage coal from Coal India; expects release over next 3 quarters
items.quote: Working capital right now is high because we have suddenly got a lot of linkage coal from Coal India and we cannot refuse that. So we -- I think this is a peak working capital and gradually, we have planned to reduce it. So working capital will be released in the next 3 quarters.

items.statement: Exploring private equity platform funding for residential and commercial portfolio scaling, not public funding
items.quote: We always are looking for raising platform fu nding for our private funding, private equity funding for scaling up our residential portfolio, maybe at some point of time even the commercial portfolio, but not in the near future for any public sort of funding

items.statement: Growing team from 350 to 500-550 employees; adding 40-50% headcount annually
items.quote: We were at 200 last year. We are at 350 now. We may go up to 500, 550 as the demand for people are there.

items.statement: RR Nagar and Walkeshwar launches delayed due to RERA approval delays; RR Nagar expected by end of month, Walkeshwar in few days
items.quote: We were supposed to have launched RR Nagar in the last quarter. But because we didn't obtain the RERA, we had to postpone the launch, and we are quite hopeful that we will be able to launch it this quarter. Similarly, Walkeshwar also we are supposed to launch last quarter. However, again, we are waiting for RERA.

items.statement: Real estate corporate overheads benchmarked at 3-4% of bookings
items.quote: But largely, I could tell you that it will not exceed about 3% to 4% of our bookings. If that's the kind of a ballpark figure, 3% to 4% of bookings is what we should kind of consider as our overheads.

items.statement: Delhi project launch deferred to Q1 FY26 due to lengthy approval process
items.quote: Delhi is difficult because the entire approval process takes a lot of time. There are more approvals than usual. So we are kind of planning it for the Q1 of next year.

items.statement: JV with Grasim in textiles at initial stage; incurred INR8 crores loss in Q1 FY25; expects profitability next year
items.quote: So it will take some time to generate profits. But it is not a significant ask on our balance sheet, it is more a new thing that we are developing in the country. So it will take some time to absorb. So hopefully, next -- this year also probably, we do n't -- we might not see the light at the end of the tunnel. But certainly next year, we will be starting to show profits from that. Yes, we had INR

items.statement: Q1 volume growth 7% vs 10% prior year; value degrowth -3% due to inferior mix and inflation; rural T3-T4 cities outpacing T1-T2
items.quote: The quarter has been tough and overall, I think the demand conditions have been fairly challenging because of a host of reasons. So, the volume growth has been still fairly healthy. We were gunning for double digit volume, we have landed at about 7%, which is still healthy over a big base of 10%, we reported in Q1-FY24.

items.statement: Targeting double-digit volume growth in Q2 FY25 and aiming to keep volume-value gap in 5-6% band
items.quote: So definitely we are looking at double -digit kind of a volume growth for this quarter, going ahead hoping that the demand conditions will be better.

items.statement: Standalone gross margin 42.9% in Q1; PBDIT margin band 18-20%; sequential PBT margin down ~50 bps
items.quote: Gross margins, if you look, basically on a material price inflation which have happened and also in terms of a lower mix. Today some bit of our work, which is around the sourcing formulation efficiencies have given us some reprieve here, but still, we see that the gross margins are at about 42.9%.

items.statement: Took 1% price increase in Q1; expect 1.4-1.5% inflation in Q2 and may take further price increases
items.quote: We have seen inflation, which is there to about 1.8% in Q1. We have also taken a price increase of about 1%. We see further challenges which are going to happen, in terms of looking at further inflation, which we expect could be in the range of about 1.4-1.5%.

items.statement: Mysuru plant capacity doubled from 300,000 KL to 600,000 KL; total installed capacity now ~2,200,000 KL
items.quote: Now, we have increased the installed capacity of Mysuru from 300,000 KL to 600,000 KL, which overall takes the capacity to about 2200,000 KL at the organization level.

items.statement: NeoBharat Latex and Premium Luxury (Prelux) grew well; Economy Emulsions, primers and some premium waterproofing underperformed
items.quote: Q1 mix was impacted overall, where we had higher growth coming from Smartcare, which is our waterproofing range, the whole area of Distempers and Wood Finishes. So, I think these were the general product categories where we did well . E conomy Emulsions did not do well and that is where we struggled to get the numbers

items.statement: Distribution touchpoints expanded to 1.65 lakh; 61 Beautiful Homes stores with more WIP for next quarter
items.quote: When we look at the distribution footprint, this continues to expand. Now we are at about 1.65 lakh retail touchpoints.

items.statement: New products contribute ~12% of top line; NeoBharat Latex launch widening bottom-of-pyramid reach
items.quote: From an innovation point of view, the new products continued to contribute to about 12% of our top line and that is something which has done well.

items.statement: B2B institutional business decelerated due to elections and slow infrastructure; B2B outperformed retail
items.quote: The Projects institutional business saw a bit of deceleration 6 | P a g e in terms of the overall numbers because, I think due to the whole general elections. I think the market was a little bit slow and especially when we saw the infrastructure sector was definitely on a slower side

items.statement: New entrants (Pidilite, Birla Opus) not impacting demand; pricing decisions driven by inflation not competition
items.quote: I think overall industry has been down in terms of the demand scenario we have seen. So, I don't think, it is really impacted by any larger competitive activity in terms of what is there.

items.statement: Employee cost up 23% YoY due to sick leave policy correction and headcount additions for distribution expansion
items.quote: were some corrections we had taken as part of our sick leave policy. If you take that out, the increase 20 | P a g e would be lesser in terms of what you see today. But having said that, we have also invested in higher number of people this year

items.statement: International revenue -2% in INR; +1.8% in constant currency; Ethiopia and Sri Lanka strong; Nepal, Egypt, Bangladesh weak
items.quote: Here, I think there has been a challenge in terms of the overall business. The top line has been under constraint. We have had a de -growth of about 2%, although in terms of constant currency, we would have grown by about 1.8%.

items.statement: Industrial business value growth ~5.8%; Auto Refinishes and Auto OE strong double-digit growth; General Industrial flat
items.quote: Overall, the Industrial business is almost at about 5.8% value growth , if you look from a combined business point of view.

items.statement: Rural demand recovery and monsoon progress key for H1; festive season in October (Diwali 31st) expected to boost demand
items.quote: Overall, we are now seeing an up kick in terms of the monsoons. And we hope that, today, whatever is the deficiency at the country level, that kind of really gets into a smaller zone. And I think this will really improve rural sentiments.

items.statement: Adding 18-20 Beautiful Homes stores per year; new automated blinds factory in Chennai
items.quote: We are adding about 18-20 stores every year . O ur model is very different in terms of where we align with the retailer. It's a unique model we have

items.statement: Q2 FY25 revenue guidance of -1% to +1% sequential growth in constant currency
items.quote: For Q2, we are guiding for a sequential revenue growth of (-1.0%) to (+1.0%) in constant currency.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 IT services revenue expected in range of $2.6 billion to $2.652 billion
items.quote: We expect revenues from our IT services business segment to be in the range of $2.6 billion to $2.652 billion.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 operating margin at 16.5%, up 0.1% QoQ and 0.4% YoY
items.quote: The operating margin was 16.5%, an increase of 0.1% over the last quarter.

items.statement: Expect margins to sustain in narrow band with upward bias in coming quarters
items.quote: We are confident that we can sustain our margins w ithin a narrow band with an upward bias in the coming quarters

items.statement: No significant shift in demand environment; clients remain cautious with muted discretionary spending
items.quote: In Q1, we did not see a significant shift in the demand environment. Clients remain cautious and our discretionary spending continues to be muted.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 total bookings TCV at $3.3 billion with large deal TCV of $1.2 billion
items.quote: Moving to order booking, our overall bookings TCV for the quarter was US3.3 billion with large deal TCV of US1.2 billion.

items.statement: Large deal bookings exceeded $1 billion for the quarter with 10 large deals signed
items.quote: Once again, we had a quarter where our large deal bookings exceeded US1 billion. Our success in securing 10 large deals in Q1 was a key factor that made this possible.

items.statement: Revenue from top 10 accounts grew 1.3% sequentially and 3.8% YoY in constant currency
items.quote: In fact, I would like to emphasize that even in an otherwise soft demand environment , o ur revenue from top ten accounts have grown 1.3% sequentially and 3.8% year-on-year in constant currency terms

items.statement: BFSI sector grew 0.5% sequentially in Q1 FY25, second consecutive quarter of growth
items.quote: Banking and financial services retained its positive momentum from last quarter, and we have now seen growth in this sector for two consecutive quarters. This sector grew 0.5% sequentially in Q1.

items.statement: Capco business achieved 3.4% sequential growth in Q1 FY25
items.quote: In Q1, we also maintain positive momentum in our Capco business, achieving a sequential growth of 3.4%.

items.statement: Consumer business grew 1.6% sequentially in Q1 FY25 driven by deal flow
items.quote: Driven by deal flow, the consumer business grew by 1.6% this quarter.

items.statement: Manufacturing and energy & utility sectors declined 3% and 6.3% sequentially in Q1 FY25
items.quote: However, manufacturing and energy and utility sectors continue to show weakness for us, experiencing sequential decline of 3% and 6.3% respectively.

items.statement: Investing in Lab 45 AI platform and Wipro Enterprise Gen AI Studio for delivery capabilities
items.quote: We are focused on nurturing innovation in our delivery capabilities by investing in our Lab 45 AI platform a nd the Wipro Enterprise Gen AI

items.statement: Provided foundational AI training to over 225,000 employees and advanced AI training to 30,000 employees
items.quote: We have already provided foundational training to over 225,000 of our employees and an additional 30,000 employees have received advanced AI training.

items.statement: Launched iAspire AI-powered career development platform for personalized learning pathways
items.quote: In fact, during Q1, we rolled out. iAspire and AI-powered career development platform. iAspire offers personalized learning pathways and aids in the career progression for each and every one of our employees.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 cash flows of $479 million at 132% of net income; cash and investments at $5.4 billion
items.quote: We generated yet another quarter of strong cash flows. Our cash flows of $479 million in Q1 is at 132% of our net income. With this, our current investments and cash balance now stands at Confidential-Internal $5.4 billion

items.statement: Margin expansion driven by improved utilization, fixed price productivity, and overhead optimization
items.quote: Improved utilization, fixed price productivity and optimization of overheads have been the key levers at play.

items.statement: Employee compensation cost continues to decline due to productivity focus and concerted action
items.quote: Our employee compensation cost continues to go down because of a focus and a concerted action around productivity and making sure you're able to deliver to a cost that we would like to given where our revenues are.

items.statement: GenAI-powered solutions being leveraged across all client deals; not worried about competitive intensity from peers giving large productivity gains
items.quote: So, whenever we put a solution to the client, all the deals that we have, we leverage GenAI. So, what goes to the client is GenAI powered solutions if you will and we are also infusing, like I said, GenAI into some of the engagements that we have with our clients.

items.statement: Macro environment unpredictable with political uncertainty and mixed signals on Fed rates and inflation
items.quote: The macro environment today is definitely not really as predictable. The political situation varies, but also there could be good news from the Fed in terms of the rates and also the inflation aspects of it.

items.statement: Healthcare deal involves consulting-led AI solution to help client comply with CMS guidelines
items.quote: In the healthcare sector, we have been selected by a leading US-based health solutions company to help them comply with CMS guidelines.

items.statement: Building AI-powered industry solutions across healthcare, manufacturing, telecom, and financial services
items.quote: We are also actively strengthening and accelerating our industry consulting capabilities to support this. We continue to build cross-industry solutions that will deliver value to clients across our horizontal play.

items.statement: Hedging policy maintained with $3 billion of forex derivative contracts at end of Q1 FY25
items.quote: Our hedges continue to be in line with our p olicy. We had about $3 billion of FOREX derivative contracts as hedges at the end of Q1

items.statement: Other income net of finance expenses grew 21% QoQ and YoY; accounting yield on India investments at 7.6%
items.quote: Our other income net of finance expenses grew by 21% quarter-on-quarter and year-on-year. Our accounting yield for average investments held in India in Q1 was at 7.6%.

items.statement: Net income at INR 30 billion grew 6% sequentially; EPS at Rs 5.75 grew 10% YoY
items.quote: Our net income at INR30 billion grew 6% sequentially and our EPS for the quarter at Rs.5.75 grew 10% year-on-year.

items.statement: Capco and Rizing fully integrated; collaboration yielding strong origination and synergy deals in financial services
items.quote: So, one of the things that we see is both the teams are actually leveraging the complementary capabilities, especially in the context of transformation deals. So, I think the collaboration between both Capco and Wipro's business has yielded strong origination and also significant number of synergy deals.

items.statement: Internally target mid-teens plus top-line growth coupled with 25% plus EBITDA margins
items.quote: internally we target a sort of mid -teens plus kind of top line growth coupled with 25% plus EBITDA margins

items.statement: EBITDA margin 28.7% in Q1 FY25, up 260 bps sequentially and 13.9 pp year-on-year
items.quote: we had a very healthy 28.7% EBITDA margin for the quarter, which represented 260 basis point sequential improvement and about 13.9 percentage points on year -on-year basis

items.statement: Margins sustainable with gross margins around 55% and high operating leverage
items.quote: our gross margins tend to be around 55% or so. So for every INR100 revenue, the direct sales related costs that I pay are around 45

items.statement: Blended monthly revenue per campaign INR1,580; Tier 2-3 at INR1,100 growing 10%+ YoY vs blended 5.7%
items.quote: currently my monthly revenue per campaign on a blended basis is about INR1580 per campaign per month

items.statement: Traffic healthy with 10 million unique users added in quarter, 181.3 million quarterly unique visitors; growth holding up in current quarter
items.quote: We had about 10 million unique users addition during the quarter, resulting in overall 181.3 million quarterly unique visitors

items.statement: Tier 2-3 realizations now 48-49% of Tier 1, up from 45% a year ago and 40-42% two to three years ago
items.quote: they are now at about 48%-49% of my Tier 1 realization. And this number just one year ago was 45%

items.statement: B2B contributes 25.5% of revenue, stable for last 4-5 quarters; B2B campaigns ~21-22% of total
items.quote: B2B contribute d around 25.5% of our revenues a nd this particular B2B contribution ha s been sort of similar for now last four quarters, five quarters

items.statement: Advertising spend budgeted at 5-6% of top-line for full year vs current 2-2.5%; Q1 spend INR5.8 crores
items.quote: very long term, 5% to 6% of the top line is what we would be comfortable . At present, we are at about, whatever, 2%, 2.5% or so

items.statement: Board discussing healthy dividend policy; aim to distribute at least 100% of annual profits in tax-efficient manner
items.quote: our endeavor would be that at least 100% of the annual profits should be sort of distributed or even higher amount in a manner which is tax-efficient for all shareholders combined

items.statement: Effective tax rate 8.2% in Q1 due to deferred tax reversal on INR2,900 crores treasury moving to long-term bucket; long-term rate expected 18-20%
items.quote: Effective tax rate stood at 8.2%, which is lower in this fiscal due to reversal of deferred tax on part of our treasury, which is moving from short -term to long -term bucket in fiscal '25

items.statement: Retention improved to ~60% of customers renewing into year 2 from 55% 1.5 years ago due to monthly payment plans
items.quote: currently for every 100 customers that are signing in approximately 60% of them are going into year two. And this particul ar number till about 1.5 years ago also was at 55% levels

items.statement: Cash and investments INR4,755 crores, up 14.3% YoY; treasury embedded yield ~7.2%
items.quote: Overall, cash and investments stand at about INR4,755 crores as on quarter end, growing 14.3% year-on-year

items.statement: Deferred revenue INR500 crores, up 11.1% YoY; Active Paid Campaigns 591,600, up 8% YoY
items.quote: Deferred revenue stood at about INR500 crores, growing 11.1% year-on-year. Active Paid Campaigns at the end of the quarter stood at 591,600 -odd, which was up about 8% year -on-year

items.statement: June collections strong at INR97-98 crores monthly run-rate (~INR290-295 crores quarterly) after slower April-May
items.quote: collections were about INR97-INR98 crores for the month alone. So that, if you look at on a quarterly basis, comes to about, whatever, INR290 crores, INR295 crores odd

items.statement: Expect momentum to continue in Q2 FY25; BFSI momentum may sustain through full year
items.quote: We expect the momentum to continue in Q2. The broader macro environment has remained unchanged, and businesses continue to adopt agile strategies to cope with the economic conditions.

items.statement: Depreciation and lease costs up sharply due to real estate investments in office capacity and employee engagement programs
items.quote: It's primarily as you have called out depreciation and lease are both relating to real estate investments that we have been making in terms of increasing our office capacity.

items.statement: Wage hike planned for Q3 FY25; quantum and timing still under planning
items.quote: We are looking at our Q3, which is the second half of the year, where we will do the wage hike. And we are working through that. We are kind of at the planning stage as far as that is concerned.
