name: Nippon Life India Asset Management Ltd

items.statement: Q1 FY25 operating profit was INR 3.08 bn, up 59% YoY and 9% QoQ; PAT was INR 3.32 bn, up 41% YoY.
items.quote: For Q1 FY25, Revenue stood at INR 5.05 bn, up 43% YoY and 8% QoQ. Other Income stood at INR 1.31 bn, up 12% YoY and 42% QoQ. Operating Profit stood at INR 3.08 bn, up 59% YoY and 9% QoQ. Profit After Tax stood at INR 3.32 bn - an increase of 41% YoY.

items.statement: Equity yield compressed 1 bp QoQ to ~60 bps due to telescopic pricing as equity AUM grew ~14% QoQ.
items.quote: On a QoQ basis, if you look at it, there is 1 basis point compression in the yield. On the asset class wise, the yields - on equity stands at around 60 basis points.

items.statement: Debt yield ~25 bps, liquid yield ~10-12 bps, ETF yield ~8-10 bps.
items.quote: On debt, it's around 25 basis points. On liquid, it's around 10 to 12 basis points. And on ETF, it's around 8 to 10 basis points.

items.statement: Added ~45 employees in Q1 FY25 and ~50 management trainees in July 2024; majority in Sales & Distribution and AIF.
items.quote: we have increased our employee headcount by ~45 employees in Q1 FY25. Further we have also inducted ~50 management trainees in July -2024 leading to a total headcount increase of ~95 employees.

items.statement: Other expenses (ex-employee cost) expected to increase ~12-13% per year, driven by digital, advertising, brand building.
items.quote: regarding the other costs, other than ex of employee cost, we believe it will be in the range of about -- you can expect about 12% to 13% increase every year.

items.statement: Headcount may grow ~10% annually for next 3-4 years (~100 more people), mostly entry-level and AIF skill sets.
items.quote: Based on how the penetration is increasing in the country and how the smaller cities are contributing, about 10% addition can happen, I think, for the next 3 to 4 years also. So about 100 more people can Q1 FY25 Earnings Call be added

items.statement: Branch expansion minimal: ~5-10 branches per year; focus on hub-and-spoke and digital in B30 locations.
items.quote: It could be maybe 5, 10 branches in a year. That's the kind of trend at this point of time we see.

items.statement: Staying away from sectoral/thematic NFOs; focusing on scaling core equity funds and passive (index/ETF) launches.
items.quote: We believe that a large share of such inflow into these funds that comes on the back of a market tailwind, may not be in the best interest of the investors and is typically not very sticky. We would like to continue to focus on scaling -up our existing products which have a long-term track record.

items.statement: SIP book de-risked across small, mid, large, multi-cap and sectoral funds; ~1/4 of flows each from large-cap and multi-cap funds.
items.quote: Today, the dispersion of the SIP flows have moved towards small cap, large cap, mid-cap. And we are also seeing a lot of flows now coming into the sectoral funds. So that's the way the SIP book is now building for us. It is quite de-risked at this point in time.

items.statement: Monthly SIP book rose 11% QoQ to INR 25.8 bn (annualized INR 310 bn); up 111% YoY vs industry 44%.
items.quote: Our monthly systematic book rose by 11% to INR 25.8 bn for June 2024 over March 2024. This resulted in an annualized systematic book of INR 310 bn. 5) On a YoY basis, the monthly systematic book grew by 111% over June 2023 when it was INR 12.2 bn, as against 44% growth for the Industry

items.statement: Evaluating SEBI consultation paper on new asset class; opportunity could be big but will remain cautious, may set entry ticket above INR 10 lakh.
items.quote: we are still evaluating the paper, given it is out only recently. I think the opportunity could be big. We must also be cauti ous on the new kind of risk associated with the new asset class and not get carried away with it.

items.statement: Dividend payout ~90% of profit; Board committed to sharing profits with minority shareholders; ROE 32% in Q1 FY25 but no forward guidance given.
items.quote: the Board of the company has a very clear view to keep sharing the profits of the company with all shareholders, including the minority shareholders, and we'll continue with that trend. But ROE, this business has high operating leverage. As AUM increase, expenses do not go up the same way. And -- but we'll not be able to give a number to it. But yes, for this quarter, the ROE was 32%.

items.statement: Closing AUM: Equity INR 2,598 bn, Debt INR 733 bn, Liquid INR 336 bn, ETF INR 1,402 bn.
items.quote: on the equity, the closing AUM is around INR 2,598 billion. on the debt side, it's INR 733 billion, on liquid it's INR 336 billion and on the ETF, it is INR 1,402 billion.

items.statement: Equity revenue yield is just short of 59 basis points, debt 28 basis points, liquid 12-13 basis points.
items.value: equity ~59 bps, debt 28 bps, liquid 12-13 bps
items.quote: Yes, so equity is just short of 59 basis points, debt has been 28 fairly steady liquid 12, 13 so yes.

items.statement: Flow yields come at a discount to book, ranging in mid-to-late 40s or sometimes 50s basis points depending on product mix.
items.quote: The flows do come in at a bit of a discount to the book. So, depending on the product, which sells more during the quarter, it does range anywhere in the range of mid to late 40s or something or maybe sometimes 50s and slightly higher.

items.statement: Manufacturing fund NFO of INR9,500 crore diluted equity margin by ~0.5 basis point; margin expected to improve from year two due to step-down structure and AUM-aligned commissions.
items.quote: I mean this NFO alon e would have reduced our equity margin on total equity AUM by nearly 0.5 basis point. But as I mentioned earlier, I'm not complaining about it. It's a good problem to have

items.statement: Operating revenue margin was 48 bps in Dec quarter and 46 bps in June quarter; dilution driven by AUM growth and regulatory telescopic pricing, partially offset by mix shift to equity.
items.value: 46 bps vs 48 bps in Dec quarter
items.quote: In December quarter, operating revenue margin then was 48 basis points. And for this quarter, it is 46 basis points. But look at how the AUM has moved as compared to December quarter.

items.statement: Team is evaluating options to manage speed of margin decline from rapid MTM-driven AUM growth, though absolute revenues rise; early to share details.
items.quote: We are definitely thinking of various options because the MTM growth has been so fast that how to arrest the speed of this fall, while, as I mentioned, in absolute terms, we make more money, but still margins get impacted and are there ways where we can manage this better.

items.statement: Employee cost guidance 12-15% YoY including ESOP; other expenses guidance 12-15% YoY, up from prior 8-10% range, reflecting investments in branches, digital, technology, alternatives, international.
items.quote: I think we have been broadly saying 12% to 15% type of expense growth expectation on an annual basis.

items.statement: Equity-oriented AUM at 64.3% of quarterly average AUM, up from 60.6% in Dec quarter; actively managed equity AUM INR4.4 trillion, market share 13%.
items.quote: Our asset mix has continued to further tilt towards equity, now at 64.3% on a quarterly average basis. On a closing AUM basis, actively ma naged equity funds have grown to INR4.4 trillion, market share of 13

items.statement: Industry equity net flows >INR1 trillion in quarter; SIP flows INR213 billion in June; HDFC AMC added 1.1 million unique investors (industry added 2.3 million); systematic transactions INR32.1 billion in June.
items.quote: Monthly SIP flows have continued their upward trend, INR213 billion for the month of June 2024. This quarter saw an addition of 2.3 million new unique customers.

items.statement: Equity markets cyclical; volatility will return; focus on disciplined SIP investing and investor education to sustain flows through cycles.
items.quote: Of course, there would be cycles. I don't think that equity markets -- you know this better, I mean, none of us believe that equity markets can deliver returns in a line ar fashion. There will be quarters or years where markets will witness higher volatility than what we have seen off late

items.statement: HDFC Bank channel: dedicated senior resource, strategic branch/cluster mapping, deepening engagement; HDFC Bank holds ~30% of its MF book with HDFC AMC, flow share higher than stock share.
items.quote: we have a dedicated senior resource ove rseeing this relationship and we have strategically mapped their branches and clusters with ours. And the strategic alignment has not only strengthened our relationship but has also deepened our engagement

items.statement: Branch expansion: 24 branches opened in early January; no plans for many more in near term; new branches small (2-3 people) in B-30 locations, low cost, quick breakeven.
items.quote: We had 24 branches that we opened in the first week of January. I think in the next few weeks or few months, I mean, we don't have plans to add many more.

items.statement: Product bouquet largely complete at 100 products (up from 43 in Mar'21); focus on consolidating to top-3 positions in existing categories rather than new NFOs.
items.quote: Our last NFO has made our product tally -- I mean, has made our product tally to 100. And to put that nu mber in perspective, in March of '21, exactly 3 years back, our total number of products we had on offer was 43

items.statement: Tax rate low in Q1 due to DTA reversal as assets move from short-term to long-term bucket; effective tax rate will normalize to corporate rate by year-end.
items.quote: Some of the assets move from short-term bucket to long-term bucket, the DTA benefit comes through which is why we had a similar setup in Q1 of last year and some of it is also flowed into Q1 of this year.

items.statement: Fintech channels contribute >50% of industry new SIPs, larger in B-30 towns; HDFC AMC share on incremental SIPs healthy and inching up over last 3 years.
items.quote: More than half of the new SIPs in the industry come through fintech channels. A larger proportion of that comes from B-30 towns. And on the incremental SIPs that come, we have a healthy share.

items.statement: Reiterates FY25 AUM growth guidance of 23%-24% with Group Loan growth at 20% and no downside risk seen
items.quote: We had factored this in our annual guidance of 23% to 24% portfolio growth in FY25, estimating a lower growth of 20% in the Group Loan business as against 24.7% growth in FY24. Therefore, we reiterate our annual growth guidance for FY25 and we do not see any downside risk to our growth guidance.

items.statement: Expects cost of borrowing to remain within 9.8%-9.9% range for FY25
items.quote: We expect our cost of borrowing will be within the range of 9.8 % to 9.9% for FY25 guided by a healthy mix of domestic and foreign borrowings along with maintaining a robust ALM position.

items.statement: Credit cost guided at 2.2%-2.4% for FY25 with expectation of delinquency stabilization in coming quarters
items.quote: We however, expect the delinquency trend to stabili se in the coming quarter and credit cost within t he guided range of 2.2% to 2.4% for the year.

items.statement: Reiterates confidence in achieving annual growth and profitability targets with ROA over 5% and ROE exceeding 20%
items.quote: Looking ahead, we would like to reiterate our confidence in achieving our annual growth and profitability targets . Our strategic initiatives coupled with the resilient business model and dedica ted team, position us well to mitigate the known risk effectively.

items.statement: Plans to implement district-based loan pricing in Q2 FY25 using business rule engine for granular risk alignment
items.quote: We plan to implement district-based loan pricing in Q2 FY25 leveraging the business rule engine that would help align the loan provisioning rates on a granular basis .

items.statement: Portfolio yield stable at 21% (lowest in industry) and cost of borrowing stable at 9.8% with NIM at 13.0% and cost-income ratio at 29.2%
items.quote: Our portfolio yield at 21% continues to remain the lowest in the microfinance industry resonating with our belief in serving customers with responsible pricing. On the other hand, the cost of borrowing was also stable at 9.8% despite the tightening liquidity scenario in the banking system.

items.statement: Expects disbursement run rate of INR 1,500-2,000 Crore per month in July-August with 60-65% of annual growth typically in second half
items.quote: Right, maybe between INR 1,500 to INR 2,000 Crore. It will be, you can calibrate it.

items.statement: Identified higher delinquency in Rajasthan, Kerala, Jharkhand and pockets of Tamil Nadu; non-core markets PAR0 increased 60-70bps but expected to stabilize at 3.5% credit cost
items.quote: Particularly what we saw a little higher is Rajasthan, Kerala, a bit of Jharkhand, and some pockets of Tamil Nadu.

items.statement: MFIN guardrails (INR 2L cap, 4 lender limit) may impact ~8% of borrowers but internal policy already aligned; expects short-term growth moderation industry-wide
items.quote: Our current analysis says there could be an impact of roughly 8%. But I think with new customer acquisition, we should be able to manage that.

items.statement: Retail finance book at INR 762 Crore with 70-75% individual business loans; targets 15% of total book by 2028 with 40-45% secured mix
items.quote: So, we already said earlier by 2028, it we will reach up to 15% of our book.

items.statement: Added 9 branches in Q1 FY25 taking total to 1,976; no new branches planned in Bihar, selective additions in UP, focus on Andhra, Telangana, West Bengal
items.quote: In Bihar, we are not planning any branch openings because we have sufficient branches there. It's only growing in the branch where we already have existing branches. In Uttar Pradesh probably, we will expect to add some more branches, but new branches should come from Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, or West Bengal.

items.statement: Customer acquisition back to normalcy at ~100,000 per month; 30-35% new-to-credit borrowers; unique customer share at 29% and declining
items.quote: Now we are already back to normalcy about 100,000 customers per month we should start going back. If you go back last 12 months other than the first quarter you would have added almost 100,000 new customers every month.

items.statement: Tightened credit filters at district level using rule engine; may restrict to 2-3 lenders vs MFIN's 4 in high-risk districts; dynamic quarterly review
items.quote: For example, if you feel a state is a high risk, we wouldn't allow even 4 lenders, we may do 3 lender s or 2 lenders, depending on our loan size variation based on the geography and risk, pricing based on geography risk.

items.statement: Normal monsoon expected to improve collection efficiency, reduce delinquency and boost demand through better agricultural income
items.quote: Rainfalls should actually help you stabili se further on what you call credit c ost and collections actually. Automatically when the rainfall is normal, agri product, agri job level gets improved, and agricultural level improve.

items.statement: Disbursement growth target for FY25 similar to AUM growth at 23-24% with 60-65% typically achieved in second half
items.quote: It is similar to about 23% to 24% of disbursement growth.

items.statement: Customer leverage increased ~16% and FOIR ~12% in sample checks over last 3 quarters; gold loans common but not impacting repayment capacity
items.quote: In the last three quarters what we observed is the leverage of the customer has increased by about 16% or something, the overall leverage we saw on a sample basis, not full customers. Similarly, the FOIR or repayment load or something also increased by about 12%.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 revenue INR11.48 cr, net profit INR93 lakh, EBITDA margin 13%
items.quote: I am pleased to share that we have achieved a 10% growth in both revenue and net profit compared to the same period last year. Our revenue increased to INR11.48 crores from INR10.40 crores and our net profit after tax rose to INR93 lakhs from INR84 lakhs. In Q1, our EBITDA margins were 13%.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 revenue target INR72-80 cr
items.quote: We are confident of doing the top line of INR7280 crores this year and step by step ahead towards our goal.

items.statement: Expect 35-40% revenue growth for next two years, reaching INR100 cr top line
items.quote: We are confident of growing 35% to 40% for the next two years. Our expected top line over the next two years would be INR100 crores.

items.statement: Long-term target INR1000 cr by 2032 remains on track
items.quote: And when I say INR1000 crores, that's achievable. There's no doubt in it. Just because of some, delays in API, filing of the, API one. So that has caused a delay. Otherwise, we are on track.

items.statement: Full-year blended EBITDA margin guidance 20-25%
items.quote: See, EBITDA will be around like I said before it will be around 20 % to 25% for average EBITDA for the year.

items.statement: API segment EBITDA margin target 40-45% at 72-inch range
items.quote: So you can say, overall, it will be around 40% to 45% because we want to extend our range till 72 inches.

items.statement: OEM route margins 25-30% initially
items.quote: As an OEM, we can do up to 25% to 30%.

items.statement: API license approval expected by end of August 2024
items.quote: There was minor discrepancy which has been resolved from our end and hopefully by the end of August, we should have the API.

items.statement: Capex funded by both equity and debt
items.quote: It will be both. It will be both equity and debt.

items.statement: Boiler mounting industry major customer base; valves replaced every 12-18 months
items.quote: But we are giving these Valves to the Boiler Mounting Industry for the pipelines. And they are changing walls every 12 months, 18 months. So that's our major customer base as well,

items.statement: Promoter holding diluted from 70.79% to 60.99% to fund expansion and working capital
items.quote: Actually we were approached by long-term investors and as an opportunity we thought this was the right time for dilution. Since we require funds for expansion post API and managing working capital.

items.statement: API commercialization expected in Q4 FY25 adding to top line
items.quote: Yes, the orders, yes, you can say that. That will add to the top line.

items.statement: Wastewater management sector inquiries received but focus remains on API; premature to comment
items.quote: It's an exciting sector for us too, but we are receiving inquiries but our current focus is API. So it's premature to say anything right now, but surely some developments are happening over there.

items.statement: Pathway diversification on hold to concentrate on API
items.quote: Yes, it is on the hold. We want to concentrate mainly on API.

items.statement: Revised FY25 revenue growth guidance to 3% to 4% in constant currency; operating margin guidance remains 20% to 22%
items.quote: Given our strong performance in Q1 and our current outlook, we have revised our revenue growth guidance for the full financial year to 3% to 4% growth in constant currency terms. Our operating margin guidance for the financial year remains at 20% to 22

items.statement: Signed 34 large deals with total contract value of $4.1 billion, 58% net new
items.quote: We had another quarter of strong large deal wins with 34 large deals at a total contract value of $4.1 bn.

items.statement: Operating margin expanded 1 percentage point sequentially to 21.1% driven by Project Maximus and normalization
items.quote: Operating margin improved by 1% sequentially to 21.1% led by 1.4% improvement in gross margins on account of strong operating performance across different dimensions.

items.statement: Acquisition of in-tech closed; annual revenue of in-tech around €170 million
items.quote: With respect to our recent acquisition of in-tech, we have received the required approvals and have closed the acquisition transaction.

items.statement: Early signs of improvement in US financial services; discretionary spend remains under pressure
items.quote: Along with our overall robust performance in Q1 and strong opportunity pipeline, we are seeing early signs of improvement in Financial Services vertical in the U.S. While discretionary spends continue to be under pressure.

items.statement: Pricing environment stable; value-based selling under Project Maximus improved pricing
items.quote: So, pricing environment has pretty much remained stable, but if you look at again one of the pillars of Maximus is value-based selling where we have been able to make an impact which has helped us improve our overall pricing.

items.statement: Generative AI traction strong via Topaz; 270,000 employees trained in AI; not disclosing Gen AI revenue separately
items.quote: We continue to see strong traction from our clients for Generative AI programs del ivered through Topaz. Enterprises are focused on their own data sets that can be used in Generative AI large language models

items.statement: Hiring 15,000 to 20,000 freshers in FY25; utilization at 85.3%; attrition stable at 12.7%
items.quote: We are lo oking at hiring 15,000 to 20,000 freshers this year, depending on how we see the growth

items.statement: Revenue guidance increased to 3% to 4% in constant currency for FY25.
items.quote: Driven by a strong all-round performance in Q1, improvement in U.S. Financial Services, strong large deal closures and in-tech acquisition, we are in creasing the revenue guidance to 3% to 4% in constant currency terms

items.statement: Operating margin guidance maintained at 20% to 22% for FY25.
items.quote: We are maintaining our operating margin guidance at 20% to 22%.

items.statement: Closed 34 large deals with TCV of $4.1 billion, 58% net new.
items.quote: We closed 34 large deals with TCV of $4.1 bn, 58% of this was net new.

items.statement: BFSI returned to positive growth after six quarters led by U.S. Financial Services recovery in mortgage, capital markets, cards and payments.
items.quote: BFSI returned to positive growth after six quarte rs led by ramp-ups of large deals and absence of one-off of last quarter. In the U.S., we see some recovery in areas like mortgage, capital markets and cards and

items.statement: Q1 operating margin benefited 40 bps from a one-time revenue recovery of 50 bps from an India client.
items.quote: It is 50 bps on revenue, Kawal, which is impacting 40 bps on margins.

items.statement: Wage hike timing undecided; variable pay increased in Q1; comp review expected during year as headwind.
items.quote: we have not really decided. We are evaluat ing, considering all the factors that we always consider including the inflation, including when was the last wage revision taken, the environment, the macro environment as well as the peer practice

items.statement: Project Maximus levers (value-based selling, pyramid, lean automation, nearshoring, fresher hiring) continue to offset headwinds; aim to more than offset in medium term.
items.quote: So you have seen that, and our endeavor is to continuously focus on all of that. At this point in time, they are offsetting the headwinds to a large extent. The endeavor is to more than offset the headwinds in the mid-term.

items.statement: In-tech acquisition closed; acquisition revenue run rate ~€170 million last year; partial revenue contribution in FY25.
items.quote: if you look at the numbers that we printed, when we announced the acquisition of in-tech, revenue was around €170 mn. And it is only going to be part of the year consid ering we just concluded or closed the transaction

items.statement: Discretionary spending remains challenging outside U.S. Financial Services; client conversations focused on cost takeout, efficiency, consolidation, automation.
items.quote: Outside of that, the discretionary still remains simi lar to where we were, when we started the year, which is still in a difficult situation. So that is the one that we have seen the change in. The client conversations, in general, there is a lot of talk and discussion with Generative AI, but the programs, even though they are not POCs, the actual projects are not large revenue projects

items.statement: Generative AI projects moving beyond POCs to actual programs in legacy modernization, fraud detection, credit process simplification; data and cloud prerequisites needed.
items.quote: We are definitely seeing more and more discussi ons in enterprises on Generative AI programs. Jayesh also shared a couple of examples. I shared a couple of examples. And these are not POCs, these are actual projects where we are participating

items.statement: H1 FY25 expected to be better than H2 FY25; guidance reflects typical seasonality and current visibility.
items.quote: We still continue to bel ieve our first half is going to be better than the second half. And Q1 is just a testimony of that. From that perspective, we have delivered from there. Of course, the fact that we have increased guidance is also a proof that we are seeing the three quarters better than what we envisaged earlier

items.statement: Expect double-digit revenue growth for FY25 without TajSATS consolidation
items.quote: We expect a double -digit growth in FY '24, '25, as we have also guided previously. And with an expected 20% revenue growth, 20% plus, I would say, revenue growth in July based on business on the books as on July 17.

items.statement: Guidance of double-digit growth excludes TajSATS consolidation from August to March
items.quote: Guidance that we have given fo r the full year of double -digit growth, could be 10%, could be 11%, could be 12%, but definitely north of 10%. That does not include the consolidated figures of TajSATS those from August to March.

items.statement: New businesses (Ginger, Ama, Qmin) to grow north of 30-35% with high EBITDA margins
items.quote: The new bu sinesses will continue to grow N orth of 30% to 35%. That's what we've guided. That's Ginger, Ama, and Qmin w ith very high EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Reimagined businesses (TajSATS, Chambers) to grow 15-20% with high flow-through
items.quote: And the reimagined businesses which is TajSATS and chambers will continue their journey also of 15% to 20% growth. Anybody's guess where it would be, but with very high flow-through.

items.statement: Management fee income to keep growing at CAGR of almost 15%
items.quote: Not to forget Achal and you followed us for -- since we announced aspiration 2022 that our management fee income will also keep growing at a CAGR of almost 15%.

items.statement: Target to open 25 hotels in FY25 with 7 already opened and 18 more to go
items.quote: We remain confident to be able to deliver on our guidance for the full financial year backed by IHCL's diversified and not like -for-like revenue growth and the tailwinds for the industry. We should not forget we still have another 19 hotels to open which will add further to not like-for-like growth with the 6 that we have opened in Q1. And actually, we did open 1 hotel a few days ago in Patna, th

items.statement: Investing in brand and revenue-enhancing capex through upgradation, expansions and new Greenfield projects
items.quote: Our free cash flows have tripled in Q1 at INR146 crores when compared with INR47 crores last year. Our gross cash reserves stand at close to INR2,100 crores, enabling us to reinvest in brand and revenue-enhancing capex through upgradation, expansions as well as investment in new Greenfield projects.

items.statement: Renovations ongoing at St. James London, President Mumbai, Taj Holiday Village Goa, Jai Mahal Palace Jaipur; Taj Malabar Cochin nearing completion
items.quote: Some of the hotels with renovations ongoing were St. James in London, President in Mumbai, Taj Holiday Village in Goa and Jai Mahal Palace in Jaipur. We are about to finish the renovation in our subsidiary that is Taj Malabar in Cochin, which is an absolutely brand-enhancing property for us in that part of India.

items.statement: Portfolio crossed 325+ hotels with 224 operational and 100+ in pipeline; 16 signed and 6 opened in Q1
items.quote: We continue to demonstrate industry-leading growth with 16 hotels signed and 6 hotels opened in Q1 '24 -25. More importantly, with 224 hotels operational and more than 100 hotels in our pipeline, we ha ve crossed the milestone of 325 -plus hotels portfolio.

items.statement: Gateway brand rollout commencing with 15 hotels, aiming to scale to 100 by 2030
items.quote: IHCL will also introduce, as we mentioned in the last call, the reimagined gateway in Q2 of this year. Gateway will be a full-service hotel offering in the upscale and maybe even in some cases, up to upper upscale segment. The brand rollout will commence with a portfolio of 15 hotels, and we aim to scale it to 100 hotels by 2030.

items.statement: TajSATS facility near Noida Airport expected to be operational by March-June 2025
items.quote: By March 25. I mean between March to June of next year. Ankur Dalwani: Basically it'll come along with -- when the airport is operational, which is expected sometime towards the end of second half -- end of first half around June May-June

items.statement: Structural tailwinds intact with demand-supply mismatch expected to continue (10% demand growth vs 6% supply growth)
items.quote: The demand-supply mismatch is expected to continue in the coming years, not just in the coming quarters, but in the coming years, with industry experts expecting a 10% growth in demand versus a muted 6% growth in supply.

items.statement: July revenue growth expected at 20%+ based on business on books as of July 17
items.quote: And with an expected 20% revenue growth, 20% plus, I would say, revenue growth in July based on business on the books as on July 17.

items.statement: 12 more auspicious wedding dates in July 24 to March 25 vs same period last year driving strong comeback
items.quote: With 12 more auspicious dates in July '24 to March '25 compared to same period last year, Indian weddings are expected to stage a strong comeback.

items.statement: TajSATS maintains market leadership with 59% share and industry-leading 24% EBITDA margin
items.quote: TajSATS continues to m aintain market leadership with a share of 59%, retaining an EBITDA margin of 24%. This 24% in the sector that TajSATS is operating in is considered an industry-leading margin globally.

items.statement: Q2 expected to be stronger than Q1 with better margins driven by rooms and wedding revenue
items.quote: On your assessment, Shaleen on Q2, basically, you have answered it what I would have answered. So you have answered for me. So Q2 will be stronger than Q1, maybe it's the best ever Q2 that the sector would have seen. At least July and part of August, we can alread y see, because half of July is behind us and the other half, we have pretty much the security. So we know that. Then if you obviously h

items.statement: Payroll cost expected at 26.5-27% of revenue for full year vs 29.7% in Q1
items.quote: I think the few things will come back as business comes back, we will see some correction or increase in the payroll cost. Also a payroll cycle will get impacted. So -- but the overall number, as you see right now in Q1 was 29.7%. For the year, we normally do 26.5% to 27%. I think we'll be in the same sort of range for payroll.

items.statement: Management fees grew 17% YoY from INR98 cr to INR114 cr in Q1; expect sustained growth with higher flow-through
items.quote: Our capital light, not like -for-like growth has helped us grow our management fees by 17% from INR98 crores last year to INR114 crores in Q1 '24/'25. We expect this growth in management fees to sustain with higher flow-throughs to the

items.statement: New businesses (Ginger, Qmin, Ama Stays & Trails) grew 37% YoY; Ginger grew 45% YoY
items.quote: IHCL's new business is comprised of Ginger, Qmin and Ama Stays and Trails continue to showcase strong growth at 37% year-on-year. Ginger grew 45% year-on-year enabled by the stellar performance of the flagship Ginger Mumbai Airport Hotel as well as a strong growth in food and beverage revenues driven by cuminization of Ginger hotels.

items.statement: Reimagined brands TajSATS and Chambers showed strong double-digit growth
items.quote: The reimagined brands of TajSATS and chambers also showed a strong double -digit growth.

items.statement: Launched Taj Branded Residences with first project in Chennai (123 residences, 235 rooms, 23 floors); market size INR22,000 cr with double-digit growth
items.quote: We are pleased to announce our entry into the new segment of Taj Branded Residences with the first one coming soon in Chennai. This is a very lucrative market segment in India with over INR22,000 crores of aggregate market value today and showcasing double-digit growth year-on-year.

items.statement: TajSATS shareholders' agreement changes approved; consolidation as subsidiary effective August 1, 2024
items.quote: The Board of IHCL has approved certain changes to the shareholders ' agreement of TajSATS Limited, which allow IHCL to consolidate TajSATS as a subsidiary in its consolidated accounts. The consolidation is expected to be effective on 1st, August 2024.

items.statement: Proposed combination of TIHL with St. James Hotels London via share swap and business transfer; expected completion in Q3
items.quote: In order to simplify our operating model and holding structure, it is proposed to combine business of TIHL with St. James Hotels London through a share swap and simultaneous business transfer agreement. The transaction is expected to complete in Q3 post closing formalities.

items.statement: Domestic occupancy averaging 76% with key markets at 80%+; RevPAR premium well above industry average
items.quote: I think what we have uploaded, you will see that we have occupancy averaging around 76% on the domestic front. In certain markets, it is in 80s like Goa, Mumbai, Delhi, in certain, it is very close to 80 like Bangalore and Kolkata and Chennai is between 75%, 78%.

items.statement: Bangalore RevPAR grew 10% driven by higher ARR; GCC demand remains strong
items.quote: Bangalore in particular has actually been one of the stronger cities grown by 10% RevPAR which has really been on the back of higher ARR etc. So I think every real estate market will have their own dynamics, residential in Bangalore was -- had gone to a different status here and there that is how that is correcting. But I think in general, the GCC has remained strong and therefore which is actuall

items.statement: Foreign tourist arrivals (non-NRI) still lagging; hoping for recovery from October-November 2024
items.quote: But I hope your comment about everything going back to what it was holds true b ecause that would mean a significant increase in foreign tourist arrivals, because outbound from India has started. But the foreign tourist arrivals, the real foreign tourists, I'm not talking about the NRIs, is still lagging behind. And that is an importa nt segment for our palaces and our iconic assets. So we are hop

items.statement: Management reiterated FY25 guidance and expects to achieve it
items.quote: Lastly, we stick to our stated guidance for FY '25 and are optimistic of achieving the same.

items.statement: Domestic order inflows slowed in Q1 due to general elections; recovery expected from Q2 end or Q3
items.quote: This decline is primarily due to slower order inflows during the quarter influenced by the general elections, which were affected both from private and public.

items.statement: Cement, steel, power and sugar sectors showing traction for H2 FY25

items.quote: I can give you the industry from rubber, plastic, steel, pump, packing, gas, and energy. These are the sectors and the commercial sector.

items.statement: Microscopic global market share; competition in West based on support and delivery not price

items.quote: We are expecting a large quantity of orders coming in from the marine sector next year. So I believe that we would be having a very healthy inflow coming next year beginning or mid next year.

items.quote: We have received our order on high speed from a large OEM, whereby we believe the potential is large and we are expecting that the orders will flow in for execution in the next calendar year.
