items.quote: There are a lot of distortion factors that makes everything difficult to predict, but overall, we can say that there is an uncertainty we expect that the market will be flat or slightly better and that is my view and it is aligned with the IHS forecast.

items.statement: EV subsidy elimination in some European countries causing electrification slowdown
items.quote: The reality in the European market is that now all this electrification process has been a slowdown mainly because of the elimination of the certain subsidies that certain countries were giving to the electric vehicles.

items.statement: India exports ~13% of sales in CY23; castings, gears, aluminum castings key export opportunities
items.quote: From India, we were closer to, I think 13%. So, export opportunities in India are there. As I said the biggest opportunities are there in castings, iron castings. They are also there in gears and aluminum castings.

items.statement: Receivables up in H1 CY24 due to stopping factoring/discounting on 30 June 2024
items.quote: The working capital especially on the receivables is because we did factoring and built and discounting on 31st December 23, which we have stopped doing on 30th June, therefore the number has gone up.

items.statement: M&A focus on India; not preferred route in Europe currently
items.quote: Not really. Let us say that it is not our preferred route right now to invest in Europe in different countries, let us say, stressed assets is not the strategy. We prefer to focus our resource on the Indian market where we think there will be development in the future.

items.statement: Dividend doubled to Rs 5/share; cash outflow INR 1,897 million in H1 CY24
items.quote: Cash outflow due to dividends was INR 1,897 million due to the doubling of dividend to Rs. 5 per share.

items.statement: India PAT margin crossed 10% for first time in H1 CY24 (10.4%)
items.quote: In fact, this is the first half year when India PAT margin has gone beyond the 10% mark.

items.statement: Europe recovery dependent on US election outcome and new government investment strategies
items.quote: We think that we need to wait until the US elections and after that probably in Q1 CY25 we will see the revamp of the market again.

items.statement: Europe market forecast uncertainty due to electrification pace, economy, elections, Chinese imports
items.quote: It is very difficult to make predictions in Europe now because of all the things that are happening with the electrifications, with the economy, with let us say all kind of elections we have had and the political uncertainty in Europe plus the introduction of the Chinese cars that are entering into our market.

items.statement: Roof Systems kept separate as Tier-1 business with centralized R&D; CIE India focused on Tier-2
items.quote: Roof Systems is a Tier-1 business. All the other businesses are Tier-2 businesses. And therefore when you say will CIE also look at plastics or forgings o r this separately, the answer is no, because CI E India since the last 10 years has focused on Tier-2 business

items.statement: Metalcastello diversification underway: new customer added, EV transmission programs delayed
items.quote: we are already working on the diversification, we have included a new customer and also we explained in the last calls that we got in big business from new American transmission manu facturer for the electric vehicles , especially for the electric commercial vehicles and light commercial vehicles. Those programs, unfortunately because of the situation of the electrification are delayed

items.statement: Aluminum forging in Europe: volumes low, relevant contribution expected in 2-3 years
items.quote: We will need at least couple of years, 2-3 years in order to see this business giving us relevant chunk of business in our companies.

items.statement: RCS revenue stream expected to start in Q2 and scale meaningfully by end of FY25
items.quote: Our MaaP platform for Google RCS has gone live in July and I expect the revenue stream to start in Q2. I expect RCS to scale up quickly and be meaningful by end of this financial year and we are best placed 3 to capture this space

items.statement: New clients added in FY24 contributed Rs.59 Cr revenue in Q1 FY25
items.quote: the new clients we added in FY24 contributed to Rs.59 Cr of revenues in Q1

items.statement: OTT contribution to revenues increased from 8% to 20% with 177% YoY growth
items.quote: OTT contribution to revenues moved from 8% to 20%, an incredible growth of 177% YoY.

items.statement: Gross margin improved YoY and sequentially despite Rs.120 Cr revenue and Rs.30 Cr gross margin impact from Vi ILD deal exit
items.quote: We improved our gross margin % on both YoY and sequential basis. The numbers do not reveal the full picture – over the last 4 quarters, we have seen a material shift in the market. We had flattish organic growth on a YoY basis. We saw a severe disruption in international messaging business on the back of consolidation between CPaaS players globally as well as shifting of use cases to OTT channels.

items.statement: Domestic SMS expected to pick up in Q2 and Q3 per historical seasonality; ILD business close to bottoming out
items.quote: Q1 is always little seasonally the Q4, so is little sea sonally, Q2, Q3 are typically stronger, particularly from a domestic side. So, I do think domestic will pick up in Q2, Q3, in line with historical trends. ILD, I think probably is close to bott oming out

items.statement: No guidance provided for Wisely ATP domestic outlook; international rollout contingent on India results
items.quote: So, Anil, like we're not giving any guidance. So, let's hope for best. We are p utting all our efforts. So, whenever there is an update, definitely we will update the

items.statement: Exited Vi ILD deal due to minimum guarantee demands; not in business of giving minimum guarantees
items.quote: Vodafone Idea Limited was asking for mini mum guarantees. Our position is very clear. We are not in the business of giving the minimum guarantees. We play to our strength, which is our core strategies technology. So, we have exited this deal

items.statement: MaaP platform went live in July with Vodafone; revenue expected from Q2 onwards
items.quote: We just went live with Vodafone, and it is expected to show some of the revenues will flow in Q2 onwards.

items.statement: Expect Q2 exports to be better than Q1 and continue on a growth path
items.quote: On this basis, we expect Q2 to be better than Q1, and will continue to be on a growth path in the exports business unit.

items.statement: Target Freedom 125 capacity of 40,000 units per month by Q4 FY25
items.quote: We are starting with a capacity of 10,000 units per month in quarter 2, but we have planned to take this capacity up to 40,000 per month by quarter 4.

items.statement: Expect domestic industry volume growth of 6% to 8% in FY25 with faster growth in 125cc+ segment
items.quote: So, the industry outlook as we said we think it should be 6% to 8%. And the top half the 125cc plus segment will grow much faster.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY25 moderated between INR700 to INR800 crores primarily for electric 3-wheeler facility at Waluj
items.quote: It should be moderated between INR700 to INR800 crores. A large part of that will primarily go towards the commissioning of our new electric 3-wheeler facility in Waluj and other capabilities that we are building essentially for electric.

items.statement: Commodity cost inflation estimated at 50-70 bps impact in Q2 FY25; pricing action taken covers about half
items.quote: The current out look for commodities suggests that we could be looking at inflation in costs across a number of lines in this current quarter. Although most pronounced within each of them is on aluminum and copper. And to partly mitigate the probable cost impact, that is looking to be anywhere in the range of 50 bps to 70 bps, we've taken around the pricing at the beginning of this quarter, which

items.statement: PLI incentive accrual at 13% of eligible EV sales contributing under 50 bps to margin in Q1 FY25
items.quote: It would be under 50 bps of contribution Binay.

items.statement: Freedom 125 addressable market 450,000-500,000 customers per month in 100-125cc segment with CNG access
items.quote: Of the approximately 1 million motorcycles sold per month in India, almost 75% are in this segment, the 100cc to 125cc segment and about 60% of the demand of these customers has access to CNG pumping station. Hence, our addressable market is about 450,000 to 500,000 customers per month.

items.statement: Freedom 125 initial bookings at ~4,200 units with 90% from Maharashtra and Gujarat, overwhelmingly for top variant
items.quote: So, the bookings right now about 4,200, I mean this is yesterday's figure. 90% of this has come from Maharashtra and Gujarat because we opened all India bookings just a couple of days back. So almost 80%, 90% of these bookings are Maharashtra and Gujarat. Most of these bookings are actually for the top end, which was the ₹1,10,000 LED headlamp disk, overwhelmingly for the top end.

items.statement: Electric portfolio contributed 14% of domestic revenue in Q1 FY25 (60% from e-2W, 40% from e-3W)
items.quote: In this quarter, a sizable 14% of the domestic revenue has been contributed by the electric portfolio comprising both electric 3-wheeler and electric 2-wheelers.

items.statement: Pulsar NS400Z bookings nearly 2,400 units; deliveries commenced with ~1,000 units last month
items.quote: Capping it all with the launch of the biggest Pulsar NS400Z, which has been received very well as reflected in the bookings of almost 2,400 units. Deliveries have commenced. And I think last m onth, we have delivered about 1,000 units

items.statement: Nigeria motorcycle sales dropped from 50,000 to under 5,000 in April, recovered to 15,000; Africa down 40% YoY
items.quote: Our benchmark motorcycle sales in Nigeria of 50,000 per month has dropped down to under 5,000 in April, but has now recovered to 15,000 levels, still far from the 50,000 benchmark. Compared to Q1 of previous year, we are down by about 40% in Africa.

items.statement: Brazil plant commenced production in June with 20,000 units single-shift capacity, scalable to 50,000; expect Brazil to be top 3 international market
items.quote: The new plant in Brazil commenced production in June, it has a single shift capacity of 20,000 units per annum, but that is scalable to 50,000 units per annum. This will make a quantum change to our capability to introduce new models and wide n distribution. Traction for our Dom inar brand has been excellent and in the medium term, we expect Brazil to be amongst our top 3 international markets

items.statement: Triumph sold over 60,000 bikes in 57 countries in first year, generating INR1,200 crores revenue; domestic at 100 stores targeting 150 by H1
items.quote: This month, we actually completed a year of Triumph sales during which over 60,000 bikes have been sold in over 57 countries, bringing a revenue of INR1,200 crores to Bajaj Auto.

items.statement: Bajaj Auto Credit (BACL) covers ~50% of markets/stores; on track for 100% coverage by March 2025
items.quote: 50% of the Bajaj Auto markets and stores have now been covered by BACL. We are on track to reach 100% by March '25

items.statement: Spares revenue crossed INR1,350 crores in Q1 FY25; financing penetration 75% for motorcycles, 19% for 3-wheelers
items.quote: The spares revenue at the moment, is about INR 1,350 crores, and the financing penetration for motorcycles was 75% and for 3-wheelers was 19%.

items.statement: Next quarter newsprint cost may increase a couple of percent but advertising should absorb it
items.quote: we believe next quarter there will be some increase in the newsprint cost, but advertising should be able to take care of that.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin expanded 700 bps YoY to 31%
items.quote: expanded our EBITDA margins by 700 basis points, taking it to a robust 31%.

items.statement: Radio segment EBITDA margin held at 34% with 6% top-line growth
items.quote: The radio segment achieved a margin of 34% this quarter, which matches last year's margin of 34%. The to p line grew by 6

items.statement: Advertising revenue grew 8.4% YoY to Rs 4,277 million
items.quote: our advertising revenue grew by 8.4% Y-o-Y, reaching Rs. 4,277 million in Q1 FY2025

items.statement: Government ad revenue grew ~20% YoY contributing ~20% of ad revenue
items.quote: The government grew at almost 20% over last year and the contribution was in the range of around 20%.

items.statement: Auto ad category grew ~35% YoY contributing ~8% of ad revenue
items.quote: this quarter we have shown a growth of almost 35% in the auto category and auto is now contributing almost 8% in the overall revenue.

items.statement: Average newsprint cost fell 17.2% YoY to Rs 46,900/MT; freight rise may push price up next quarter
items.quote: Our average newsprint cost has reduced to Rs. 46,900 per metric ton, representing a substantial 17.2% Y-o-Y reduction in rates.

items.statement: Newsprint cost currently 37% of total cost; Indian mills price on import parity, hedging limited to 3-5 months
items.quote: As of now, news print is 37% of my overall cost. And why it has come down , b ecause the overall cost has come down.

items.statement: Advertiser mix largely unchanged YoY; education ~20%, real estate 7-8%, auto 8%, FMCG 4%, jewellery 4%
items.quote: The advertising mix has remained almost the same between last year and this year . For example, education, this is one of the biggest quarter for education , remains there only , contributing almost 20% plus even last year and same year .

items.statement: Average pages stable at 20.88 vs 20.8 last year; minimum ~19 pages, festival up to 24-26
items.quote: Same, we are at 20.8 8 pages, last year in the same quarter we were at 20.8, so almost same , 0.3% growth.

items.statement: Circulation ~40 lakh copies; new distribution and readership schemes launched, impact expected post-September
items.quote: We are doing around 40 lakh copies as of now, sir. And as we discussed that our efforts going forward will be that that we need to increase the copies from here on.

items.statement: Digital monthly active users crossed 18 million in June 2024; paywall and app advertising experiments underway
items.quote: our monthly active user in the month of June has crossed 18 million, which is a very, very positive sign.

items.statement: Radio growth limited until government allows news and current affairs on private FM
items.quote: this segment largely will stay in the same size, same percentages, unless until Government of India opens up the news and current affairs in this.

items.statement: Board declared Rs 7 interim dividend for Q1; further payout ratio decisions with Board
items.quote: The Board has decided and declared a Rs. 7 interim dividend for this quarter . And I am sure considering the overall growth of the business and the cash , Board will take a very arrived and thoughtful call going forward also.

items.statement: Newsprint price may rise a couple of percent next quarter due to freight cost increase
items.quote: Because of the international sector, the freight has again started going up. So, maybe in the next quarter we may see a couple of percentages increase in the news print price.

items.statement: Committed to doubling VNB every four years (approx 19% CAGR) through APE growth and margin improvement
items.quote: we are focusing on two outcomes. One is growth that is faster than industry growth. This is new business retail APE growth. And second is in terms of VNB growth , again getting back to doubling every four years in a very consistent manner

items.statement: Q1 FY25 VNB margin at 25.0%, down from 26.2% YoY due to product mix and investments
items.quote: Our new business margins are 25.0% compared to 26.2% last year. The margin compression is primarily due to the product mix and continued investments in infrastructure, manpower, and technology.

items.statement: Expect ~100 bps gross margin impact from new surrender value regulations if no mitigating actions taken
items.quote: We anticipate a gross impact of approximately 100 bps on the company's new business margin due to higher surrender value payable on early exits.

items.statement: Will remain range-bound on margins, flexible to trade off within a range to pursue APE and VNB growth
items.quote: As the year unfolds, our focus remains on achieving absolute APE and VNB growth. We will be flexible in trading off margins within a range, in order to pursue these objectives.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 mix: ULIPs 38%, non-par savings 35%, par 16%, term 6%, annuities 5%; ULIP mix moderating from 38% to ~35% exit rate in June
items.quote: While we began the year with a high ULIP mix, we have been successful in lowering it during the quarter. We anticipate this moderation to continue in the coming months, driven primarily by product launches across other categories.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 individual APE grew 31% YoY (21% 2-year CAGR), outpacing private sector and industry
items.quote: We have kicked off the year on a strong note, achieving a robust YoY growth of 31% based on individual APE, translating to a 2-year CAGR of 21%.

items.statement: Raising sub-debt up to Rs 2,000 crore in one or more tranches over next 12 months to strengthen solvency and fuel growth
items.quote: To strengthen our solvency position, we will be raising sub-debt up to Rs 2,000 crore, in one or more tranches, over the next 12 months. This sub-debt raise will help fuel our growth aspirations.

items.statement: New IRDAI surrender value regulations effective Oct 1; mitigating via distributor payout restructuring (deferment and clawbacks), not SOS basis
items.quote: We endeavour to achieve this primarily through restructuring distributor pay-outs using a combination of deferment and clawbacks. We also believe this regulation will improve market conduct, moderate competitive intensity, and benefit players who have been relatively prudent.

items.statement: Tax sensitivity assumes current 12.5%+surcharge rate moving to 25% on all policyholder and shareholder surplus with no exemptions
items.quote: It's assuming that the current tax rate of 12.5% plus surcharge changes to 25%. And the policyholder and shareholder segment surplus get taxed at the higher rate. Essentially, everything gets taxed at the higher rate.

items.statement: Project Inspire technology transformation on track for group business launch between Q3-Q4 FY25
items.quote: We are on track to launch our group business transformation between Q3 and Q4 this year.

items.statement: Calibrated pricing approach maintained; retail protection pricing changes minimal (5% for age >60 segment, <0.1% of business)
items.quote: For one segment which is above 60 there was up to a 5% change in price and this business is less than 0.1% of our overall business. So honestly not hing of any consequence at all a nd pricing will evolve based on how deep we go into the country in terms of customer segments

items.statement: Q1 margin gap driven by 1.3% negative product mix from ULIP share rising to 38%, offset by 0.3% positive fixed cost absorption from 31% growth
items.quote: In the Q1 context, everything is pretty much product mix because the scale is back. The growth was 31% for the period. You will see a positive fixed cost absorption of 0.3%, but we have a 1.3% negative on the product mix, which is largely the unit -linked mix increasing from 25% to 38% on a like-to-like basis.

items.statement: ULIP mix at 38% for Q1 but exit rate in June dropped to 35%
items.quote: I just want to add tha t, while for the quarter, ULIP mix was 38%, but exit rate in June has come down to about 35%.

items.statement: Sub-debt headroom of INR 2,000 crores approved for 12 months; full raise would add 20-22% to solvency
items.quote: Our headroom today, based on the regulatory limit is about INR 2,000 crores. We will see in terms of how we want to go about it. We have an approval to raise this over a 12 -month period in one or more tranches.

items.statement: Full INR 2,000 crore sub-debt raise would increase solvency by 20-22%
items.quote: And to your other question, it would add about 20% to 22% if we raised the entire INR 2,000 crores.

items.statement: Risk-based capital regime expected in 12-18 months, allowing more business with same capital
items.quote: We are also expecting over the next 12 to 18 months risk -based capital regime to kick in. When that happens, our understanding is that we will be able to write more business with the same amount of capital.

items.statement: Non-par product competitiveness to improve; IRR calibration expected due to lower surrender charges
items.quote: Our product competitiveness should definitely go up. And like I mentioned earlier, today, one is that we reprice with a lot of frequency as and when interest rates move materially. That is number one. And number two is, even today, there is a material difference in IRRs, and that IRRs can't come out of thin air. It has to be funded from somewhere either by the customer or by the shareholders or th

items.statement: Non-par savings seeing broad-based traction across ticket sizes, tiers, and new product launches like Click 2 Achieve
items.quote: We are seeing good traction in this category. We are seeing traction both in above 5 lakhs and below 5 lakhs. We are seeing traction in Tier 1, 2 and 3. So any which way we cut non-par, we are seeing traction.

items.statement: ULIP sum assured multiple increased from 20x to near 30x; rider attachment still nascent with significant headroom
items.quote: So, I mentioned the 20x was the number some time back. Now it is close to 30x.

items.statement: Longer policy tenures (21 years vs 16) driven by Click 2 Achieve variants; longer terms improve margins meaningfully
items.quote: On your second question in terms of the increase in tenure, that is something that we have been consciously driving because longer-term products can offer better value to customers. And this has been enabled by our new launch of Click 2 Achieve that we had launched a few months back.

items.statement: Higher surrender values from Oct 1 neutral to margins due to pricing prudence and surrender assumptions
items.quote: Not in our case because of what all Eshwari had mentioned , prudence in pricing as well as surrender assumptions does not result in a very significant change in our reserves. So that does not affect our accounting profit.

items.statement: VNB margin decline QoQ due to lower absolute scale in Q1 vs Q4, not product mix or profitability changes
items.quote: On a sequential basis, there is not much difference in product mix. But yes, the difference is largely on account of absolute scale of business that gets done in quarter 1 versus quarter 4. That is probably the difference.

items.statement: Annuity business degrew due to calibrated approach avoiding irrational pricing; surrender charges to impact deferred annuity post April 1
items.quote: There is some irrational pricing in certain pockets. We have to take that into account, and we are not in the business of writing business which is not viable for us in terms of either managing the risk or the pricing.

items.statement: Sub-debt negative carry minimal at 20-30 bps; no material VNB impact due to large investment book and duration flexibility
items.quote: In the past the sub-debt that we carry has a fairly negligible negative carry of about 20- 30 basis points because we have the ability to invest. All the sub debt that will be raised will get invested and we don't expect negative carry on that to be significant.

items.statement: Solvency ratio post-dividend impact ~5% lower than current 186%
items.quote: Around 5% impact on solvency after assuming impact of dividend payout.

items.statement: Composite license hopeful for parliamentary passage; internal product ideas ready if approved
items.quote: So, we are hopeful that it gets introduced in both the houses of parliament. And hopefully, it gets passed. We have been waiting for quite a long time. And if that were to happen, we will evaluate our options. But the bigger picture is how do

items.statement: Target PAT margin roughly 20% and EBITDA margin 23-24%; invest excess margins in growth
items.quote: We have said that generally roughly around 20% PAT and roughly around 23%, 24% EBITDA that's kind of a target number we are carrying today on our mind.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 PAT margin ~15% due to seasonality; expect expansion as revenue scales
items.quote: So for the quarter, it is roughly around 15% being a seasonal quarter, it's lower in top line, while the costs are slightly more flattish for the year.

items.statement: US growth 13% YoY; early signs of revival but conservative outlook for the year
items.quote: Right now for us as you are rightly saying there are early signs of revival of our banking the large because the large banks is one of our target customer portfolio. We see some hope, but we have not seen a big momentum shift right now out there.

items.statement: Annuity revenue 60% of annual revenue (ATS, AMC, SaaS, support); license 18-20%, implementation 21-22%
items.quote: We have about 60% of revenue coming in from the annuity streams. We have three annuity streams which is the ATS, AMC, the SaaS revenue and the support revenues together they comprise 60% of our revenues on an annual basis.

items.statement: 13 new logos added in Q1 FY25; key deals in Indonesia, Malaysia, US, Qatar, India
items.quote: We had good additions in our client portfolio and added 13 new logos in Q1.

items.statement: R&D expensed fully in P&L; no capitalization of development costs
items.quote: We expense off always in P&L. We don't capitalize any expenses.

items.statement: Seasonality reducing slowly; Q1 historically 17-21% of annual revenue, shifted 3-4% over 3 years
items.quote: I think we have moved from the Q1 generally falls between roughly around 17% to 21% of our annual revenue for the same year. And from 17% to 20%, 21%, we have moved over the last 3 years.

items.statement: Average deal size grew 20-25% last year; Q1 too small to judge trend
items.quote: So I think our average deal sizes last year has substantially grown I think, from -- around 20%, 25% because our number of deals were at the same level, but the average deal size has grown substantially.

items.statement: EMEA 25% YoY, India 20% YoY, APAC 65% YoY, US 13% YoY in Q1 FY25
items.quote: There was good business growth across regions with EMEA region growing at 25% Y-o-Y. India at 20% Y-o-Y. APAC has come back on the growth path with 65% AOI in the quarter and U.S. region was at 13% growth.

items.statement: Revenue growth target 20-25% YoY; sustained for last 8-9 quarters
items.quote: I think it is in trend, it's in line with where we have been going for the last 8, 9 quarters and we have been growing in the range of 24% to 30% in last 8, 9 quarters.

items.statement: LumYn GenAI hyper-personalization platform launched; early POCs with 2-3 global customers
items.quote: We have launched a product for almost a couple of months back and it's an early stage of adoption. We are doing at least proof of concept with at least 2, 3 customers globally.

items.statement: Cash and investments INR 850 crores as of 30 June 2024
items.quote: INR850 crores with cash bank and investments put together.

items.statement: ESOP dilution ~2-3% over last 3 years; no incremental P&L impact expected
items.quote: I think in the last 3 years, we have got roughly around 2% and 1% permission from the Board to add to the ESOP scheme.

items.statement: Partner revenue ~20% of total, stable; 80% direct sales
items.quote: So generally, I think it remains static on an annual basis, at around 20% of revenues, which is partner-related and 80% is still direct.

items.statement: Existing customers contribute 80-85% of annual revenue; new logos max 15-20% of yearly revenue
items.quote: So Vinay, generally at the annual basis the existing customers contribute roughly around 80% to 85% of our business.

items.statement: Hired ~500 campus employees since January 2024; lateral hiring ongoing
items.quote: I think we have hired roughly around 500 campus people since January to until now.

items.statement: Mid-term guidance: top line CAGR 17-18%, operating EBITDA margin 27-28%, PAT margin 12.5-13% by FY26
items.quote: We expect to achieve a top line CAGR of around 17% to 18% and an operating EBITDA margin of approximately 27% to 28%, and a PAT margin of about 12.5% to 13% by FY '26.

items.statement: FY25 revenue expected Rs 690-700 crore; FY26 revenue expected around Rs 850 crore
items.quote: Our revenue for FY '25 is expected to be somewhere around Rs. 690 crores to Rs. 700 crores. And in FY '26 it's around approximately Rs. 850 crores.

items.statement: Second solar project at Jamshedpur ~6 MW, capex ~Rs 30 crore funded 75% debt, 25% internal accruals
items.quote: We are launching a second solar energy project in Jamshedpur with an approximate capacity of 6 megawatts. The capital expenditure for the project would be about Rs. 30 crores funded 75% by debt and 25% by internal accruals.

items.statement: No oversupply risk foreseen for at least two years; steel demand to grow with economy
items.quote: No, I mean, at least you can see two years down, I can't even see that much. But I don’t foresee a oversupply situation. I think we are a growing economy; steel plays a very large part in that. And as the economy continues to grow, uses of steel, fabrication, structural will continue to grow

items.statement: No formal order book; operate dedicated capacity under long-term contracts (3-5 years); practical utilization assumed ~70%
items.quote: We do not have specific order books per say, we have long term contracts for the entire capacity that we operate for the customers. And so, in some way if my tubes capacity is 530,000 tons, that's the expected order load. But like I said, let us say 70% of that to be practical.

items.statement: Contract renewals with Tata Steel extended: tubes to Aug 2024, CRM to Sep 2024, TMT to Nov 2025; negotiations ongoing
items.quote: We have already extended a number of times the current tubes contract has been extended up to August, and the CRM contract is up to September. The TMT contract is up to November 25.

items.statement: Net debt Rs 117 crore (Jun'24) vs Rs 221 crore (Jun'23); net debt/equity 0.17, net debt/EBITDA 0.69; cash conversion cycle improved to 53 days from 130 days
items.quote: Net debt remains at a stable level and stood at Rs. 117 crores in June '24 as compared to Rs. 221 crores in June '23. Net debt by equity stood at 0.17 and net debt by operating EBITDA stood at 0.69 in June 24. We have seen a steady improvement in our cash conversion cycle from 130 days in June '23 to 53 days in June '24.

items.statement: TMT utilization already at ~82% target for FY26; expect to sustain for FY25 barring customer supply changes
items.quote: Based on our assumptions, we expect the numbers to hold for the rest of the year. However, should there be any material change on the customer side in terms of steady supply, we will keep you guys updated in the following quarters. But as things stand now, I think it is a very safe assumption to meet the numbers for the full year.

items.statement: Bansal Super brand growth continues independent of Tata negotiations; focus on cash-positive sales and distribution network
items.quote: No, Bansal Super has nothing to do with negotiations with TATA Steel. As we mentioned in the past, we will continue to nurture and grow this vertical of our business because it's a very slow and steady and a long process to build a brand and a distribution network.

items.statement: Aggregate demand environment shows little change; OEMs split between those with strong balance sheets investing through transition and those balancing investments with short-term needs
items.quote: At an aggregate level, we're not really seeing any drop in demand. What we have seen over the last couple of years is that there are specific customer related issues that are impacting the quantum of investment and the speed of investment.

items.statement: Three large deals won in Q1: battery pack design for global EV battery manufacturer, turnkey cab development for North American commercial vehicle OEM, and first/business class seat development for European Aerospace Tier 1
items.quote: Q1 was also a solid quarter in terms of deal signings, with 3 large deals won during April, May and June.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margin at 18.2% in Q1 vs 18.4% previous quarter; net profit increased 3.1% sequentially; aim for 20%+ EBITDA margin long term
items.quote: Despite the decline in revenue in Q1, our margin performance remained resilient with operating EBITDA coming in at 18.2% in Q1 compared with 18.4% in the previous quarter. Moreover, net profit increased by 3.1% sequentially.

items.statement: Confident in sequential growth from Q2 onwards; expect consistent quarter-on-quarter growth through fiscal year; no specific revenue guidance provided
items.quote: We are confident in the quarter-on-quarter growth that should see the business at the end of the year being much improved in terms of volumes from where we are today.

items.statement: BMW joint venture expected to launch in second half of fiscal year; regulatory approvals and team confirmation underway; business plan execution on track
items.quote: We expect the joint venture to be launched in the second half of this fiscal year. I announced in April that we have to go through regulatory approval. We have to confirm the seed team and confirm the leadership team that will run that organization.

items.statement: Headcount reduced 1.4% to 12,505; utilization improved 50 bps to 86.5%; focus on pyramid optimization with campus hires and strategic hiring in growth areas
items.quote: The total headcount stood at about 12,505 at the end of the quarter, a reduction of about 1.4%, reflecting about 183 employees compared with the previous quarter and this reflects an optimization of our capacity between full-time employees and the outsourced resources.

items.statement: Last 12-month attrition down to 13.7% from 14.5% in Q4; annualized attrition at 12.8%; expect further reduction in coming quarter
items.quote: Trends on attrition levels continue to remain favorable as we saw our last 12-month attrition coming down again this quarter to 13.7% compared with 14.5%, which it stood in Q4.

items.statement: DSO at 84 days vs 83 days previous quarter; billed DSO 58 days, unbilled DSO 26 days; free cash flow INR 220 crores; net working capital release of INR 70 crores
items.quote: We've maintained robust collection efficiency with a total DSO of 84 days compared with 83 days of the previous quarter and 96 days in the same quarter of last year, and billed DSO came in at 58 days, while unbilled DSO stood at 26 days at the end of Q1.

items.statement: Remain debt-free; net cash $131.4 million vs $146.3 million previous quarter after $49 million dividend payout in June
items.quote: At the end of first quarter, we continue to remain debt free and the net cash on our balance sheet stood at a healthy $131.4 million compared with $146.3 million at the end of the previous quarter. This balance is after a dividend payout of $49 million that we did during the month of June.

items.statement: Services revenue down 1% sequentially due to VinFast ramp-down and project phasing; Technology Solutions down 7.4% due to product seasonality; education vertical grew 4% sequentially
items.quote: In Services, we also recorded a sequential revenue decline of 1% on account of the short-term phasing of a number of large programs and the completion of our ramp down at VinFast.

items.statement: Anchor customers Tata Motors and JLR showing strong results informing capex confidence; BMW JV building presence in Germany; Airbus relationship growing with new seat manufacturer deal
items.quote: We are engaged obviously with our anchor customers, Tata Motors and JLR. They have had a very good set of results themselves in the recent past and that's informing their confidence in terms of capex and investment in new products.

items.statement: Offshore revenue mix improved 130 bps sequentially to 39%; services ex-VinFast grew ~26% year-on-year and ~1% sequentially
items.quote: Regarding our mix of on-site and offshore revenues, revenues generated from outside our delivery centers in India and Romania and executed offshore improved by 130 basis points sequentially, reaching 39%.

items.statement: EV adoption not following smooth curve but IEA projects 17M units in 2024 and 50% of global car sales by 2035; North America volatility from potential legislation changes; aerospace highly regulated requiring capability demonstration
items.quote: We believe that most technology transitions, including EVs, do not follow a smooth adoption curve. Despite growth rates tapering in 2024, the International Energy Agency continues to assert that global EV sales are likely to increase to somewhere close to 17 million units this year.

items.statement: Operating expenses down 2.2% QoQ; employee benefits flat; other expenses up 11.5% from professional fees, CSR, travel; outsourcing charges down 12.4% from subcontracting optimization
items.quote: We continue to exercise strong operating discipline during the quarter with the operating expenses reducing by 2.2%, thereby enabling us to maintain a relatively stable EBITDA margin that came in at 18.2% compared with 18.4% of the previous quarter.

items.statement: Commercial vehicle sector accelerating software-defined vehicle investments; expanding beyond passenger vehicles into off-highway and truck sectors with middleware and full vehicle capabilities
items.quote: Notably, we are now starting to witness the accelerated adoption of software-defined capabilities within the commercial and off-highway vehicle space. This growing demand should help us extend our ambitions beyond our traditional focus upon passenger vehicles.

items.statement: BMW JV requires regulatory approval before launch in H2 FY25; aerospace engagements require process and capability compliance demonstration before larger projects
items.quote: I announced in April that we have to go through regulatory approval. We have to confirm the seed team and confirm the leadership team that will run that organization.

items.statement: Targets 4%+ PAT margin and 6-7% EBITDA margin for FY25
items.quote: So, somewhere around like we are looking the 4% plus PAT margin, we are looking. And the EBITDA margin is around like 6% to 7%.

items.statement: Plans to open 3 new stores in FY25, targeting 20 stores by FY28
items.quote: We plan to open three new stores in FY '25, aiming to increase the total number of stores from eight in FY '24 to 20 by FY '28.

items.statement: Targets diamond studded jewellery revenue share increase from 6% to 15%
items.quote: Our target is to increase the revenue share from diamond studded jewellery from 6% to 15%.

items.statement: Capex of Rs 6-8 crore for three new stores in FY25 plus Rs 100 crore inventory
items.value: Rs 6-8 cr capex, Rs 100 cr inventory
items.quote: CAPEX, we require somewhere around Rs. 6 crores to Rs. 8 crores to build a new showroom, because we are coming up with three new stores in FY '25. And for inventory, we require somewhere around Rs. 100 crores.

items.statement: New stores in Neemuch, Ajmer and Ratlam flagship (8,000-10,000 sq ft) to open in FY25
items.quote: Similarly, we are going to open new stores in Neemuch, Madhya Pradesh and Ajmer, Rajasthan in this financial year which are estimated to start in the next two to three months. Our Ratlam store, which is our hope town from where we have started our journey, that store also needs renovation as per the changing time, so we are also coming up with a new and improved flagship store and Ratlam, and we w

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin 8% on Rs 504 crore revenue, PAT up 60% to Rs 25 crore
items.quote: Despite elevated gold price and weak industry demand, our consolidated revenue impressively grew by 7% year-over-year to Rs. 504 crores. Our EBITDA soared by 51% to Rs. 38 crores with a strong margin of 8% during Q1 FY '25. Our profit after tax surged to Rs. 25 crores, reflecting a remarkable growth of 60%.

items.statement: Expects to maintain EBITDA margin 6-8% for full year FY25
items.quote: But this EBITDA 8%, we will be able to maintain it around 6% to 8% somewhere.

items.statement: Making charges 9-10% for gold jewellery, 15-17% for diamond studded
items.quote: And average making charges for our pure gold jewellery is like 9% to 10%, and for the diamond studded, it is like 15% to 17%.

items.statement: Diamond studded share 6% of sales, targeting 10-15% in 3-4 years
items.quote: So, right now and before, our studded ratio is 6% and now we are like planning to achieve like between 10% to 15% of the studded ratio, the gold versus studded reserve ratio.

items.statement: Wedding jewellery 52% of sales, implementing shop-in-shop model across stores
items.quote: Like out of total sales, 52% is the wedding jewellery sales. So, technically every 5 out of 10 customer comes in for the wedding jewellery. So, in Indore we have implemented one shop-in-shop model where which is an exclusive outlet for the wedding customers, where there is a different hospitality, different field, different D. P. Abhushan Limited July 19, 2024 designs, enhanced designs. So, in all

items.statement: Q1 demand weak due to elections and fewer wedding dates (25-27 vs normal 45-60), expects recovery from Q3
items.quote: this quarter, there are multiple reasons, because election is going on and due to the limited wedding dates, that’s why the season was little low in the 1st Quarter. I think in a normal case, they are like 45 days to 60 days where the marriage dates, but in this quarter there is like 25 to 27 dates are available thoroughly. Vikrant Kashyap: Okay. So, how do you see quarter two onwards? Vikas Katar

items.statement: Old gold exchange 20-25% of procurement, monthly saving schemes 3-5% of sales
items.quote: So, our old gold exchange program is like somewhere around 20% to 25% we are like procuring from the old gold. And the monthly saving scheme is somewhere around 3% to 5%, the total entire sale.

items.statement: Follows natural hedging - buys gold same day as sales, no MCX hedging
items.quote: So, we maintain the natural hedging policy. So, we do not hedge anything on MCX or like that. We maintain a natural hedging policy, like whatever gold we sell on the particular day, we buy it on the same day at the same price.

items.statement: Weighted average inventory cost below market due to legacy stock (Rs 100 to Rs 70,000 per 10g)
items.quote: And how it has impacted our margin is like because we are following the weighted average cost of method, and we have been in this business since 1940. So, in our inventory there is a gold which is like Rs. 100 per 10 grams ranging from Rs. 70,000 per 10 grams. So, our weighted average cost is always lesser than the current market price.

items.statement: Focus on Tier-2/3 cities with less competition and high purchasing power; metro entry after 2 years
items.quote: So, Maharashtra and Mumbai we have in our plan, but after like two years maybe we are focusing on Mumbai and big metro cities. Because right now we think there is a lot of scope in the Tier-2, Tier-3 cities where the competition is less, but the purchasing power is very high. So, we are more focusing on particular those areas first.

items.statement: Gold price spikes cause customer pullback; volumes recover when prices stabilize
items.quote: Because there was a sudden spike in the gold prices, so that's why we have seen in the recent past trend that whenever there is a sudden spike in the gold prices, the customer takes a back foot. And once the gold prices get stabilized, the sales gets on increasing.

items.statement: Domestic demand recovering driven by favorable monsoon and kharif sowing up ~10% YoY; export demand soft with oversupply from China keeping prices depressed
items.quote: In domestic markets, there is a positive sentiment primarily driven by monsoon prediction of IMD. There was a deficient rainfall till June '24 , that did impact first quarter in fiscal year '25 sales. But of late, monsoon has started really picking up well and the kharif sowing is registering significant growth of about 10% as compared to last year.

items.statement: Key crop acreages up significantly: Paddy +21%, Soyabean +30%, Maize +34%, Pigeon pea +191% YoY; cotton acreages down significantly in North due to pink bollworm
items.quote: If you look at key crops, Paddy is about 21% up, Soyabean about 30%, Maize 34% and pigeon pea about 191%. This is one crop that has seen a significant increase in acres driven by commodity prices. From field reports, what we are hearing, cotton acreages have reduced significantly in northern part of India, there's one particular pest called pink bollworm that has been bothering the farmers.

items.statement: Near-term outlook challenging for international business for next three months; domestic business positive with good rains and commodity prices; confident on medium-to-long-term growth
items.quote: In conclusion, I think near -term outlook for the business particularly international remains challenging at least for the next three months; however domestic business with the rain and the commodity prices being good is looking positive, we are very confident and optimistic about the overall growth prospect in the medium- to-long- term.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA Rs.96 crore (-13% YoY), gross contribution margin 30%, PAT Rs.48 crore vs Rs.63 crore YoY; margin compression from adverse mix (seeds down) and lower domestic/international margins vs history
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at Rs.96 crore; it is lower by about 13% compared to the same quarter last year with a gross contribution margin of 30% and PAT for the quarter stood at Rs.48 crore compared to the Rs.63crore reported during Q1 of fiscal year '24.

items.statement: International business not making negative margin; spreads compressed, margins lower than historical; Q1 EBITDA drop Rs.14 crore YoY, Rs.4 crore from seeds, Rs.10 crore from crop care largely international gross contribution drop
items.quote: See, gross margin has come down not because of international business making any negative margin. So, we did not make negative margin in the international business. We have mentioned in the earlier calls that we were taking swift actions in terms of liquidating old inventory. Overall, spreads has indeed compressed and hence the margins are lower than what we have made historically, but we have not

items.statement: Domestic price decline upwards of 10% YoY (14% in Q1); volume growth 13% led by herbicides and new launches; price declines in undifferentiated portfolio where brand share weak
items.quote: In domestic business, price decline was upwards of 10% and this is YoY decline, the QoQ decline has come down, but obviously because Q1 was on a higher price last year; it's 14%.

items.statement: International revenue Rs.133 crore (-5% YoY) with volume growth ~19% but price challenges impacting revenue; Acephate, Hexaconazole, Pendimethalin, Metribuzin prices muted, Metribuzin ~half of two years ago
items.quote: Coming back to International business, Revenues stood at Rs.133 crore, which is lower by 5% compared to the similar period last year, though we had a decent volume growth of about 19%, but the price challenge s are really impacting overall growth from a revenue perspective.

items.statement: Capex envisaged in range of Rs.100 crore for the year; commissioned Water-Soluble Fertiliser Plant during the year; integrated R&D facility in Bangalore expected ready in two years
items.quote: We are also very prudent in CAPEX investment and envisage our expense would be in the range of Rs.100 crore.

items.statement: Seed supply constraints in hybrid maize and hybrid paddy (significant revenue contributors); North cotton hybrid Diggaz good volume growth despite lower acreage; South/West cotton liquidation to be watched
items.quote: So, if you see our business, the two areas where we had supply challenges primarily were hybrid maize as well as hybrid paddy. Subhra Gourisaria: So, North cotton actually we said we had very good momentum. South and West cotton we will have to yet see how the liquidation progresses, but it's not a big part of our portfolio. So, paddy and maize were the bigger dip for us

items.statement: Improving front-end capabilities on customer centricity theme; building connected organization leveraging digital for scale and closer customer access; 'Anubandh' program for channel visibility beyond distributor to retailer; expanding reta
items.quote: We are improving our front-end capabilities based on the theme of customer centricity . And as we work more on this, you will start hearing more about this as we move forward. Our endeavor will be to build a more connected organization leveraging digital. I think digital will give us a scale and that's where we will get closer to the customer.

items.statement: Healthy cash balance as of 30th June with no external borrowings
items.quote: We do have a very healthy cash balance as of 30th June as well, and with no external borrowings.

items.statement: Leadership changes underway to bring fresh thinking; rightsizing organization; investing in people as key pillar alongside R&D
items.quote: And the last but not the least is investment in people. I think we are moving; we are looking at some significant leadership changes wherever required to bring some fresh thinking and also looking at not only from the perspective of rightsizing the organization.

items.statement: Innovation Turnover Index (ITI) ambition to move to high teens; uptick seen in Q1; last 4 years contribution vs overall portfolio
items.quote: ITI is difficult to say because it's last four years contribution of it versus the overall portfolio and we do expect the overall portfolio to grow as well. Having said that, our ambition is certainly as we said earlier as well, that ITI should start moving to the high teens and which is where we are seeing an uptick happening in 1st Quarter as well.

items.statement: International pricing volatile, no visibility 10-11 months out; Acephate faces regulatory review risk; China oversupply continues capping prices; domestic technical prices creeping up MoM/QoQ may compress margins where brand strength weak
items.quote: What we see is, if you start splitting our business in segments, as I said, domestic formulation demand is looking good for the various factors I mentioned. Seed, the majority of our season is over. P rimarily the bulk of the business happens in kharif, and the only adjustment would be related to how much return comes versus what we have estimated. So, that adjustment you will see probably in the

items.statement: Strategy shifting to make-vs-buy decisions; partnerships and collaborations with global and domestic companies key for portfolio refresh; 'Mark Plus' 9(3) product launched in collaboration with a major; not pursuing everything in-house
items.quote: I think we are moving to a mindset to say we have to make a smart decision , make versus buy, in a world where so many supply chain and product partnerships are available. We have to be very prudent in making a decision. So, whatever is financially better, that's a decision we should make a nd obviously there's a point on supply chain certainty. So, our decisions are more going to be based on make

items.statement: Export pricing pressure: Metribuzin prices ~half of two years ago; Acephate, Hexaconazole, Pendimethalin prices muted; Baltic Dry Index doubled YoY increasing sea freight; domestic pricing product-specific, most products down YoY
items.quote: We have some old products like Acephate, Hexaconazole and Pendimethalin where prices continue to remain muted. Metri buzine prices actually are almost at the level of half compared to what they were two years ago. On top of that, sea freight has also seen steep hike as the Baltic Dry Index has doubled over last year, impacting margins.

items.statement: Export recovery soft in key markets (Brazil, US, SEA); volumes picking up but prices depressed due to China oversupply; Northern Hemisphere season may balance inventory; sequential price drops stabilized
items.quote: On the export front, recovery remains soft with the key markets like Brazil, US, SEA. So, while volumes have started picking up, prices continue to depress due to oversupply from China. We think with the ongoing season in the Northern Hemisphere including US, should lead to some balancing of the inventory and hopefully things will move start looking positively from there.

items.statement: Digital investments across 5-6 initiatives: SAP S/4 HANA ERP changeover, 'Drishti' AI/ML tool for farmer advisories, 'Anubandh' channel visibility, 'Seed-Say' AI/ML forecasting, customer-connect, manufacturing automation evaluation; digital
items.quote: So, if you look at all our digital spend actually you can categorize into five categories. One is obviously the back end is very, very important, which is SAP S4 HANA where we are going through complete changeover of our ERP system. That obviously takes time and money. On our other efficiency related, we are building a tool called “Drishti” and I think it has been talked about in the past and that

items.statement: Capex for FY25 expected around INR 800-900 crores on cash basis
items.quote: I would say on a cash basis, it could be INR800 crores, or it could be INR900 crores, depends upon how we ultimately end up sort of spending on the same.

items.statement: FY26 and FY27 capex expected INR 1,000-1,100 crores including new cable capacity announcement
items.quote: Yes, and if we include about INR300 crores what we announced, INR1,000 crores to INR1,100 crores will be the overall capex if you include that.

items.statement: Lloyd capex around INR 100 crores out of total FY25 capex
items.quote: Out of which, Lloyd is lower because most of the capacity is there and only about INR100 crores are for Lloyd.

items.statement: Switchgear contribution margins historically range 38%-41%, EBIT margins 24%-30%
items.quote: We believe that the long-term range, which one should assume for this business is between 38% to sort of 41%. And I think that's something we believe is something we'll continue to maintain.

items.statement: Lloyd EBIT margin 3.5% in Q1 FY25, driven by premiumization, cost efficiencies, operating leverage
items.quote: Now having said that, whatever things that you mentioned, it's not pricing action, but it is premiumization over a long period of time, ability for trade to accept a certain price level and the consumer to give a certain price level to a brand.

items.statement: Price hikes taken across product categories in Q1 FY25 due to commodity inflation
items.quote: So as far as price increases are concerned, most of that has been done in many product categories, including Consumer Durables in the first quarter.

items.statement: Consumer demand improvement seen but uncertain if sustained; ECD growth aided by summer and low base
items.quote: Whether we are seeing a sustained improvement in consumer demand, I would still say I hope it continues, but we are not very sure whether this is just a one-off.

items.statement: Cables & Wires channel destocking in June due to commodity price decline; July returning to normal
items.quote: We are seeing July to be coming back to normal levels.

items.statement: Crabtree brand merged into Havells Crabtree; Standard, REO, Lloyd to remain independent brands
items.quote: So all switching solutions from the Havells brand are now termed as Havells Crabtree. And Crabtree because of the legacy brand of the switches, so we'll continue with that brand for all switching solutions from us.

items.statement: Export approvals for Lloyd HVAC and Cables in US expected in 9-12 months
items.quote: I think we should set our target around 12 months from now. So that's what we are looking at. So that's where we're in the journey for the HVAC.

items.statement: Cables & Wires capacity expansion for domestic, export, underground cables over next 1-1.5 years
items.quote: For the next 1-1.5 years, we'll see more capacity expansion in Cables & Wires.

items.statement: A&P spend: Lloyd 4%-4.5%, Havells 2.5%, consolidated 3%-3.5% of sales
items.quote: Overall, I think generally, Lloyd is between 4% and 4.5% and Havells is about 2.5%. So overall, it's about 3% to 3.5%.

items.statement: Inventory at 63 days; scope for improvement but seasonality and unpredictability require buffer
items.quote: I would say yes there is scope for improvement in the same. And I think we should see some better sort of ratios in that going forward.

items.statement: Tumkur cable facility awaiting final approvals; sales to start within Q2 FY25
items.quote: We are just awaiting the final approvals for our sales to start happening from the new facility in Tumkur. So it should start within this quarter.

items.statement: Aspiration for international business to reach ~10% of revenue over time, no medium-term targets
items.quote: Over a period time, may be around 10% of our business should come from international. But that's an aspiration. I mean we are not holding out any medium-term targets for that.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA was 15.2% in Q1 FY25, down 80 bps QoQ due to one-time hits including US project ramp delays and Middle East PDD provisions.
items.quote: Our operating EBITDA was a disappointment. We had some onetime hits which we'll talk about in the subsequent discussion. But there were a couple of provisions that we had to make, and it was at 15.2%.

items.statement: Management aims to bring operating EBITDA margin back to 16.5%-17% range in H2 FY25 and exit the year at that level.
items.quote: we definitely want to operate closer to that 16.5%, 17% type of margin in the second half of the year.

items.statement: 12-month order book backlog was flat QoQ but increased 23% YoY; Q1 is typically slower for order book but pipeline momentum is strong.
items.quote: Our 12 months order book backlog, while it was flat quarter -on-quarter, increased 23% year-on-year. Q1 is typically a slower start to the order book, but we see some really good deal momentum in pipeline building and confident about the deals in the future quarters.

items.statement: US Healthcare momentum powered by Oracle Cloud has kicked into high gear with providers, senior living facilities, and regional health plans.
items.quote: U.S., in particular, the Healthcare momentum powered by Oracle Cloud, has really kicked into high gear and we see continued momentum there with providers, with senior living facilities as well as with regional health plan.

items.statement: UK government business sees improved clarity post-election; early signs of deal restarts in revenue & customs and NHS programs rejuvenating.
items.quote: We're seeing early signs already on, for example, in the revenue and customs department, there were a couple of deals that were paused 6 months back. We were hopeful 6 months back on some of the deals that got paused as a result of election period, and now they are coming back up, in terms of the process.

items.statement: Consciously reduced AMEA accounts from 250 to 175 over last 2 quarters while growing top line, focusing on deeper account mining and larger $1M-$5M accounts.
items.quote: by conscious design, we've continued to reduce the number of accounts, particularly in our AMEA geography from 250 accounts to 175 accounts over the last 2 quarters while of course, growing top line.

items.statement: US business mix shifting from project-heavy to more managed services; expects comfortable mix by end of FY25.
items.quote: I would say in the next one or two quarters we'll reach by the end of this fiscal year a good mix a comfortable mix.

items.statement: Depreciation & amortization in Q1 reflects regular run-rate after one-time useful life alignment for acquired intangibles; incremental increase expected with future capex.
items.quote: So what you see in depreciation is more the regular one and you will see the incremental increase as and when we make the capex, but broadly what you see in the current quarter is the range you should look for.

items.statement: Macroeconomic uncertainties and deal delays persist; customers remain cautious on cost preservation with high scrutiny on deal approvals.
items.quote: As we look ahead, there are continued macroeconomic uncertainties and deal delays, which we see in the market. So customers are still cautious when it comes to cost preservation as well as high scrutiny on some of the deals and the approvals.

items.statement: UK defense deal ramp-up paused for 2 months due to election; restarting in August with incremental H2 FY25 revenue impact, scaling over next 2 years.
items.quote: the ramp-up on that was definitely paused in the last 2 months. And now we are seeing that is starting to open up. So we see the defense and the ramp- up from the wins that we had there, starting in August r amp-up, the actual impact in FY '25 is not going to be that significant, but there will definitely be some incremental impact in H2 in terms of revenue and it will start to pick up even more i

items.statement: No fund raise development; replied to exchange regarding market rumors, will inform investors proactively if anything materializes.
items.quote: There's no development as such. But if anything comes, we will be proactive and be coming and informing to the investors.

items.statement: No specific numeric guidance provided; confident Q1 top-line momentum (4.3% QoQ, 12.1% YoY) can be sustained in remaining quarters.
items.quote: we feel that the healthy kind of top line revenue momentum will continue. We have some good growth in the pipeline that has happened in the last few quarters, and we believe that, conversion to order book and then, of course, conversion to revenue.

items.statement: No pricing pressure in US; winning high-quality digital/cloud deals at right price and margin, not bidding on price-sensitive deals.
items.quote: We are not seeing any margin pressure. It continues to be healthy, and we are not bidding for deals which are more of where you lose the pricing. We are bidding for the deals which are high -quality digital and cloud deals, and we are getting right price and right margin in those areas.

items.statement: Launched iConniX GenAI portfolio with partnerships across NVIDIA, Microsoft (InfoGENius), Oracle (TalentGenius); targeting industry-specific use cases in manufacturing, fraud analytics, benefit verification.
items.quote: We're very excited about our umbrella brand called iConniX, which is what we launched and announced a few weeks back. iConniX is our GenAI portfolio of offerings.

items.statement: Project Nucleus internal transformation targeting order-to-cash lifecycle automation and efficiency gains; AI Amigo platform automating finance, marketing, HR functions.
items.quote: We also have kicked off an internal transformation, which we're calling Project Nucleus. And this is looking at the entire order-to-cash life cycle, some of which we had been doing some groundwork, but this is important to further streamline processes, automate certain inefficiencies and then hopefully, we can generate enough savings to repurpose in future investment areas, but also help with impr

items.statement: US business at ~$100M annual run rate with 35+ Fortune 1000 clients; expects US margins to reach double-digits in coming quarters and approach company level (15% range) by FY26.
items.quote: But in FY '26 and beyond ; we'll always prioritize growth in the U.S. market because I think the opportunity untapped is still pretty high. But our margin profile needs to be a lot more closer to the company level. It might be a couple of percentage points lower, let's say in the 15% of the range.

items.statement: Management expects 20-30% capacity utilization in first year of new facility
items.quote: 40%, 50% utilization in the first year may not happen. My guess would be around 20% to 30%.

items.statement: Planned capex of INR70-100 crores for FY25 excluding Sahasra project
items.quote: We have planned a capex of INR70 crores to INR100 crores for the financial year 2025, out of which a portion will be utilized in setting up one more EMI/EMC testing chamber in our new facility.

items.statement: Sahasra project incurred INR50 crores last year, may incur INR10-20 crores in current year
items.value: 10 crores, INR15 crores or close to INR20 crores

items.statement: Majority of operating capex allocated to pharma, 10-15% to food, rest to electronics
items.quote: Majority goes into pharma and food, probably 20% or 10% to 15% goes into food, but for that majority goes into pharma.

items.statement: Gross margins expected to be maintained despite new facility ramp-up
items.quote: We can expect our existing margins to continue going forward as well.

items.statement: Food segment faring better than last year with no export/import headwinds; government increasing surveillance
items.quote: Compared to last year, the Food segment, I think, is faring much better. Last year, we were impacted by the export/import scenario of the count ry, so compared to that there are no headwinds to food industry as of now

items.statement: Electronics testing industry vibrant with Make in India push; EMI/EMC chamber at 80%+ utilization
items.quote: The current EMI/EMC chamber is occupied at 80% or sometimes even more every day.

items.statement: Re-strategized portfolio focusing on pharma, food, electronics; defocusing diagnostics and environmental services
items.quote: The company re-strategized its services portfolio, providing greater impetus for driving growth in food, pharma, and electronics testing, while opt imizing our other industry services based on their

items.statement: Food and pharma together ~85% of revenue; remaining 15% from other segments
items.quote: Food and pharma put together is about 85%. The rest is in the remaining 15%.

items.statement: Revenue impact from equipment shifting to new facility; teams working to minimize impact
items.quote: We are trying to do it efficiently. Obviously, ther e will be some impact, but teams are working very hard to bring down the impact

items.statement: Successful US FDA remote audit with no observations for clinical research studies
