items.statement: Offshore ratio improved to 58.9% from Q4; aspiration to reach 60%
items.quote: The Onsite:Offshore mix improved mo ved slightly towards offshore compared to Q4 . Offshore percentage now stands at 58.9%. Our aspiration is to improve the offshore ratio to 60%.

items.statement: AI revenue generation: 2 significant empanelment deals won (Middle East oil, European auto) with ramp-up interest; pipeline significantly higher than two quarters ago
items.quote: AI has finally become a revenue generator – we have won 2 significant empanelment deals, one with the Middle Eastern oil customer and a second with an auto major in Europe and both are showing a lot of interest in ramping up with us. We are also seeing increased interest and traction in this area and the pipeline is significantly higher than two quarters ago last quarter in this area.

items.statement: Monitoring China curbs risk; no revenue impact expected from elections or China situation
items.quote: So, at this stage we are closely monitoring the situation. But I, to my mind, don't think there will be a revenue impact from the elections or plus/minus from China.

items.statement: Cash and investments ₹2,784 cr vs ₹2,883 cr end Q4
items.quote: Our Cash and Investments stood at ₹ 2,784 crores at the end of Q1, vs ₹ 2,883 crores end of Q4.

items.statement: Investor and Analyst Day planned for August 27 in Bangalore
items.quote: Before I end, I would like to announce that we plan to host an Investor and Analyst Day on August 27th in Bangalore. We will be providing additional details in the coming days.

items.statement: Acquired 2.34 lakh customers in Q1 FY25, 116% YoY growth; total customer base reached 44.7 lakhs
items.quote: In Q1 FY'25, we also acquired 2.34 lakh customers, reflecting a 116% growth y-on -y and our total customer base has reached to 44.7 lakhs.

items.statement: ADTO grew to INR 3.67 trillion, up 27% YoY
items.quote: During the quarter, our ADTO, which stands for Average -Daily-Turn-Over, grew to 3.67 trillion a growth of 27% YoY

items.statement: Client funding book stood at INR 271 crore, up 20% YoY
items.quote: our client funding book stood at INR 271 crore, a growth of 20% y -on-y

items.statement: Mutual fund AUM reached INR 1,124 crore, up 90% YoY
items.quote: our mutual fund AUM reached INR 1,124 crore, a 90% growth YoY.

items.statement: Achieved lifetime highest PAT of INR 20.1 crore, up 248% QoQ and 39% YoY; PAT margin 20%
items.quote: we have achieved our lifetime highest ever PAT of INR 20.1 crore, which is a growth of 248% QoQ and 39% YoY, along with PAT margins of 20%.

items.statement: Employee benefit expense INR 13.6 crore includes annual increments, RSU/ESOP cost, and variable incentives; one-time positive impact of INR 8.66 crore from unvested ESOP/RSU reversal
items.quote: Our employee benefit expense of INR 13.6 crore includes the impact of annual increment of employees, RSU ESOP of cost and proportionate of annual variable performances incentives. In this quarter, this also includes a one time positive impact of INR 8.66 Crore with respect to unvested ESOP and RSU costs as per Indian Accounting Standard 102.

items.statement: Broking revenue INR 40 crore (+11% YoY), allied income INR 29.7 crore (+27% YoY), total revenue INR 102 crore (+21% YoY)
items.quote: in Q 1 FY'25, our broking revenue has gone to INR 40 crore, a growth of 11% YoY. Allied income is INR 29.7 crore, a growth of 27% YoY and overall, our total revenue stood at INR 102 crore, which is a growth of 21% YoY.

items.statement: Revamped iOS and Android mobile apps to be live by end of Q2 FY25; Trade Station 2.0 web platform now accessible to all users
items.quote: We are happy to report that our revamped mobile app for both iOS and Android, which will be live and available to our users by end of Q2 FY'25. Trade Station 2.0, our revamped web platform previously in beta is now accessible to all users, offering enhanced user interface and a smoother experience for high end traders.

items.statement: Market share stands at 2%-2.5% for both cash and F&O segments; target is to reach 6% market share through quality acquisition
items.quote: Our market share stand between 2% - 2.5% for both, cash segment as well as F&O segment.

items.statement: Aiming for 6% market share; focus on quality acquisition, RPC, CAC metrics to grow ADTO market share
items.quote: We are continuing to work towards 6% market share and for that we understand that only the quality acquisition will work. We don't want to acquire customers just for the sake of the number. And we are really having the diversified strategy internally and the key metrics in terms of RPC, CAC, so that our ADTO market share will grow in future.

items.statement: Anticipated regulation may require INR 20 lakh minimum value for option selling and fewer expiries; could impact volumes but extent unknown
items.quote: Coming to the regulation side, which is anticipated that now there will be a INR 20 lakh minimum value required for option selling to enter into an option contract and there will be a few expiries. We feel that yes, it can impact our volumes but we need to see at what extent it is going to impact.

items.statement: Narayan Gangadhar remains part of IFL Group; major portion of ESOP/RSU reversal linked to his departure; CEO search is ongoing
items.quote: Mr. Narayan Gangadhar is still a part of IFL Group, and we have disclosed it in our exchange filing also. And, yes, the major portion in this quarter, reversal effect of RSU, is related to Mr. Narayan Gangadhar sir and some other employees also.

items.statement: CEO search is on; will update investors once finalized
items.quote: Second, regarding that, CEO, yes, the search is on and we will update the investors as soon as we get the clarification on that.

items.statement: No current plan to enter lending business; fully concentrating on broking business
items.quote: As of now, there is no plan to do any lending business, and that's our stand as of now.

items.statement: Reiterates 1.5x industry volume growth guidance for FY25 despite Jaypee insolvency
items.quote: We had earlier guided the street that we will deliver 1.5x of the industry growth and we reiterate our guidance. In spite of the recent development on Jaypee, we believe that we can deliver 1.5x of the industry growth in this financial year.

items.statement: Targets cost reduction of INR150-200 per ton over next three years from current footprint
items.quote: We have also identified levers for sustainable cost reduction, and we believe that we will be able to reduce our cost to the tune of INR150-INR200 per ton in the next three years.

items.statement: Expects FY25 depreciation in range of INR1,350-1,400 crores
items.quote: We expect FY25 depreciation to remain in the range of INR 1,350 crores to INR1,400 crores.

items.statement: Current capacity 46.6 mt; will reach 49.5 mt by end FY25; commissioned 1 mt each at Kadapa and Ariyalur; NE and Bihar expansion on track
items.quote: We are currently at 46.6 million tons, and we will reach 49.5 million tons by the end of Financial Year 25. We are on track to complete the North-East and Bihar expansion as per the earlier committed timelines.

items.statement: Sector demand grew 2-4% YoY in Q1 FY25 due to election quarter, heat waves, water shortages, floods; expects recovery post-monsoon
items.quote: In line with our expectations, Quarter 1 of FY25 being an election quarter, we saw a moderation in cement demand across all markets in the country. Some other factors such as heat waves, water shortages and floods in certain regions further added to the slowdown. Based on all these, we believe that the sector demand grew in the range of 2% to 4% on a Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Pan-India cement prices down 2-3% QoQ in Q1; June exit prices down another 3% vs Q1 average; expects prices soft until monsoon quarter, recovery from Q3
items.quote: On average, PAN India cement prices were softer by 2%-3% Q-o-Q, while exit prices in June were lower by another 3% compared to the Q1 average. I believe that the prices may remain soft until the monsoon quarter and thereafter price increase could happen from Q3 onwards this year.

items.statement: Company NSR declined only 0.3% QoQ in Q1 due to brand mix improvement, price positioning, discount rationalization vs sector decline of 2-3%
items.quote: On a Q-o-Q basis, while prices for the sector have declined in the range of 2%-3%, our NSR declined marginally by 0.3% in Q1 of FY25 because of our initiatives to improve brand mix, price positioning and rationalization of discounts.

items.statement: Current quarter prices ~3% lower vs previous quarter; no improvement expected in Q2; recovery hoped from Q3
items.quote: For the current quarter already we are seeing that the prices are lower by about 3% or so compared to the previous quarter a nd we don't expect these to improve in the current quarter. Hopefully from Q3 onwards we should start seeing the recovery in the prices

items.statement: Raw material cost INR729/ton (ex-Jaypee tolling), down 5% YoY from mining optimization and procurement efficiencies; deemed sustainable
items.quote: Excluding the cost of these purchases, raw material cost in Q1 FY25 was INR729 per ton of cement production, which is lower by 5% Y-o-Y. The reduction Dalmia Bharat Limited. July 19, 2024 in raw material cost has been contributed by our mining cost optimization and usage and procurement efficiencies, which we feel are

items.statement: Committed to selling IEX stake (short-term investment) to fund expansions; no timeline given
items.quote: We continue to maintain our stand that yes, it will be a short-term investment. And of course, exact timelines I cannot give but we'll be looking to sell this to meet our funds' requirement for the expansions.

items.statement: Inorganic growth remains part of strategy; will evaluate on strategic fit and financial hurdle rates; no specific targets disclosed
items.quote: No, I think we have always maintained it will be a mix of inorganic and organic. There are uncertainties in inorganic, so it is hard to commit what will happen, what will not happen. But there will be a mix of organic and inorganic as it has been in the

items.statement: Top 4 cement cos capacity share rose from 48% (FY23) to 55% in 15 months; consolidation accelerating; aspires to grow capacity/volume share faster than industry
items.quote: If you look at 2013, the capacity share of the top 4 cement companies was about 36%, which increased to 48% by the end of FY23. i.e. it took almost 10 years to increase this share by 12 percentage points. However, it has now increased to 55% in a period of just 15 months, demonstrating that the consolidation is accelerating. Against this backdrop, we aspire to increase our capacity and volume shar

items.statement: Brand ambassador marketing spend now part of regular other expenses; committed to strong brand building
items.quote: It is part of the other expenses, and we are committed to keep our brand building efforts strong. And you'll see the results in the sales also. And that is already part of the cost structure, which is already reflected in the first quarter results.

name: Sterling and Wilson Renewable Energy Ltd

items.statement: Order inflow guidance of INR 8,000 crores for FY25
items.quote: With the order wins announced in Q1 setting up a strong base, we remain confident of meeting our order inflow guidance of INR 8,000 crores that we have indicated during the previous conference call.

items.statement: Revenue guidance of INR 8,000 crores plus for FY25
items.quote: Further, in terms of execution, we anticipate to see a strong pickup in execution from Q2 onwards, and we will be targeting to achieve majority of our execution run rate in the second half of the fiscal year , with which we remain confident to deliver on the revenue guidance of INR8,000 crores plus as well.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 new orders of INR 2,170 crores
items.quote: Beginning with our order book, we have started off the first quarter of this financial year on a strong note with INR 2,170 crores of new orders, building on the order booking momentum in FY '24, where we closed the full year at approximately INR6,023 crores of orders inflow.

items.statement: Unexecuted order book stands at INR 9,396 crores with 71% domestic
items.quote: Our unexecuted order book currently stands at INR 9,396 crores with approximately 71% constituting domestic orders.

items.statement: Active pipeline of 23 GW in India and 5 GW internationally
items.quote: In terms of pipeline, we are actively pursuing projects totalling 23 gigawatt in India and 5 gigawatt in other geographies, including Middle East, Europe and Africa.

items.statement: Gross margin expected to hover in 10% range for domestic EPC
items.quote: On the margins front, our reported gross margin was 11% in Q 1. We believe our gross margin will hover in the 10% range as seen in the domestic EPC margins for the quarter.

items.statement: Recurring O&M margin at 23% in Q1, trending toward steady-state
items.quote: Recurring O&M margin was 23% in the first quarter and has begun to trend towards more steady -state margins compared to FY '24 margin of 16.7%.

items.statement: International project margins 10-12%, domestic 10-11%
items.quote: as we have explained in our previous calls, that in domestic market, margins remains from 10% to 11%. And now we are replicating the same margins for the international market - where the margins remain 10% to 12%.

items.statement: Overhead optimizations largely complete, run rate stable
items.quote: On the overhead front, we have continued to make further progress as seen in the lower quarterly run rate. We do believe bulk of the optimizations we had planned have been incorporated.

items.statement: India power demand expected to grow 7-8% annually for next 3-5 years
items.quote: The demand for power is expected to continue to increase annually by 7% to 8% over the next 3 to 5 years.

items.statement: India auctioned 35 GW renewable projects in FY24, highest ever
items.quote: India saw auction of 35 gigawatts of renewable projects in fiscal 2024, the highest-ever in a single fiscal year and solar remains at the forefront.

items.statement: O&M portfolio grew to 8.2 GW as of June 2024
items.quote: Our operation and maintenance portfolio outlook remains strong, and we have seen our portfolio grow to 8.2 gigawatts as of June 2024.

items.statement: Nigeria project contract terms finalized, financial closure expected in 6 months
items.quote: post our last call, contract terms and conditions have been finalized and we are in the last leg of approval. So that is happening and which is very, very positive.

items.statement: Nigeria project execution mostly in FY26, revenues next financial year
items.quote: The execution, however, will mostly happen in the next financial year.

items.statement: Non-fund limits INR 5,500-6,000 crores, INR 3,800-4,000 crores utilized
items.value: INR 5,500-6,000 crores total, INR 3,800-4,000 crores utilized
items.quote: The total nonfund limits are between INR5,500 crores to INR6,000 crores and roughly INR3,800 crores to INR4,000 crores stand utilized.

items.statement: Net debt INR 97 crores as of June 2024, no debt repayment till Q3 FY25
items.quote: Our net borrowing has declined sequentially by about INR19 crores, and therefore, our net debt stands at INR 97 crores as at June 2024. We do not have any debt repayment till Q3 FY '25

items.statement: Q1 FY25 revenue INR 1,920 million, EBITDA INR 521 million, EBITDA margin 27%, PAT INR 299 million, PAT margin 16%
items.quote: The total consolidated revenue of the company stood at INR1,920 million in the quarter one of financial year '25 as against INR1,291 million in quarter four of financial year '24, resulting in EBITDA of INR521 million in Q1 of financial year '25 as against INR144 million in quarter four of financial year '24, a significant increase in the comparing periods. EBITDA margin stood at 27% in Q1 of FY '

items.statement: Site 4 revenue guidance INR 200-250 crore in FY25, INR 400 crore in FY26
items.quote: We are seeing top line revenues of INR200 crores, INR250 crores approximately from the Site 4 as of today, which was supposed to be approximately at the optimum level at INR400 crores.

items.statement: Capex run rate INR 300-350 crore in FY25 and FY26
items.quote: Yes, it should be around INR300 crores to INR350 crores in both the years.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target 29-30% by FY26
items.quote: So, we see that by '26, we should be able to come back to 29%, 30% levels, for sure.

items.statement: Working capital cycle target ~200 days by end FY26, further improvement by FY27
items.quote: So '25 -- yes, we should be reaching around 200 days the end of '26 so that we can ramp up and make it more better by '27.

items.statement: Debtor days target 120 days by end FY25, 100-110 days by FY26
items.quote: Debtor side, we see a reduction by which we should come around 120 days by end of financial year '25, and by '26 we should be coming up. So 100, 110 would be normal in this current scenario of chemical industry. Going forward.

items.statement: Site 3+ and 3++ capex underway, Site 3++ commissioning expected by end Q4 FY25
items.quote: Capex at our Site 3+ and 3++ is underway as per schedule, with ongoing civil work and initiation of procurement of machinery, equipment shortly. The commissioning of Site 3++ is expected by the end of quarter four of fiscal year '25.

items.statement: Site 5 Phase 1 commissioning by end FY26, Phase 2 expansion from Q4 FY25
items.quote: Phase 1 of Site 5 is expected to be commissioned by the end of fiscal year '26 and expansion of phase 2 is set to begin from quarter four of fiscal year '25 onwards.

items.statement: Enabling resolution for fund raise to expand Site 5 and R&D/pilot facilities
items.quote: Furthermore, as we need to meet the minimum shareholding pattern, we have taken an enabling resolution to raise funds, which we will propose to our shareholders in the upcoming AGM. This will further aid us for the expansion of our visionary greenfield manufacturing Site 5 and also for expansion of our R&D and pilot plant facilities.

items.statement: Site 2 revamp expected 100% operational by August 2024 (Rohan) / end September 2024 (Faiz)
items.quote: The accident affected Site 2 is being revamped and is expected to be up and running 100% by August 2024 in a highly compliant and safe manner.

items.statement: Site 4 production ramp-up from Q2 FY25, optimum by Q3-Q4
items.quote: From Q2 the Site 4 will ramp up into production and dispatch and you will see the sales coming on from Site 4 from Q2 onwards and Q3 and Q4 will be on the optimum level.

items.statement: 5 MW solar plant commissioned in Q1 FY25, remaining 10 MW in Q2 FY25
items.quote: Out of the total 15 megawatt solar power plant order, initial commissioning of 5 megawatt solar power plant was successfully completed in quarter one, which is set to improve the bottom line of the company. The remaining 10 megawatts power plant will be commissioned in quarter two.

items.statement: Baker Hughes SSA for 6 products, 15,000-19,500 tons annual volume, $2.5-6/kg pricing
items.quote: With the SSA that we have signed, it's on six products. And in terms of the volumes of the SSA, they are range -- that has been put in the SSA is between 15,000 tons to 19,500 tons over the six products potential annual basis. And the price points range from between $2.5 to about $5 to $6 a kilo.

items.statement: Otsuka Japan project revenue from Q2 FY25 after pricing renegotiation due to JPY devaluation
items.quote: For the quarter 1 we had zero revenue from Otsuka Chemical. We are renegotiating the pricing because of the Japanese currency is being devalued quite a lot. So we're reworking on the pricing and the business will start onwards from quarter 2 and we are seeing the projections the same as before.

items.statement: Volume growth in all three business models; prices bottomed out, optimistic for upswing
items.quote: During the quarter under review, we witnessed growth in overall volumes, but the prices have been impacted due to China's dumping. We feel the prices have already bottomed out and we are optimistic for an upswing in the business scenario with numerous inquiries pouring in, in all the three business models of Aether.

items.statement: Significant influx of CRAMS inquiries due to expanded infrastructure and supply chain diversification to India
items.quote: We have been witnessing a significant influx of business inquiries in our CRAMS business model. The CRAMS business model has grown quarter-on-quarter. The huge influx of inquiries is on the backdrop of our expanded state-of-the-art infrastructure, cutting edge technology innovations, and core chemistry practices.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 revenue mix: 66% large scale manufacturing, 18% contract/exclusive manufacturing, 14% CRAMS
items.quote: With respect to Aether's business model, we have seen 66% contribution of the total top line coming from large scale manufacturing, 18% coming from contract/exclusive manufacturing, and 14% coming from contract research and manufacturing services business model during the quarter one.

items.statement: New sustainability & renewables segment launched: Converge polyols with Saudi Aramco, plastic waste-to-monomer with Novoloop, organic electrolyte additives for Li-ion batteries
items.quote: Today we are excited to announce that we are introducing a new business segment focused on sustainability and renewables. Aether Industries is likely the first company in the chemical industry, especially in India to launch such a segment. This segment includes a notable initiative and partnerships. Number one, Converge polyols, the product which has up to 40% carbon dioxide by weight. This is a j

items.statement: China dumping impacted prices; Site 3 product prices corrected 30-35% but bottomed out
items.quote: The prices have corrected up to 30%, 35% on this product, so -- on an average. So the realizations are less at the moment, but the pricings have bottomed out already.

items.statement: Solar plant to save electricity costs and improve operating margins
items.quote: This is a major investment which will be crucial in saving of electricity costs and further aids in improving operating margins of the company.

items.statement: Inventory days reduced to 160 from 210; debtor cycle ~140 days; expect improvement with Baker Hughes commercialization
items.quote: Though the debtor cycle is at around 140 days, our inventory days have reduced to 160 days by end of quarter one of financial year '25, which had increased to 210 days as on the 31st March, 2024. With the commercialization of the SSA with Baker Hughes, we anticipate to have the better debtor cycle in future.

items.statement: Received INR 210 million on-account insurance payment against INR 1,000 million claim; claim admitted
items.quote: During the quarter, we have received INR210 million from the insurance company as an on-account payment towards the insurance claim that we have submitted of total INR1,000 million. This on-account payment also envisages that the insurance company has admitted our claim.

items.statement: Baker Hughes strategic supply agreement signed; first strategic contract manufacturing partner in India for them
items.quote: We have signed a multi-year extendable contract to manufacture six new products for Baker Hughes globally. We will be the first ones in India manufacturing these products and the supply will be to the global Baker Hughes locations with a focus on India's oil and gas sector as well.

items.statement: Novoloop pilot validation completed initial phases; extended integrated pilot validation underway; demo plant ~2026, full commercialization ~2028-29
items.quote: We are currently doing the pilot plant validation of the Novoloop technology, and that is successfully completed in terms of the first few phases. And now, we are going to do the extended integrated pilot plant validation of the Novoloop technology and that's under discussion right now. And then the -- if it all works out, if it all goes forward, we'll be looking at commercializing and doing the f

items.statement: Site 5 all statutory and regulatory approvals in place
items.quote: All the statutory and regulatory approvals are in place for the same as well for the Site 5.

items.statement: R&D spend INR 143 million (7.5% of revenue) in Q1 FY25; pilot plant commissioned
items.quote: Our R&D expenses for the quarter one of fiscal year '25, which is the current quarter -- past, stood at INR143 million, i.e., 7.5% of our total revenues was R&D spending. We have successfully expanded and commissioned our pilot plant, which is now set to aid us in enhancing chemical development and scale up of our in-house molecules, as well as further expanding our CRAMS portfolio.

items.statement: Management will not provide any guidance to avoid distraction from long-term objectives
items.quote: One of the things that we have been mentioning is that we would like to desist from providing any guidance of any form as it is providing a distraction from our long-term objective.

items.statement: Deposit growth fell short of expectations due to current account outflows and HDFC non-retail deposit runoff
items.quote: But this time around obviously, we were a little bit surprised on the period-end numbers because of some unexpected flows in the current accounts, which was more than what we had anticipated.

items.statement: NIMs stable at 3.4-3.5% with increasing bias; CASA ratio 36-38%; cost-to-income 40-41% with decreasing bias
items.quote: For example, the NIMs have been in the range of 3.4% to 3.5% with an increasing bias. The CASA ratio has been in the range of 36% to 38%. The cost-to-income has been in the range of 40% to 41% with a decreasing bias.

items.statement: Average deposits show steady secular upward trend from Q1 FY22 to Q1 FY25
items.quote: If you've seen the numbers and once you digest the average numbers on a quarterly basis, which we have given from quarter 1 of FY '22 to quarter 1 of FY '25, that will give you a reasonable amount of comfort that there is a steady build up , a secular trend, an upward trend in the momentum.

items.statement: Bank remains disciplined on deposit pricing, not competing on rates; weighted average term deposit cost below peers
items.quote: So we have tried to remain disciplined on price as much as possible to win over the customer through engagement and service delivery. So we've not gone into this term -- in terms of the rate as such.

items.statement: Consciously reducing transactional corporate business not meeting pricing thresholds; shifting mix toward profitable growth
items.quote: What we are losing is transactional business consciously because it's not meeting our pricing thresholds. We are all right to do so because we -- maybe this is the best time for us to adjust our mix.

items.statement: Added 2.2 million new customer relationships in Q1 FY25; monthly deposit inflows up over 20% year-on-year
items.quote: we did add 2.2 million new customer relationships in the quarter. So last quarter was very similar. So from that sense, the pace at which the g round teams are operating is quite strong

items.statement: Reduced borrowings by ~INR600 billion in Q1 FY25; INR150 billion commercial paper maturity; scheduled maturity profile INR650 billion for FY25
items.quote: In the quarter, we did take down close to INR60,000-odd crores or INR600 billion of borrowings down. About INR150 billion was commercial papers - which matured, and we had to run it down anyway.

items.statement: GNPA stable at 1.2-1.4% range (ex-agri declining); HDB Financial GNPA flat at 1.9%, credit costs higher due to seasonal collection issues
items.quote: The GNPA has been in the range of 1.2% to 1.4%. And if you exclude the seasonality of agri, in fact, it's been on a declining trend.

items.statement: Loan-deposit ratio to be reduced faster than anticipated; focus on profitable growth over loan growth
items.quote: It is in our interest to bring down the loan -deposit ratios much faster than what one would have anticipated. It is in our interest, and I'll explain that to you probably when one of you ask questions.

items.statement: No regulatory prescription for LDR; SMF category target 10%, was ~9% in past year, tried to close gap by June
items.quote: the SMF category target is, of course, the obligation is 10%. We were close to 9% in the past year. But as of June, we did not see much. We've tried to clos e it on as of June

items.statement: No compromise on strategic investments in distribution or technology; focusing on digitization and productivity efficiencies
items.quote: I'm very clear about it. So what we are trying to do is how do we juice out efficiencies out of digitization, out of better productivity.

items.statement: Avoiding period-end performance pressure on ground teams; aligning internal and external metrics to daily averages
items.quote: Focusing on certain period -end numbers is leading to some unintended performance -related pressures, which we want to avoid. And that is the reason why we want to converge or align our internal and external metrics.

items.statement: EPS similar to pre-merger levels (~21.3 vs 21.4); changed liquidity conditions and forgone forbearances impacted merger accretion assumptions
items.quote: The EPS for the bank, June, pre -merger was 21.4 - last year June. And in this quarter, it was 21.3. So thereabouts, right, it is similar levels.

items.statement: HDFC One App cross-sell progressing: >85% of new home loan borrowers taking savings accounts; insurance journeys expected shortly
items.quote: Incrementally, we are now doing what percentage of our home loan borrowers are -- taking upwards of 85%. Now as I said, the bundling of other products such as the consumer durable loans, the credit cards, the insurance and all has commenced.

items.statement: FY25 volume growth expected healthy in replacement and OEM segments
items.quote: We expect FY '25 volume growth in replacement segment to remain healthy and OEM growth in most categories, led by 2-wheelers and passengers and MHCV will continue to be good.

items.statement: Price hikes taken in Q1: commercial 2.3%, passenger 2.5-3%, 2-wheeler 1%
items.quote: We have tried to mitigate it with price increase in all segments, led by replacement in commercial segment, as we speak, including July, we have had a 2.3% price hike. In passenger segment, including July, we have had a similar price hike of around 2.5% to 3%.

items.statement: Further 3-4% price hikes needed in Q2 to cover RM cost gaps
items.quote: I think progressively because raw material costs impacts as we based on arrivals. I think about overall to recover all the cost gaps in quarter 1 and now, 3% to 4% kind of increase would be required progressively.

items.statement: Natural rubber prices surged 25-30% to INR200/kg, highest in 13 years
items.quote: Domestic natural rubber prices has surged by about 25% to 30% over the past few months. And currently, it has scaled INR200 which is the highest in the last 13 years.

items.statement: RM basket up 5% QoQ, natural rubber at INR207/kg, crude derivatives range-bound
items.quote: Our raw material cost has gone up approximately by 5% quarter -on-quarter and this is singularly responsible for the contraction in gross margin.

items.statement: Q2 RM costs expected 5-6% higher than Q1, freight rates to normalize
items.quote: Overall, we expect raw material prices in quarter 2 to be higher by about 5% to 6% over quarter 1.

items.statement: Gross margin contracted 184bps YoY and 306bps QoQ due to RM cost increase
items.quote: Coming to gross margin , our gross margin during the quarter shrunk by about 184 basis points year -on-year and 306 basis points quarter -on-quarter, largely due to increase in raw material costs that you know about 5% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 12.2%, down 130bps QoQ due to RM costs and higher marketing spend
items.quote: Our consolidated EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR388.2 crores, this is about 12.2% margin. This is a contraction of 130 basis points quarter-on-quarterand primarily, the contraction is on account of increase in raw material prices and higher but planned marketing expense in quarter 1.

items.statement: FY25 capex guidance INR1,000 cr, INR254 cr spent in Q1, projects on track
items.quote: We indicated a capex for the year at around INR1,000 crores, out of which about INR254 crores were spent in quarter 1, and all expansion projects are progressing as per plan.

items.statement: Capacity utilization ~80%, Chennai TBR capacity coming online end of Q2
items.quote: Further happy to share that we have had the highest ever production in our Chennai, Bhandup and Halol plants during the quarter, leading to a better capacity utilization overall of about 80%.

items.statement: International order base strong, double-digit export growth expected for FY25
items.quote: Our order base looks strong and the growth is coming from desired focused markets of Latin America, Europe and progressively, it will also come from US.

items.statement: Rural demand recovering with good monsoons, replacement double-digit growth expected to continue
items.quote: Rural demand seems to be coming back gradually. With good monsoons, we expect rural demand to keep coming back as sustainably as a high level as compared to urban demand.

items.statement: Replacement volume growth double-digit in Q1, led by commercial and 2-wheeler segments
items.quote: Replacement volume was led by commercial vehicles and 2-wheeler segment, I spoke about the brand relaunch, which has led to increased traction in premium categories.

items.statement: Premiumization saliency increasing in passenger and 2-wheeler segments
items.quote: Our saliency in premium categories is continuously up in passenger segment as well as in 2-wheeler segment.

items.statement: EV OEM share ~30% in 2W, 3W and 4W EVs in India
items.quote: We have consolidat ed our position in electric vehicle OEMs in both 2-wheeler and 3-wheeler. We have close to 30% share now in both 2-wheeler and 3-wheeler EV OEMs as well as in 4 -wheeler EVs being sold by OEMs in India.

items.statement: International business saliency 20% in Q1, targeting 25% in 2-3 years, margin accretive
items.quote: International business has been a focus. 20% is saliency in quarter 1, and we have targeted at levels of 25% in 2 to 3 years. This is margin accretive.

items.statement: US TBR channel build-out 60% complete, PCR rollout by Q4 FY25 or Q1 FY26
items.quote: In US truck bus radial the channel build out has happened to a significant extent. We have created, let's say, so me kind of geographies within U S in mind and 60% of those geographies are already covered by way of network access and we have started booking orders and shipping truck bus radials to US.

items.statement: Negative working capital INR240 cr, healthy operating cash flow funded capex
items.quote: We kept tight controls on our working capital, as always, and closed the quarter with a negative working capital of INR240 crores. We generated healthy operating cash flow, which allowed us to meet the entire capex of INR25 44 crores during the quarter funded from our internal accruals.

items.statement: Consolidated debt INR1,647 cr, debt/EBITDA 1.1x, debt/equity 0.4x
items.quote: Our consolidated debt stood at INR1,647 crores, a marginal increase of INR18 crores over quarter 4 of last year and INR343 crores reduction year-on-year basis. Our debt to EBITDA on a stand-alone basis stand at healthy 1.1 and debt to equity of 0.4.

items.statement: EPR treated as normal RM cost internally, provision taken in Q1, rates uncertain
items.quote: No, EPR now from our planning point of view we should assume it as a part of the cost. Internally, we would like to treat that like a normal raw material cost while working out internally gross margins and internal margins.

items.statement: Employee cost lower QoQ due to normalization of variable incentives, VRS costs in exceptional items
items.quote: Employee costs was lower during the quarter, as in the quarter 4 of last financial year, we had higher variable incentives and retirals that was provided for based on t he previous year's

items.statement: Revenue growth 8.8% YoY driven entirely by volume growth, pricing flat
items.quote: Yes, year-on-year basis as well as quarter -on-quarter basis, the revenue growth is actually a volume growth. In fact maybe plus or minus 0.1% level. Okay . So you might assume it as a volume growth.

items.statement: Container shortages and 3-4x freight hikes impacting international business growth
items.quote: There have been some headwinds in terms of significant freight hikes to the extent of 3x to 4x in international business and also, coupled with this was the issue of non -availability of containers.

items.statement: Full-year volume guidance of 6.5 million tonnes cement, excluding clinker sales
items.quote: I think we are reasonably sure that we should be very close to 6.5 million. This includes the lower vol umes that have been moved, and this definitely excludes the clinker sale. So, 6.5 million is our volume guidance

items.statement: Full-year EBITDA guidance of ₹350-375 crore, translating to ₹550-575 per tonne
items.quote: From a profitability guidance perspective, we believe that t he overall EBITDA should be in the range of around ₹350 crores to ₹375 crores, which should roughly translate to ₹550 to ₹575 EBITDA per tonne

items.statement: Prices dropped ₹10/bag from Q4 to end of Q1, and a further ₹5/bag from end of Q1 to mid-July
items.quote: We believe, or at least what we have noticed in most of our operating markets, there has been a drop of ₹5 per bag from the exit of Q4 till middle of t his month. That has been the case across the markets

items.statement: Expect seasonal price increase of ₹10-15/bag from mid-Q3 as demand picks up
items.quote: We are not trying to be euphoric about the potential kind of a price increase that is possible in the marketplace, what we have penci lled is ₹10 to ₹15 per bag potentially to go up from middle of Q3 is what we are factoring, which is normal seasonal kind of thing

items.statement: Demand expected to pick up sharply from mid-Q3 as election-related deferrals resume and Amaravati project progresses
items.quote: we strongly believe that from middle of Q3, the demand is likely to sh arp up more sharply

items.statement: FY25 capex plan of ~₹300 crore, with ₹33 crore spent in Q1; Andhra Cements expansion ₹255 crore this year, balance in FY26
items.quote: If you look at the Slide 12, we did indicate the overall kind of a CapEx plan for Andhra, it is ₹255 for the current financial year, balance in FY '26.

items.statement: Targeting ₹250/tonne cost reduction at clinker level from Andhra Cements efficiency capex, plus ₹25/tonne at cement grinding level
items.quote: So all in all, we are looking at close to ₹250 per tonne, up to clinker to come down. And from a perspective of cement grinding, we expect the number of units to come down by five units. So that should be another ₹25-odd at the cement level.

items.statement: Clinker sales of ~84,000 tonnes in Q1 at ₹3,050/tonne ex-works due to excess inventory; not a regular strategy
items.quote: Yeah, I think it's around 84,000 has been the sale of clinker for the last quarter. The average realisation is close to around ₹3,050 kind of a number per tonne. I'm talking about ex-work.

items.statement: Industry utilisation in AP/Telangana at 45-50%; new supply ramp-ups (Shree, Dalmia, My Home, UltraTech, Deccan) to be absorbed by demand recovery from mid-Q3
items.quote: So the average capacity utilisation in our view is somewhere around 45% to 50% in general. There could be one or two units, which could be exceptionally higher or lower than this, but in general, the capacity utilisation is somewhere around in the range of around 45% to 50%.

items.statement: Net debt target capped at ₹1,250-1,300 crore for FY25; gross debt not to exceed current level; Vizag land sale not factored into cash flows this year
items.quote: I think we should be at a similar level. I think around ₹1,300 odd, ₹1,250 to ₹1,300 is what we are limiting ourselves. So I think we would be capping our net debt position there. Gross, we would not exceed the current position itself.

items.statement: Andhra Cements expected to break even by Q1 FY26 as ramp-up and optimisation progress
items.quote: Yeah, I think we shoul d be very close to that time line . It's just a question of ramping up. The internal capacity as well as optimi sation is progressing. It's a question of doing volumes. I think we should be breakevening by Q1 is what we strongly think

items.statement: Renewable energy roadmap: 6MW solar each at Gudipadu and Dachepalli in FY25; 4MW WHR at Gudipadu by FY27; 4MW solar at Mattampally and Jeerabad by FY27; 2MW WHR at Mattampally by FY28; 9MW WHR at Dachepalli by FY29
items.quote: If you can look at the same Slide 12, yeah, we did indicate just solar Gudipadu is 6 MW by FY '25, waste heat recovery for Gudipadu by FY '27. Solar 4 megawatt at M attampally by FY '27. Waste heat recovery for Line 1 at Mattampally, which is 2 MW by FY '28. Solar at Jeerabad 4 megawatt by FY

items.statement: Madhya Pradesh market down 15% YoY in Q1; Gujarat down 5% YoY; Odisha flat to slightly positive
items.quote: assessment is that Madhya Pradesh market has come down by 15% year -on-year. Whereas Gujarat actually is trending upward, but it is 5% lower at the current quarter year-on-year kind of thing. Odisha is flat to slightly with a positive bias

items.statement: Green power share at 30% currently; moving to 50% could add ₹50-75/tonne EBITDA as blended power cost falls from ₹6 to ₹4.75-5/unit
items.quote: Now the minut e we go up to 50%. That is incrementally. We believe that it should contribute close to around another ₹50 to ₹75 per tonne because it also has its cost, right? It's not that it is coming free

items.statement: Hyderabad prices already at floor; further significant decline unlikely as industry bleeding; Chennai prices at par or below Hyderabad for first time
items.quote: For the first time in my career, I've seen Chennai prices, either at par or lower than par, this we have never noticed. So would Hyderabad prices get corrected way below Chennai prices just because Chennai prices have come down? Only time will tell. But I think Hyderabad prices are not at its best either.

items.statement: Maintenance capex of ₹150-200/tonne/year for pyro section plus ~₹100/tonne for other consumables; long-term kiln overhauls capitalised
items.quote: But all in all, what we generally do not only for the kiln, but the entire equipment, anywhere between ₹150 to ₹200 per tonne as we replace the maintenance kind of a cost for the overall kind of maintenance.

items.statement: Expect revenue growth uptick starting Q2 FY25
items.quote: We do believe from Q2 you will see us back on the growth side and we will build on that as we accelerate towards where we want to go with our clients.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA for FY25 to exceed last year's 11% consolidated level
items.quote: Our goal remains to achieve double-digit EBITDA. We believe we will be much higher than last year's 11% on a consolidated level.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin at 9.9%, up 176 bps QoQ
items.quote: On the EBITDA level, we grew 21% quarter-on-quarter, ending at a 9.9% margin. It's a bit short, but still a growth of 176 bps points.

items.statement: Strong demand across US and Europe; opening Toronto office to service North America
items.quote: We have never had this kind of demand from our customers, especially in U.S. and Europe. And I think that number is only going to increase is what I see as we keep hiring more account delivery managers and account sales managers for the clients that we already serve.

items.statement: Targeting 70% revenue from outside India (currently 50%)
items.quote: I believe the right sweet spot for us is 70% of the revenue should come from outside India. That's always been the dream and that's where all our investments has been and that gives us a good balance from a risk perspective as well over the next few.

items.statement: Investing in labs, centers of excellence, delivery teams across three verticals and horizontals
items.quote: Our balance sheet remains robust. For the first time, we crossed Rs 100 crore in cash on hand as of June 2024, and this number will keep improving as we continue to build a strong business model with investmen ts in labs, centers of excellence, and delivery teams across the three verticals and horizontals

items.statement: Execution risk from visa/work permit delays for onsite hiring in US, UK, Germany, Canada
items.quote: For execution, I do need a lot of visas, whether it's UK, Canada, Germany, U.S., and that's something Onward does not have. That's a new business for us in the last three years. So, we are building on that and we are seeing amazing momentum towards that.

items.statement: Signed Rs 6.5 crore 3-year deal with Microsoft including Copilot GenAI licenses
items.quote: Just to give you a perspective, a couple of days back, we signed a Rs 6.5 crore deal with Microsoft for the next three years or something along those lines. We see that we are confident of the demand that we see for the next three years.

items.statement: Annual rate negotiations with T&M clients (80-90% of revenue) showing positive outcomes
items.quote: And on the pricing side, it's always a conversation because the majority of our business model, 80% or 90% of our revenue comes from time and material. So, every year, Sapna, my team and me have a conversation with all our clients, not just the top 5 clients, every client that we have on the T&M side, which is on pricing, right? And we see a lot of positives.

items.statement: Targeting 200-300 H-1B visas within 2-3 years to drive substantial revenue growth
items.quote: For example, we applied for over 200 H-1Bs last year and received 25 to 30 approvals—our first approvals in six to seven years. This is a significant development, and we aim to have 200 to 300 H-1Bs available within 2-3 years, which we anticipate will drive substantial revenue growth.

items.statement: Net headcount target of 2,700-2,900 consolidated; focus on adding 1,500 people in Europe and US
items.quote: I think it will be between 2,700 and 2,900 people net as a consolidated basis. And what is important is can we add that 1,500 people in Europe and U.S.?

items.statement: Q1 revenue shortfall due to lack of technical people in US and work permit delays in Europe
items.quote: Yes, so two things from a U.S. perspective, we did not have the technical people and that's something where we lost some traction, let's say, in the month of June. And from a Europe perspective, the projects that we won, which were supposed to start billing in Q4, did not start and some are starting as I said as early as coming Monday. Because work permits took longer and something or the other.

items.statement: Dividend increased from Rs 3 to Rs 5 per share, approved at AGM
items.quote: Earlier today in the AGM, we increased the dividend from Rs. 3 to Rs. 5, which got approved by the shareholders.

items.statement: No demand deferment seen; customers want immediate project starts after award
items.quote: No. So, another point that you mentioned, execution challenge continues to be there for us in Europe and U.S., where after winning a project, and I have shared it before as well, customer wants to start tomorrow because every company that we are working with, and you guys all know some of the names, are very cash-rich, very powerful, very largest companies in the world, and they have huge budgets.

items.statement: Reducing customer count from 85 to target 60-75 for deeper engagements across three horizontals
items.quote: In terms of customer engagements, we had about 250 customers three years ago. Now, we are down to 85 plus customers, aiming for a sweet spot of 60 to 75 customers to build deeper engagements and add value across our three horizontals: mechanica l engineering, embedded electronics, and digital services

items.statement: Do not share quarterly or annual revenue projections; too young as a company
items.quote: We don't share projections. As I said we are too young. We have to get to what we are good at and get back to work.

items.statement: FY25 deposit growth guidance 9-11%, advances 11-13%
items.quote: The deposits have grown by 8.5% YoY, advances by 11.5%, largely in alignment with our guidance range of 9 % to 11% for deposits and 11% to 13% for advances.

items.statement: FY25 NIM guidance 2.8-3%, actual Q1 3.05%
items.quote: Our NIM is at 3.05% surpassing our guidance of 2.8% to 3% for FY25.

items.statement: FY25 credit cost guidance below 1%
items.quote: We have given a guidance of less than 1%. So, yes, we're looking at sticking to that.

items.statement: FY25 ROA guidance above 1%
items.quote: ROA, we have given a guidance that we will be above 1% and that's what We have achieved in Q1.

items.statement: FY25 cost-to-income ratio expected 44-45.5%
items.quote: We expect to be in the range of about 45% to 45.5% somewhere there. So, it will be between that 44% range to the 45.5% range.

items.statement: Plan to open 200-250 branches in FY25, mostly premium at RUSU locations
items.quote: This year we would be opening about 200-250 branches. And basically, these branches will be in the premium kind of a branches.

items.statement: Board approved Rs.10,000 crore capital raise for FY25: Rs.6,000 crore equity, Rs.4,000 crore AT1/Tier 2
items.quote: We also have a plan to raise capital to the extent of Rs.10,000 crores for FY25. It has been approved by the board, of which Rs.6,000 crores will be equity and Rs.4,000 crores through AT 1 and Tier 2 instruments.

items.statement: Q1 total business Rs.21.36 trillion, deposits Rs.12.24 trillion, advances Rs.9.12 trillion
items.quote: Total business of the Bank reached Rs.21.36 trillion with deposits of Rs.12.24 trillion and advances at Rs.9.12 trillion

items.statement: RAM advances grew 14.5% YoY, large corporate 7.8% YoY
items.quote: We grew better under RAM advances by 14.5%, while large corporate advances grew by 7.8%.

items.statement: Gold loan portfolio Rs.78,000 crore, Rs.66,000 crore in agri, up from Rs.43,000 crore YoY
items.quote: Total portfolio of gold is about Rs. 78,000 crores and out of that, Rs. 66,000 crores is in agri.

items.statement: Yield on advances declined 11 bps QoQ due to lower dummy ledger recovery
items.quote: Yield on advances has declined by about 15 days, primarily due to the fall in our DL recovery. About 11 bps impact it had because of the DL recovery compared to the previous quarter.

items.statement: GNPA 4.54%, NNPA 0.90%, PCR 93.5%, credit cost 0.73%
items.quote: GNPA has reduced by 280 bps, net NPA has come down by 68 bps to 0.90%, PCR has improved by 263 bps to 93.5%. The credit cost improved to 0.73%

items.statement: Gross recovery Rs.3,368 crore, slippages Rs.2,318 crore in Q1
items.quote: In line with our guidance, gross NPA reduced to 4.54% with gross recovery at 3,368 crores and slippages restricted to 2,318 crores.

items.statement: Standard asset provision Rs.1,296 crore for potential stress in couple of accounts, one-off
items.quote: Standard asset provisioning, we have done to the extent of about Rs.1,296 crores. It's increased to that extent. This increase is due to an anticipated distress or potential restructuring in a couple of accounts.

items.statement: Agri GNPA down from 10% to 8% YoY, gold loan GNPA ~0.02%, SHG GNPA <2%
items.quote: We started off with almost like 10% in June 23, today we are at 8%. That's the kind of secured NPA that we have seen in our agriculture.

items.statement: MSME NPA improving, 50% micro advances with 75% CGTMSE cover
items.quote: If you look at my MSME book, almost 50% of my MSME book is in the micro advances and which is 75% collateral is available in the form of CGTMSE.

items.statement: SMA book Rs.5,144 crore in June 2024, distributed across retail, MSME, agri, corporate
items.quote: The total SMA book consists of about, if you look at the June '24 book, it's about Rs. 5,144 crores and that's differentiated between retail, MSME, agriculture and the corporate.

items.statement: Cost of deposits fell 5 bps QoQ due to excess liquidity, may rise as credit grows
items.quote: QoQ, the cost of deposits is slightly reduced by 5 bps over March '24. It is because we did not take much funds in the market and we have got enough of liquidity with us.

items.statement: Swap-related treasury income ~Rs.700-800 crore per quarter, stable
items.quote: Yes, it will be around Rs.700 to 800 crores, madam. It is on par with the year and quarter basis, similar income.

items.statement: CASA 72% of total deposits, grew 3.7% YoY, SB deposits 4.6% YoY
items.quote: CASA and retail term deposits form 72% of our total deposits and we are maintaining this ratio consistently for a long time.

items.statement: PSLC income Rs.955 crore in Q1, traded at Rs.1.80-2.00, mainly private bank buyers
items.quote: fees, we have got about Rs. 955 crores. That is generally a Q1 event

items.statement: Recovery from written-off accounts Rs.954 crore in Q1, target Rs.4,000+ crore for FY25
items.quote: On an average, we recover around Rs. 1000 crore plus in technical write-off. Last year also, it was Rs.4000 crore plus for the entire year.

items.statement: New investment norms from April 2024: AFS reclassified as banking book, MTM gains to P&L daily
items.quote: As far as treasury is concerned after the new guidelines, AFS book will not be treated as a trading book, it is a banking book.

items.statement: ECL implementation expected FY26-27, one-year timeline after final guidelines, impact manageable
items.quote: The news is that it will be implemented for FY26-27. So, in this scenario, we will not have a substantial impact on our balance sheet with regard to ECL.

items.statement: Digital frauds 70-80% of reported Rs.465 crore fraud, real-time monitoring and AI deployed
items.quote: Almost like 70% to 80% of these frauds are digital frauds of small in nature and of course the remaining are credit and credit fraud that is happening.

items.statement: Telangana farm loan waiver impact unknown, second phase completes by Aug 15
items.quote: It has just started. So, we will not know the impact because we are doing it in two phases. The second phase will be completed by August 15th.

items.statement: Credit growth outpacing deposit growth industry-wide, wedge may persist 12 more months per RBI
items.quote: The RBI itself in the latest financial stability report has come up with an analysis which shows that in high growth phases, typically, the wedge between credit and deposit growth lasts for 2 to 4 years.

items.statement: Opened first branch in Lakshadweep at Agatti, 12 premium branches in RUSU locations
items.quote: We have opened the first branch in Lakshadweep at Agatti and also opened 12 premium branches in the RUSU locations.

items.statement: Construction commenced at Thervoykandigai; plant and machinery erection in progress, trial by end of calendar year, production from Q4 2025
items.quote: Erection of plant and machinery is in progress and is expected to be completed for trial by the end of this calendar year and production to commence from Q4 2025 at our unit at Thervoykandigai, Tamil Nadu, where we are increasing capacities in Lead vertical from 1,32,000 metric ton to 2,04,000 metric ton per annum in two Phases.

items.statement: Lead production target for FY25 is 85,000 to 90,000 metric tons; FY26 target is 100,000 to 110,000 metric tons
items.quote: The production sales in terms of metric ton should be around -- last year, it was about 71,000. This year, it should be around the range of 85,000 to 90,000 metric tons

items.statement: Expect 15% volume growth in coming years, 20% ROCE growth, EBITDA margins tending towards 7% to 8%, value-added products increasing to 60% plus
items.quote: So we see the trend continue for us. And we have also kind of released our investor presentation where we see the growth numbers in volumes to continue for us. So there will be 15% volume growth in the coming years. In terms of the return on capital employed, we expect 20% growth. And in terms of EBITDA margins, we will be tending towards 7% to 8% levels and we will be increasing our value-added p

items.quote: The domestic markets for our product portfolio is seeing a positive momentum in growth. In future, we expect the numbers to remain at similar level with a variation of plus or minus 5%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin percentage remains constant at 5% to 6%; absolute EBITDA grows with volume; new project will increase both percentage and absolute EBITDA
items.quote: But EBITDA, we should not see in absolute terms. We should see in the percentage terms. So in terms of percentage, it is remains constant at the level of 5% to 6% EBITDA. Now, over the period, we are increasing the volume. So naturally in absolute terms, overall EBITDA value also going up gradually and once our new project comes in, the Thervoykandigai, EBITDA in terms of percentage and absolute t

items.statement: Pricing arrangement uses previous month average applied to next month providing natural hedging
items.quote: Pricing arrangement is such that previous month average will be applied to the next month. So natural hedging is there.

items.statement: Global lead market growing 6-7% CAGR; India growing 12-13%; strong demand supports capacity expansion to 204,000 tons
items.quote: Globally, lead market is growing at about 6% to 7%. Now, when it comes to India, India is also growing at relatively 12% to 13%. And we see a lot of potential in the global demand. And that is one of the reasons which initiated the expansion plan for the Thervoykandigai unit where we are increasing our capacities from 1,32,000 tons to 204,000 metric tons per annum.

items.statement: Currency exposure mainly USD; hedged via natural hedge and forward contracts per risk management policy; minimal P&L impact
items.quote: So in terms of currency, our major exposure is towards USD, both on the import leg as well as the USD leg. We have defined risk management policies wherein we hedge our currency risk, mostly its natural hedge and balance, we hedge -- do a forward contract and hedge the balance. So generally, for currency fluctuation, there is not much impact in our P&L

items.statement: Multi-sourcing strategy from 70+ countries, 270+ suppliers with long-term contracts ensuring supply consistency
items.quote: So, on the sourcing part, when you mentioned the scrapyards, so we follow a multi-sourcing strategy and right now we are procuring from almost 70 plus countries. And it's very important to note that we have an overall supplier base of 270 plus and most of them have long-term association with our company. And furthermore, it is important to note as well that we have long-term contracts with them. S

items.statement: Smelting capacity to increase from 80,000 to 160,000 metric tons per annum in two phases at Thervoykandigai
items.quote: The existing capacity for smelting is about 80,000 metric ton. And when we make this Thervoykandigai plant operational, this smelting capacity will increase up to 1,60,000 metric tons in two phases. When the two phases get complete, our overall smelting capacity should be around 1,60,000 metric tons per annum.

items.statement: Aluminum die-cast alloy segment paused due to unprofitable market; reviewing portfolio for value-added products or forward integration
items.quote: No. So, aluminum, what is happening is -- I'll just give you a background on aluminum. We were manufacturing the die cast alloy segment, and unfortunately, for the last two years, the particular industry was bleeding. And even though that we had, I mean, initiated production and sold the material, we don't want to enter into a bandwagon effect where we get into a fragmented market and have to rush

items.statement: Overall EBITDA margins targeted at 7% to 7.5% by FY27 from current 5% to 6%
items.quote: Till FY '27 -- yeah, so this will span over the next three years where right now we are doing about 5% to 6% and by -- in the next three years, we will be tending towards 7% to 7.5%.

items.statement: Lead EBITDA margins expected to improve 120-150 bps to 6% to 6.5%
items.quote: we will see a positive impact on the lead margins to the extent of about 120 to 150 basis points. So we see that number come to about 6% to 6.5%.

items.statement: Plastics revenue target of INR50 crores with positive EBITDA this year
items.quote: this year, we look -- like we've mentioned in our investor presentation and previous calls, we look at about INR50 crores of top line in plastics with a positive number, of course.

items.statement: Aluminum business loss stopped in current year
items.quote: Aluminum current year's loss is totally stopped. There is no loss in the current year.

items.statement: Lead smelting capacity expansion from 80,000-85,000 tons to 150,000-160,000 tons per annum
items.quote: we are at between 80,000 tons to 85,000 tons smelting capacities, which we tend -- which we will be increasing to about 160,000 tons --150,000 tons to 160,000 tons per annum.

items.statement: Lead volume growth of 15% to 20% expected this year
items.quote: we see about 15% to 20% growth in volumes this year.

items.statement: Overall market demand projections expected at 20% plus across all customers
items.quote: Overall market scenario and the projections are expected to be 20% plus this year across all customers.

items.statement: Plastics recycling margins 6% to 8%, compounding margins 12% to 14%
items.quote: On the recycle segment, it is 6% to 8% on a good day. On better days, it is probably a little higher. But if you look at the compounding segment which we -- where the major value addition happens, we're looking at roughly 12% to 14% numbers there.

items.statement: Shift to battery-focused procurement for higher margins in lead recycling
items.quote: we see a lot of procurement of batteries happening in the last one year, and we see that trend to grow in the coming years. And that was one of the major reasons that we intended to start the expansion plan for lead.

items.statement: Copper expansion planned after Thervoykandigai plant commissioning, focusing on smelting, refining and alloys
items.quote: We are looking at smelting and refining and also doing some copper alloys and other product portfolio mix. That is -- the project team is evaluating both the techno-commercial proposal and we will see that happening once the Thervoykandigai plant goes live.

items.statement: Q1 revenue included INR20-25 crores spillover from previous quarter
items.quote: Around INR20 crore to INR25 crore on account of that previous quarter. Balance is normal sale for this quarter only.

items.statement: New customers comprise 15% to 20% of overall sales, added in East Asia and Western regions
items.quote: So the new customers comprise about 15% to 20% of this overall sales. So there are some new customers in East Asian regions where we have added up. And in the case of Western parts of the globe also, we have added one or two customers.

items.statement: Expects net addition of 50 screens in FY25 with 120 gross additions and 70 exits
