items.statement: Implementing capital-light growth model by partnering with developers for joint capex investment
items.quote: As guided last quarter, we are been selective in new screen additions and gradually implementing a capital-light growth model by partnering with developers and jointly investing in new screen capex.

items.statement: Q2 started strong with Kalki spillover and strong lineup across languages; no major event disruptions expected
items.quote: With Kalki's spill over and the visibility of a great lineup ahead across the languages, Q2 has started off on a great note. We see no other major event disruptions that could hamper the release calendar.

items.statement: Ticket prices increased ~4% in Q1 but ATP declined 5% due to lack of blockbusters; strong uptick post Kalki
items.quote: We did pass on the inflation-led increase in ticket prices to the customers. So in fact, the ticket prices were increased by about 4%.

items.statement: Fixed costs up 7% YoY; same-store fixed cost growth 2.5%; rental escalation 3.7% on same cinemas
items.quote: So on our fixed cost, actually, if you look at our total fixed cost, it has gone up by 7% compared to last year quarter 1. And if we further break that down into like-for-like same-store basis, the same-store growth is only about 2.5%.

items.statement: 15% of current screens are premium formats; 15-20% of new screen additions will be premium formats
items.quote: New screen additions that we are doing, we are adding anywhere between 15% to 20% of new screens in premium or special f ormat screens

items.statement: Karnataka 1-2% cess media report not confirmed as government order; industry engaging with authorities
items.quote: We've been in touch with the government officers. We reached out to the relevant mini stry. And so far, there is no confirmation that this is a definitive government order

items.statement: Monetizing two non-core office assets for INR 300-350 crore; bids received, negotiations ongoing
items.quote: So about 300 to 350 is what we believe it shall be the capital values of the two assets.

items.statement: Re-releases contributed ~12 lakh admissions in Q1; expanding curated film festivals across all geographies
items.quote: This quarter, we contributed close to about 12 lakh admissions coming in from the re-releases itself. So we believe that this is a funnel, which should be truly irrigated, and we will be working on this very vigorously now going forward.

items.statement: Expects similar full-year admissions as FY24 if remaining films perform per original estimates
items.quote: I think Q1 got impacted because the films which were earlier scheduled to be released in Q1 got shifted. So as far as the full year picture goes, what we had earlier estimated, we feel that if the films which are sch eduled to be released in the remaining part of the year, if they perform as per our original estimates, then we should be doing similar admissions as we did in last financial

items.statement: Theatrical window harmonization across regions has consensus but no timeline; South at 4 weeks vs 8 weeks elsewhere
items.quote: We've had some positive conversations with respect to increasing windows, making them consistent across the country. We would not put any timelines to it.

items.statement: New screens typically reach cinema-level EBITDA breakeven within 6-9 months; majority of year-old screens profitable
items.quote: Typically, they start becoming profitable at EBITDA level -- at cinema EBITDA level within 6 to 9 months of opening. And payback periods, et cetera, will vary depending on where the screen is and what sort of formats they are operating.

items.statement: Content pipeline for Q2-Q4 looks strong with many Q1 films pushed forward; full recovery to pre-COVID levels expected next financial year
items.quote: Fortunately, Q2, Q3 and Q4 is looking fairly strong also partly because a lot of films, which were coming in Q1 were pushed to Q2 or Q3. Therefore, it's looking fairly crowded, but we believe the next calendar year and the next financial year will -- is when the content pipeline will be fully back to where it used to be pre-COVID.

items.statement: Bulk of cost synergies from merger reflected in P&L; revenue synergies dependent on footfall recovery
items.quote: I think bulk of it from a cost perspective is reflected in the P&L. I think the revenue-related synergies would also be a function of the recovery on footfalls.

items.statement: Ad revenue grew ~5% YoY driven by Kalki and off-screen sponsorships; expect growth in Q2-Q3 with bigger releases
items.quote: Overall, as well, we looked at not only on-screen, but offscreen sponsorship deals with certain clients where we were playing classics and rereleases. So because of all of that effort, the team was able to deliver this 5% growth.

items.statement: Reaffirmed FY25 revenue guidance of INR1,400-1,500 crores, EBITDA of INR230-260 crores, and exit Q4 EBITDA of INR80-90 crores (20-22% margin).
items.value: Revenue INR1,400-1,500 cr; EBITDA INR230-260 cr; Exit Q4 EBITDA INR80-90 cr
items.quote: We continue to reaffirm our guidance for our outlook for our full year. We expect revenues to be in the range of INR1,400 crores to INR1,500 crores, with our EBITDA in the range of INR230 crores to INR260 crores and with an exit Q4 EBITDA expected to be in the INR80 crores to INR90 crores level, approximately 20% to 22%.

items.statement: Gross margin dipped due to inventory reduction but expected to return to 48% in H2 FY25.
items.quote: So, we said you should estimate that our gross margins will get back to 48% in H2.

items.statement: Debt reduced by INR160 crores in Q1 (INR40 crores from free cash); target year-end net debt under INR500 crores and debt/EBITDA under 2x.
items.value: Debt reduction INR160 cr; Target net debt <INR500 cr; Debt/EBITDA <2x
items.quote: We have reduced debt by about INR160 crores, almost INR40 crores of that coming from free cash generation through the quarter. With a targeted further cash debt reduction from cash flows, we expect end of the year debt adjusted for the uncalled money of the rights to be under INR500 crores and significantly better than our Debt to EBITDA guidance of under 3 times, we should be now comfortably guid

items.statement: Vizag facility retrofit capex amount not finalized; will be funded internally without additional borrowing; update expected next quarter.
items.quote: We don't have the exact numbers as the work is being conducted by consultants. So, we will probably be able to update that in the next quarter. But we would not need to borrow any additional monies to achieve this.

items.statement: Regulated markets revenue share back to 75%+; CRAMS currently 5-8% of revenue, targeting ~10% next year.
items.quote: Well, at this time, we are still in the 5% to 8% range. But based on our confidence and RFP that we expect this to be to grow to about 10% in the next year.

items.statement: Ibuprofen pricing has come down but inventory normalized; Pondicherry facility fully utilized at ~5,000 tons; Vizag retains 3,000-ton ibuprofen block.
items.quote: To answer your specific point on pricing, the pricing has come down, but we do not operate in that market where there is intense competition. And the urge for us to do that earlier and which also caused a lot of trouble for us has been removed by the fact that we have shut the tap from the Vizag facility.

items.statement: Biosecure Act relevant only to biologics, not small molecules; sustained low crude prices expected to improve margins.
items.quote: As the law correctly calls itself The Biosecurity Act, this is only relevant to biologics, and it is not so relevant to

items.statement: Q1 adjusted EBITDA INR50 crores (14% margin) vs reported INR42 crores; difference due to non-recurring Vizag/R&D costs.
items.quote: The adjusted EBITDA reported is INR50 crores against a reported EBITDA of INR42 crores. And the reason for this is mainly because part of our network optimization, you would have probably seen in our deck that was released today, we have mothballed our vizag facility.

items.statement: Significant number of CRAMS RFPs issued; expecting conversion of some major programs during the year.
items.quote: We are seeing now with a renewed focus on our CRAMS operations, a significant number of RFPs that we have issued. And we hope that during the year, we would have achieved success with some of these major programs.

items.statement: Reaffirmed Project Leap target of ₹20,000 crore revenue by FY26; new mid-term guidance to be released during FY25
items.quote: We had this target of reaching ₹20,000 crores of top-line by FY26. We exited the previous year at a top-line of about ₹18,000 crores. And that is where we believe that we should be either able to achieve or beat the guidance ahead of its time.

items.statement: International business target of 10% contribution to consolidated revenue by FY26 maintained
items.quote: As part of the Project Leap, we target to reach 10% of contribution from international business for FY26.

items.statement: Capex guidance of ₹1,000-1,100 crore for FY25 maintained; Q1 spend ₹280 crore; expect to be at higher end of range
items.quote: No, there is no change. As you would have seen, during the first quarter, we've done capex of about ₹280 crores. So, we are on track to do the capex on our guided range of ₹1,000 crores to ₹1,100 crores for the year.

items.statement: Wires & Cables long-term EBITDA margin guidance 11-13%; near-term expectation 12-14% due to operating leverage
items.quote: See, our guided range on cables & wires for the long term is 11% to 13%. But we also think that because as of now, we are realizing better operating leverage, we should be able to generate somewhere between 12% to 14% at EBITDA level.

items.statement: EPC business sustainable operating margin expected in high single digits over medium to long term
items.quote: The annual sustainable operating margin for this business is expected to remain in the high single digits over the medium to long term.

items.statement: FMEG advertising and promotion spends guided at 3-5% of B2C top-line annually
items.quote: At an annual level, our advertising and promotion spends will continue to be within our guided range of 3% to 5% of the B2C top-line.

items.statement: Domestic Wires & Cables volume growth ~10% YoY in Q1 FY25 on high base; expect improvement in coming quarters as commodity prices stabilize
items.quote: The domestic Wires & Cables business registered a volume growth of about 10% while the value growth, because of the increased commodity prices, was there but to a large extent, it was negated because of the effect it had on sales.

items.statement: Strong real estate upcycle expected to drive wires demand growth over next 4-8 quarters
items.quote: We do believe that there should be a pickup in the demand for wires over the course of the next few quarters. And if that pans out, there should be an improvement in the mix more towards wires going ahead.

items.statement: EPC contribution expected to normalize to mid-to-high single digits of consolidated revenue from current 10% in Q1
items.quote: Going ahead, on a consistent basis, if you take a yearly view, the contribution from the EPC business will range in mid to high single digit.

items.statement: FMEG mix: fans & lights 50-55%, switches & switchgears high-teens, conduit pipes & fittings similar, others single digits
items.quote: As far as the mix is concerned, the fans and lights both of them are the larger contributors within the FMEG segment contributing somewhere between 50% and 55% of the FMEG top-line.

items.statement: International business softness in largest geography (US) due to distribution model transition; recovery expected over few more quarters
items.quote: We've guided that it will take some more quarters for the new model to stabilize. So once, hopefully, that is done, the sales from that geography should recover back to its normal levels.

items.statement: Freight cost increases compressing international margins; expected to be temporary and normalize
items.quote: What has also happened is the freight costs have increased over the past few quarters. And hence, when you compare this, the margin profile of international business in Q1 of this year versus Q1 of last year, we had that additional impact.

items.statement: Working capital cycle expected to normalize to 50-55 days from current 64 days as inventory moderates
items.quote: We believe 50 days to 55 days of working capital days is what is an optimum working capital cycle for us. Within that, the inventory days will be somewhere closer to about 100 days.

items.statement: Board reconstituted Audit and NRC committees to comprise only Independent Directors for enhanced governance
items.quote: Both these committees will now fully comprise of Independent Directors, in-line with globally accepted best governance practices.

items.statement: India Ratings upgraded credit rating outlook to 'positive' from 'on watch with negative implication'
items.quote: India Ratings has improved the outlook on our credit rating to 'positive' from the earlier 'on watch with negative implication'.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expected to be 13%-13.5% for current year
items.quote: as Mr. Chari said this is what at least for the current year, this is what we are seeing, 13%-13.5% will play between these two numbers.

items.statement: Cash outflow of close to Rs. 100 crore for Dahej expansion projects this year
items.quote: Overall, we will have an outflow of close to about Rs. 100 crore.

items.statement: Dahej expansion including 20,000 tons HPPC capacity and 30,000 MT ethoxylation capacity expected to be completed by end of current year
items.quote: Moving forward, our expansion projects at Dahej are progressing as planned and are expected to be completed by the end of the current year.

items.statement: FY26-27 expected to be the right year for 100% utilization of new capacities
items.quote: But I think as we have said in earlier calls also, FY26-27 should be the right year for us to see 100% utilization of those capacities.

items.statement: Institutional cleaning chemical business targeting Rs. 250 crore this year, Q1 was Rs. 60 crore
items.quote: Institutional cleaning chemical this year, we are expecting it to be Rs. 250 crore, the 1st Quarter was about Rs. 60 crore.

items.statement: EBITDA margin dropped to 13.3% from 14.1% due to higher freight, travel, maintenance and selling costs
items.quote: Our EBITDA has improved by 12.5% to Rs. 64.9 crore from Rs. 57.7 crore, with an EBITDA margin of 13.3% compared to 14.1% in the previous year.

items.statement: Prices are stable with slight price cuts in some areas to drive volumes
items.quote: Prices are more or less stable now. There are some places where we have taken slight price cuts just to get into the volume game, but overall prices seem to be stable now.

items.statement: Healthy demand seen in both domestic and export markets for HPPC and Textile segments
items.quote: Both the markets we see healthy demand both domestic and in exports. As I said earlier, the home textile markets especially from the US, the orders are full with our current customers in India and also in Bangladesh.

items.statement: Exports grew ~50% YoY, now 24-25% of revenue, targeting 25-30% range for next 2 years
items.quote: If you see overall the business itself is growing, so it's growing both on the domestic as well as on the exports. But if you see, I think, last year Q1 our exports would have been 20% of our revenue. Today, this quarter it's almost 24%-25%.

items.statement: No provision for Rs. 25 crore GST penalty notice, appealing order, confident of favorable outcome
items.quote: No, there will not be any provision. That's an order which has been passed, as per the department it's an IGST refund, which they claim to be erroneous. We have taken proper legal views on the order which has come, and we are now going to appeal against this order with the higher authority of commissioner appeal, and we are quite hopeful of getting a favorable order on this.

items.statement: Freight costs up 35-40% YoY, container shortages and shipping delays persist as new normal
items.quote: if you see YoY it would have definitely increased about 35%-40% of what it was in Q1 of last year.

items.statement: Ethoxylation utilization at 90%+ at both Tristar and Unitop sites, overall average utilization 55-60%
items.quote: On ethoxylation side, our utilizations are at 90% plus at both the sites of Tristar and Unitop.

items.statement: New Dubai subsidiary incorporated for global expansion, may start with marketing then manufacturing
items.quote: We incorporated the subsidiary in Dubai primarily for any global expansion that we may plan going forward. So, rather than holding it through India, we currently incorporated this subsidiary.

items.statement: Working capital at 90-100 days is new normal, hoping for some release by September
items.quote: And as we said in the last 2 earnings call, between 90-100 days is a new normal which we should consider.

items.statement: HPPC and TSC segments both grew 21% YoY, AHN flat due to industry headwinds
items.quote: We are especially pleased with the outstanding performance of our HPPC segment, which achieved a robust 21% growth. Our Textile Specialty Chemicals division also performed well, registering a 21% growth. However, the Animal Health and Nutrition performance remained flat due to industry headwinds.

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth guided at 18% to 22% with approximately 13% EBITDA margin
items.quote: In terms of FY '25 guidance, we expect our revenue growth to be in the 18% to 22% band with approximately 13% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Free cash conversion from EBITDA expected at 50% to 75% band for FY25
items.quote: The free cash generation for the business should improve meaningfully during the year and we expect the cash conversion from EBITDA to be within the 50% to 75% band.

items.statement: Dividend payout ratio maintained at up to 20% of consolidated PAT for FY25
items.quote: Some of these proposed acquisitions may not warrant significant capital to be deployed, hence shall continue to maintain a similar dividend payout ratio of up to 20% of our consolidated PAT for FY'25.

items.statement: Direct margin growth expected to be slightly better than revenue growth due to margin expansion
items.quote: So, I think the growth rate on direct margins w ill be little tad better than the revenue margin growth, simply because of the direct margin expansion. Plus, yes, it will grow in line with the revenue

items.statement: ILD volumes grew year-on-year in Q1 FY25 despite some OTT players cutting budgets
items.quote: So, in terms of ILD, I think we have definitely seen growth in terms of volumes on a Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: New product revenue grew 94% year-on-year and 16% sequentially in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Our new product revenue continues to witness very strong momentum, registering 94% year-on-year growth and 16% sequential growth.

items.statement: Promoter shareholding at 83%+ post open offer; one year to reduce to 75% minimum public shareholding
items.quote: So, pursuant to the open offer, the promoter's shareholding actually increased to 83+% and we have a stipulated timeframe of one year to bring it back to the minimum public shareholding of 75%.

items.statement: Proximus-Microsoft 5-year strategic partnership on digital communication services including CPaaS announced
items.quote: Proximus and Microsoft announced a five-year strategic partnership on digital communication services, including CPaaS.

items.statement: Cost of sales synergies from Proximus immediate; cross-charging shared services from Q3 FY25
items.quote: Cost of sales, as we said, it's already kind of happening, I mean, immediately after we started to get the minority's approval. In terms of the cross-charging on the share services, that will happen from Q3 onwards.

items.statement: TruSense digital identity product development capitalization stopped; licensing TeleSign stack instead
items.quote: We have already shared that we would be licensing, I mean, their digital entity stack to our customers. So, in a way, I mean, we are looking at sunsetting the TruSense development and incremental development.

items.statement: Aspiration to achieve $1 billion revenue in next two to three years remains intact with concrete plan
items.quote: We are still having our aspiration to achieve that $1 billion, and we are very much sure that we will achieve that number. Because we can clearly see the synergy between both the companies, and how we are going to move forward and we have already laid down a plan to reach $1 billion in next two to three years down the line.

items.statement: Amazon deal: already serving India and UK destinations; testing 10 total destinations
items.quote: I think I just mentioned, we already started getting some traffic for UK termination from Amazon. And we are already testing for more destination s. I think we have already signed total 10 destinations

items.statement: RCS and WhatsApp pricing higher than SMS with better margins; strong pipeline building
items.quote: RCS prices and WhatsApp prices are better, higher than SMS for sure. And definitely there's a higher margin than SMS in both the channels.

items.statement: Management expects FY25 EBITDA margin around 24-25% and year-on-year volume growth around 20%
items.quote: We are not giving any guidance, but considering what we are seeing right now, we believe somewhere around 24%-25% of the time margin is something which can be achieved in FY25, considering the current situation.

items.statement: Management indicates FY25 revenue could be Rs 2,500-2,600 crore and PAT Rs 300-350 crore based on current trends
items.quote: Yes, it should be in that range, looking at the current situation.

items.statement: FY25 capex planned at Rs 300 crore; total investment for CPVC and chlorotoluene projects around Rs 500-550 crore
items.quote: The CAPEX that we have planned for this year is around Rs. 300 crore and that will be also for next year. But once we announce the CAPEX, I guess that will give more clarity.

items.statement: New capex for chlorine and hydrogen derivatives to be announced in next 3 months; will drive FY27-28 growth
items.quote: We will be announcing in a three-month time another CAPEX that will drive the volume growth and the value growth in FY27 and 28.

items.statement: Chlorotoluene value chain commissioning by end of Q2 FY25; full benefit from FY26
items.quote: We are planning to commercialize production from end of quarter two for the chlorotolu ene and its value chain and it will take probably 3 months’ time to take approval from all the big suppliers and probably you will see the movement from the supply side will start happening from quarter four itself

items.statement: CPVC compounding commissioned 30 June; meaningful revenue from Q3, optimized by Q4
items.quote: CPVC compound, we just commissioned on 29th June. So, it is yet to contribute anything in terms of va lue. It might start, but again, it will take time to ramp up. It might contribute in a meaningful way, maybe by end of December

items.statement: Overall plant utilization 80% in Q1 FY25 vs 71% in Q1 FY24; Chlor-Alkali target 80-85%; derivatives target 65-70% in FY25, 80% in FY26
items.quote: For the quarter, capacity utilization of the plant stood at 80% against 71% in Q1 FY24.

items.statement: Derivatives and specialty revenue share 53% in Q1 FY25 vs 37% in Q1 FY24; target 70% by FY28
items.quote: In line with our strategy to diversify our business model, revenue contribution from the derivatives and the specialty business stood at 53% in Q1 FY25 versus 37% in Q1 FY24.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin 27% vs 21% in Q1 FY24; PAT margin 13% vs 7%
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 27% in Q1 FY25 against 21% in Q1 of FY24. PAT grew by 172% to Rs. 88 crore s in Q1 FY25 against Rs. 32 crores in Q1 FY24. And the margin stood at 13% against 7% on account of last financial

items.statement: Product-level EBITDA margins targeted around 25% for new projects
items.quote: In terms of our EBITDA margin for each of the products that we have selected, all consist s in the range of 25

items.statement: Chemical industry recovery started in pockets; expect further improvement through FY25
items.quote: Chemical industry had started witnessing recovery in the few pockets and we expect that to further improve for year as a whole for

items.statement: Derivative realizations down 1-7% QoQ; ECU Rs 30,000/ton in Q1 vs Rs 29,000 in Q4; CPVC realization Rs 130,000-135,000/ton; ECH realization ~Rs 100,000/ton
items.quote: See, the realizations have dropped, but it's not like a drastic drop. It is in the drop range of around 1% to 7%.

items.statement: Coal prices stable for last 2-3 months; no major change expected this financial year
items.quote: The coal price is not much different compared to the last 2-3 months. It is on stable conditions almost. The variations are very minimal. So, we don't see any big change in the coming quarter in terms of the energy mix going forward.

items.statement: Caustic exports <5% of production; ECH exports ~30% of production; freight costs impacting margins in Q1 and Q2
items.quote: Caustic export is ve ry hardly. We are doing not significant in terms of the quantity which we produce. We are doing hardly less than almost 5% kind of exports we are doing it

items.statement: Debt/EBITDA 1.59x at June 2024 vs 1.99x at March 2024; debt expected to reduce to Rs 850-900 crore by year-end
items.quote: Our debt to EBITDA stood at 1.59x at the end of June 24. This is again 1.99x at the end of March 24. The ratio has improved in line with the increase in profitability and reduction in debt.

items.statement: Internal accruals sufficient for current capex; future capex funding mix to be decided later
items.quote: Considering the current situation, the CAPEX that we have announced so far, the internal accruals are good enough for the CAPEX that we want to do. But future CAPEX that we do, at that appropriate time, we will evaluate whether we want to do any kind of raising or we can do a mix of internal accruals, debt and also raising.

items.statement: Chlorine internal consumption 65%; expected to increase by end FY25
items.quote: Currently, the chlorine consumption in and out is around 65%. And as we ramp up our further capacities, that will inch up by maybe end of this FY25.

items.statement: Red Sea logistics crisis increasing freight costs and impacting export margins in Q1 and Q2
items.quote: Yes, for a time being that is true, that is there. But agai n, so yes, that is true for a time being. So, that is witnessed in the Q1 FY25. And also it might get impacted in Q2 as well

items.statement: Chlorotoluene commissioning delayed by couple of months due to equipment and mechanical completion delays
items.quote: But the couple of equipment and the mechanical completion was delayed than what we have expected. And I think we are able to do it and compensate probably by end of this quarter, we are going to commission the plant.

items.statement: Company remains in 35% tax bracket due to MAT credit of Rs 30 crore; will shift to 25% bracket once utilized in ~2 years
items.quote: We expect that we still have a MAT credit of Rs. 30 crores as of now. And we expect that in next coming two years, it will be utilized fully.

items.statement: Focus on chlorine and hydrogen derivatives; downstream chlorotoluene value chain under evaluation
items.quote: Once we commission the Chlorotoluene value chain, we are also looking for a down the line value chain of Chlorotoluene also as a future CAPEX.

items.statement: Industry export market weak; specialty chemical demand recovering quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: Yes, so right now the chemical industries, the export market is not great. So, all the specialties and the derivatives who are depend on the export business, they are not doing good. So, it is on the recovery mode. So, it has started moving upward.

items.statement: Customer approvals for chlorotoluene products expected to take 3 months; supply movement from Q4
items.quote: It will take probably 3 months' time to take approval from all the big suppliers and probably you will see the movement from the supply side will start happening from quarter four itself.

items.statement: Targeting at least one profitable quarter in current financial year at EBITDA break-even before ESOP cost and excluding UPI incentive
items.quote: We are hoping and working on making sure that we deliver at least one profitable quarter inthis financial year as soon as we are able to see a lot more clarity coming our way

items.statement: Expect EBITDA break-even before ESOP cost and before adding UPI incentive
items.quote: looking at it without that extraordinary one-time item. So you can expect us to talk about EBITDAbreak-even before ESOP cost and before adding UPI incentive

items.statement: Capex this year will be meaningfully lower than last year due to device redeployment
items.quote: Our Capex this year will be meaningfully lower than our Capex last year.

items.statement: Expect non-UPI payment margin of 15-18 bps and overall payment margin of 3-3.5 bps excluding UPI incentive, 5 bps+ including incentive
items.value: 3-3.5 bps excl UPI incentive; 5 bps+ incl UPI incentive
items.quote: we expect the non-UPI, to be again, 15 to 18 basis points, as it was a couple ofyears ago, actually. So, that was one component. The second is, in our deal with third party banks such as Yes Bank and HDFC Bank and Axis Bank andso on, our commercials are slightly different in the sense that we do bear a little bit more of paymentcosts. But we get a slightly higher share of UPI incentive. So on an o

items.statement: Target high double-digit or close to 20% EBITDA margin over next 3-4 years
items.quote: Medium term, we do want to get to sort of high double digits or close to 20% EBITDA margin.But I think the overall platform can do much better than that. But over the next, if you had to sayover the next 3 or 4 years, that's what we should be aiming for

items.statement: Consumer onboarding pending NPCI approval; expect approval during fiscal year unless extraordinary event occurs
items.quote: We definitely believe that it should definitely come, during the fiscal. Definitely, Unless something extraordinary happens.

items.statement: Focus on credit, insurance, wealth as dollar-value growth sequence; mutual fund distribution growing very well; insurance distribution finding both consumer and merchant takers
items.quote: So credit, insurance and wealth in this sequencing as a dollar value, total valuebasis is what my personal pick would be. And advertising is a by-product of traffic. And all these arethe bottom line accretive

items.statement: Lending growth constrained by lenders' prudent policies per regulatory guidance; not pursuing aggressive credit disbursement
items.quote: But at thesame time, this also means the quality of credit etc. for them is coming out to be great as they'reseeing the data on their side on the books. So core philosophy, I'd say that, we remain very, very disciplined with our lender partners where wesuggest to them that they should be taking the decision which they want to take, and this is wherewe are. So net net, we don't have much guidance t

items.statement: PayPay investment carrying value ~Rs 2,000 crore; FVTOCI changes due to forex (yen/rupee)
items.quote: And the carrying value for PayPay is roughly for our stock acquisition right andPayPal's roughly Rs 2000 crores

items.statement: Investing in sales and marketing including global events and hiring salespeople, impacting EBITDA
items.quote: We have been making investments in sales and marketing sides. So we've been attending global events. We've been hiring salespeople, and we're also investing in it. That is where the EBITDA is showing the impact.

items.statement: Order book is healthy with no anticipated drop; more predictability from partnerships and market optimism
items.quote: So, the order book is going good, I would say. I mean, there is no, I mean, I don't anticipate any drop in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Scope to increase margins exists; focus on efficiency while growing profitably
items.quote: Do we have any scope to increase the margins? Yes, yes. We always have the scope to increase the margins. We always have the scope to be more e�cient. And constantly working towards it

items.statement: Tax incidence increasing due to SEZ sunset for 2 out of 3 units, impacting PAT
items.quote: We have also had SEZ sunset for 2 units out of 3. So that is also causing the increase in tax incidence.

items.statement: Mixed US demand with green shoots; positivity and demand returning from clients who withdrew earlier

items.statement: EPS expansion to complete by end of calendar year or Q4 FY25; XPS expansion in next financial year

items.quote: No, that is for the current power requirement, when the ABS comes up, then we will go in for additional solar power capacity.

items.statement: Targeting 45-50 new store openings in FY25 with focus on South, smaller towns and drive-thrus
items.quote: Aligned to our vision 2027, we are targeting to open 45 to 50 new stores in FY25 with a focus on South, smaller towns and drive-thrus.

items.statement: Aim to achieve 15-18% contribution of McCafe to store AUV by 2027
items.quote: We aim to achieve a 15% to 18% contribution of McCafe to store AUV by 2027.

items.statement: Eating out frequency higher sequentially and close to last year's level; discretionary consumption expected to improve gradually
items.quote: Eating out frequency was higher sequentially and close to last year's level. As retail level inflation continues to moderate coupled with higher incomes and savings, we believe discretionary consumption will improve gradually.

items.statement: Exit month of Q1 was better; sequential sales about 10% higher vs Q4 in line with seasonality and new stores
items.quote: On a sequential basis, sales were about 10% higher versus Q4 in line with seasonality and some contribution from new stores.

items.statement: Network expansion plan unchanged at 45-50 restaurants in FY25
items.quote: Our network expansion plan remains unchanged. We will add 45 to 50 restaurants in FY25 reflecting our confidence in the structural growth and opportunities which lie ahead.
